News.title: Italian foreign minister ‘targeted by pro-Putin hackers who leaked his personal info on dark web’ after Ukraine support
News.content:
HACK PROBE Italian foreign minister ‘targeted by pro-Putin hackers who leaked his personal info on dark web’ after Ukraine support







Next

A SENIOR politician has been targeted in a series of sick cyber attacks which he says have been launched over his support for Ukraine.

The personal data of Italy’s foreign minister has been plastered all over the dark web in a suspected Russian hacking spree.



Twisted fiends have also targeted the politicians’ families in a seriesof continuouss attacks over several days.

Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said: “For days now, cyber-criminals have been publishing my personal data on the dark web and seeking further information, effectively exposing me to new threats and intimidation.”



The stricken politician did not share what type of information had been maliciously disseminated.

Tajani claimed: “Our position on Ukraine is the political reason I have been targeted.



“Defending the freedom of a sovereign state, taking a clear stand in support of a nation’s democracy and independence, is dangerous in the eyes of these criminal entities.”

Italian prime minister Georgia Meloni blamed the leaks on pro-Russia hackers and swore her “full solidarity”.

She added that the sale of private information “must be tackled with the utmost determination”.

The Kremlin has not responded to the allegations.



It comes as Vladimir Putin is ramping up his shadow warfare against Europe – with fears mounting that Moscow was behind a wave of chaos at supermarkets and on passenger flights this week.

Devastating cyber attacks wiped out fridges across Europe and cost companies millions of pounds worth of damage.

And at least 24 flights were hit by bomb threats across three days of mid-air chaos – with several forced to make emergency landings.



A Russian hate group claimed responsibility for at least two incidents, allegedly threatening to “turn the skies red” in one chilling email.

Blood banks in France were also struck by cyber attacks which sent the temperatures of their life-saving stock soaring from -30 degrees celsius to over 100 degrees celsius.

The barrage of cyber crime has seen eyes swivel to the Kremlin with fears mounting that the attacks are part of Vladimir Putin‘s increasingly brazen hybrid campaign.

Experts have warned that the hacks could spark war if they continue to go unchecked.

One MP also warned that NHS blood banks and vaccine reserves are at high risk of hacks.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Graeme Downie, chair of the Coalition on Secure Technology, warned that “hostile actors” could target the UK next and urged hospitals to check the security measures on kit storing crucial medical supplies.

He added that NHS fridges were “vulnerable” to an attack like France faced “or worse”.

News.title: Three in ten kids want parents to put their phones away while a third wish mums & dads would play more, study finds
News.content:
SWIPE OUT Three in ten kids want parents to put their phones away while a third wish mums & dads would play more, study finds







Next

AROUND three in ten kids want their parents to put their phones away.

A survey by toy maker Playmobil also found 38% youngsters aged four to nine wished their mums and dads would play with them more often.



It was also revealed 15% of parents realise their child wants them to spend less time on their phones.

The findings come after five kids were appointed by Playmobil to create its Christmas advert – and they decided they wanted it to be about children calling on adults to put their phones down and play with them.



Every scene in the advert has been imagined and filmed by the children.

Delilah, aged 8, who worked on the advert, said: “We wanted to show in our advert that Christmas is much more fun when everyone plays.



“My mum does really funny voices when we play, and sometimes they’re so silly that we can’t stop laughing.

“This Christmas, I think grown-ups should put their phones away and come play with us.

“After all, a phone can’t be a princess, an astronaut or a dinosaur… well, not a very good one anyway.”

What kids want adults to do when they play with them Play with me more – 38%

Help me come up with ideas – 33%

Pretend to be a character – 31%

Put their phone away – 28%

Play with me rather than watching TV – 23%

Be more silly – 22%

Let me be messy – 22%

Start the story in a funny way – 21%

Let me play on my own – 12%

The study also found 70% of parents say using devices with screens during playtime is often the easiest option when they’re busy and their child needs entertainment.



Despite this 54% feel guilty handing a device over to their children.

Meanwhile, six in ten parents don’t think children experience boredom, thanks to devices and constant entertainment.

News.title: Lisa Nandy sparks fury from veterans and MPs after bungling Remembrance Sunday announcement
News.content:
Next

CULTURE Secretary Lisa Nandy sparked fury from veterans and MPs after bungling a Remembrance Sunday announcement.

The Tories said her tribute to the Armed Forces suggested no one in our country had fought a war since 1945.



In a press release, Ms Nandy said: “This Remembrance Sunday, we come together to reflect and honour the sacrifices our Armed Forces made in the First and Second World Wars, and continue to make today.

“We are about to raise the first generation for whom fighting a war really is part of history.



“Future generations must know the significance of those who served in our national story, that they forged a path for friendship and cooperation that meant no one in our country has had to fight a war since.”

Tory chairman Kevin Hollinrake blasted: “She seems to be saying that no one in our country has had to fight a war since 1945. Tell that to veterans of Korea, the Falklands, Northern Ireland, Iraq and Afghanistan, and to families of the hundreds who never came home. Many will be at the Cenotaph.”



Reform UK’s Treasury spokesman Robert Jenrick said: “This shows shameful disregard for the 7,193 British soldiers who have sacrificed their lives in conflicts since World War Two.”

Veteran Simon Weston, 65, who suffered severe burns in the Falklands War, said: “It’s tragic that somebody could be so obtuse. I am stunned.”

Sean Williams 52, who served in the Royal Logistic Corps, told The Sun: “My family fought in the Falklands. We’ve lost people. I’m speechless to be honest.”

Ex-Royal Navy seaman Maurice Quinlan, 47, who served on HMS Liverpool from 1998-2000, added: “She’s swept us all under the carpet.



“I’ve lost mates who gave their lives for our country.”

Ms Nandy’s claims about the diminishing prospect of war also appeared to contradict Government messaging on stockpiling. The Be Ready Campaign told the public to prepare for disruption caused by “hostile state actors”.

News.title: Veterans and military personnel will have rail discounts protected in law
News.content:
HEROES' DISCOUNT LAW Veterans and military personnel will have rail discounts protected in law

Source: Getty







Next

VETERANS and military personnel will have rail discounts protected in law.

Our heroes are entitled to a third off fares through a railcard, and children travelling with them get 60 per cent off.

But ministers hope that enshrining it in law will give veterans and serving members of the Armed Forces reassurance discounts will continue for generations to come.

The announcement comes after free rail travel was extended to bereaved military family members attending Remembrance events.





Rail Minister Lord Hendy told The Sun on Sunday: “They deserve our support, this Remembrance weekend and always.”

Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said: “We have a moral duty to stand by our veterans and the military families who sacrifice so much.”

The King will lead the nation in two minutes’ silence at The Cenotaph today for those who have served in the Armed Forces and died in conflicts.

PM Andy Burnham said: “I want to offer my personal thanks to those who served and continue to serve.”

And Nigel Farage teared up while filming a documentary on World War One battlefields and asked cameras to stop.

The Reform UK leader said: “The process was very brutal so if you died in the war your family got one of those called the dead man’s penny.

“Very often if you see them today, they’ve got solder on the back. They were stuck above mantelpieces.

“That was what the dead soldier got…and you can stop recording now, please.”

News.title: Tory MPs launch bid to close loophole that lets sanctioned firms from Russia and Iran sponsor workers’ visas
News.content:
Next

TORY MPs are launching a bid to close a loophole that allows sanctioned firms from Russia and Iran to sponsor worker visas.

They warn that the current situation could threaten our national security and allow immigration backed by our “enemies.”



MPs have tabled an amendment to Labour’s immigration legislation to force the Home Office to remove visa sponsor licences from any individual or company under UK sanctions.

It comes after investigations earlier this year found companies under sanctions for links to the Russian and Iranian regimes were approved to sponsor worker visas.



Alicia Kearns, Shadow Security Minister, warned that Labour was leaving Britain’s backdoor “open to immigration sponsored by our enemies”.

She added: “Sanctions are supposed to punish those who threaten our national security and undermine our interests. It is therefore utterly absurd that a company can be sanctioned by Britain and still bring in workers to our country.



“The Conservatives would close this loophole. We will not allow sanctioned firms from Russia or any country to import people to our country and put our safety at risk.”

Chris Philp, Shadow Home Secretary, added: “It is ridiculous that we are handing out the right to bring foreign workers into Britain to companies that have been blacklisted by our Government.”

Russian airline Aeroflot, cryptocurrency platform Exmo Exchange and Iranian banks Melli and Persia International, were listed as holding licences to bring employees to the UK earlier this year.

The two Russian companies are no longer on the sponsor list.



Another probe also found UK subsidiaries of sanctioned Russian companies could still sponsor Russian nationals to enter the UK via the loophole.

Technically, while a company may be sanctioned for a particular activity, it does not mean that having a sponsor licence contravenes the sanction.

But the Government insisted the powers already exist to revoke a sponsor licence where an organisation is subject to sanctions.

A Home Office spokesperson said: “The power to revoke sponsorship from sanctioned companies already exists.

“We will not hesitate to act to protect the integrity of the system. More broadly, we have taken robust action against Russia and Iran.



“The UK has now sanctioned over 3,500 individuals, businesses, and ships under the Russia sanctions regime, as well as sanctioning more than 550 individuals and entities under the Iran sanctions regimes, including the IRGC in its entirety.”

News.title: Angry French rioters defy protest ban as thousands flock to the streets and clash with cops in fourth weekend of chaos
News.content:
Next

FURIOUS French rioters defied protests bans as thousands swarmed the streets and clashed with cops in a fourth weekend of chaos.

Police launched tear gas and stun grenades as a fresh wave of fury saw bikes and wheelie bins set ablaze – with some 45,000 marching through the barricaded boulevards of Paris.



Around 3,000 shops have been ransacked and more than 4,000 people arrested as France confronts its worst rioting spree in recent years.

Over half a million marched through the nation on Thursday – with numbers dwindling to 146,000 on Saturday – although unions claim some 250,000 left to protest.



The eatstern city of Lyon bore the brunt of the violence with rioters defying bans on protest after torching a tourist office in the city last week.

Police fired tear gas to disperse several hundreds of people who had gathered to block a road during an unauthorised protest.

Interior Minister Laurent Nunez deployed 70,000 cops on Saturday in what was described as “Act IV” of the ongoing riot battles.

Certain protests routes through Paris had been banned by police – but several rebel members of the Yellow Vest movement shirked the shut down and demonstrated close to the National Assembly – France’s equivalent of the House of Commons.



Cops arrested some 20 members including one of the group’s leaders Benjamin Ball and spokeswoman Azelma Sigaux.

The vast anti-government protests have plunged the entire nation into chaos and left dozens wounded.

One teen who lost an eye from a rubber pellet fire by police and one demonstrator had his hand blown off by a stun grenade.



Panicked French leaders imposed curfews and demonstration bans across several major cities in a desperate bid to fight mob chaos on the country’s embattled streets.

Interior Minister Laurent Nunez vowed to crack down with “an extremely firm response” on any “acts of violence”.

He added that an attempted murder probe had been launched over petrol bombs hurled at cops during a real-life Halloween night of horror.

Horror photos showed a police officer engulfed in flames while battling rioters as around 3,000 shops were broken into and looted.

More than 4,000 people have been arrested in the past month, with hundreds wounded.



It comes as more than 600,000 people took to the streets in what has been dubbed a “black Thursday” for France.

The Eiffel Tower was forced into lockdown as flaming garbage heaps littered the streets and swarms of teens flooded the capital.

About a third of France’s high schools were closed or unable to operate on as some students set up blockades and teachers went on strike.

Hooded and masked thugs set Françoise high school in Tournefeuille ablaze after they let off fireworks at the premise.

Witnesses described the horrific blaze as an act of “guerrilla warfare”.



A teacher at the school told local media outlet La Dépêche: “They came to destroy everything.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“What unfolded this morning was in no way a blockade, nor even a student protest.

“These were not students who had come to voice their demands – they were individuals who had come to terrorize, ransack, and set fires. And they succeeded.”

News.title: Man, 49, and woman, 29, arrested on suspicion of child neglect amid safety concerns at nursery – as cops launch probe
News.content:
NURSERY PROBE Man, 49, and woman, 29, arrested on suspicion of child neglect amid safety concerns at nursery – as cops launch probe







Next

A MAN and a woman have been arrested on suspicion of child neglect as cops probe safety concerns at a nursery.

Reports of health and safety issues at Greenfields Nursery in Blackwood, Wales, prompted a probe into the childcare facility.

Police were alerted to the concerns by Caerphilly County Borough Council on November 3.

Gwent Police said a 49-year-old man from Cardiff and a 29-year-old woman from the Caerphilly area had been arrested on suspicion of child neglect.





Both have since been released on bail pending further investigation, cops said.

Investigators are continuing to conduct enquiries at the nursery so residents will see an increased police presence in the area – the force said.

Care Inspectorate Wales said it had been instructed to cancel the nursery’s registration in the wake of the probe.

The body took initial action to suspend the nursery’s registration on October 20.

According to the regulator, the action was taken to “ensure the safety and wellbeing of children” and to “allow further enquiries to be made.”

Detective Inspector Gavin Wilkes said: “We understand that allegations of this nature are upsetting and working with partner agencies, we are conducting a thorough investigation.

“We are aware of social media posts circulating and while we understand the public interest in this case, we urge people not to speculate or post anything online that could impact the investigation.

“If you have any information that you think might help our investigation, please come forward to report to us directly.”

News.title: Hundreds of ‘boomerang’ foreign criminals are sneaking back into UK at record rate, shock figures reveal
News.content:
SNEAKING BACK Hundreds of ‘boomerang’ foreign criminals are sneaking back into UK at record rate, shock figures reveal







Next

HUNDREDS of ‘boomerang’ criminals are sneaking back into the UK at a record rate of nearly 10 a week, The Sun on Sunday can reveal.

Home Office figures show more than 1,800 convicted offenders who had been kicked out were found back on Britain’s streets in the last five years.



Shockingly, more than one in eight of the total had been kicked out at least twice – but still managed to return.

The criminals uncovered in our figures had each been handed a deportation order after a conviction, only to be picked up again by police or immigration officers and put back on a plane.



The true figure is likely to be even higher, as government statistics only cover those who were actually caught.

Ministers have made removing foreign criminals the centrepiece of their immigration crackdown, with the Home Office spending upwards of £8million on detention centre places to deport thousands more a year.

Since the election, over 80,000 immigration offenders and individuals illegally in the UK have been returned, an increase of 52 per cent on the previous two years, with levels of removals at their highest since 2016.

But the number of deportees caught back in the country has gone up in each of the last three years.

The Home Office figures show 473 foreign national offenders were removed last year after returning in breach of a deportation order, which works out at close to ten every week.

Last year’s total was up 45 per cent on the 327 caught in 2021 and the figure has now risen for three years in a row, from 284 in 2022.



Over the last five years 1,848 deported criminals were caught back in the UK and removed again, with 246 booted out on at least two separate occasions.

One recent case saw Lithuanian Audrius Verkauskas jailed for two years at Peterborough Crown Court after police found him living in the UK despite having been deported five times since 2015.

A deportation order is served on foreign nationals jailed for a year or more and bans them from coming back for at least a decade.

Sneaking back into the country in breach of the order is a crime in its own right, carrying up to five years in prison.

The returns will fuel concerns over how porous Britain’s borders have become, with small boats bringing hundreds of migrants ashore while there are more than 10,000 foreign prisoners in the nation’s jails.



Alp Mehmet, Chairman of Migrationwatch UK, said: ““These are shocking revelations. It beggars’ belief that our borders are now so wide open that deported criminals can, seemingly, walk in at will.

“The Home Secretary must explain herself and tell us what she is going to do about this scandal.”

A Home Office spokesperson said: “Any foreign national offenders who return in breach of a deportation order will face robust enforcement action, and we will seek to remove them from the UK at the earliest opportunity.

“Returns are at their highest level in nearly a decade, with almost 12,000 foreign criminals returned or deported since the election – a 41% increase on the two years prior.”

News.title: M20 closed after horror 30-vehicle pile-up leaves two seriously injured
News.content:
M20 closed after horror 30-vehicle pile-up leaves two seriously injured

More than 30 vehicles have been involved in a major crash on the M20, leaving two people seriously injured, with multiple others also sustaining injuries

View 2 Images Cars were seen queuing on the M20 (Image: Traffic Highways)

Two people have suffered serious injuries after the major collision on the M20 in Kent, with road closures expected to remain in place overnight

‌



‌



More than 30 vehicles have been involved in a major crash on the M20, leaving two people seriously injured.

‌



Kent Police officers are currently at the scene of the collision, which happened on the London-bound carriageway between junctions 8 and 9 at around 6.41pm on Saturday, November 7.

‌



Two people are understood to have suffered serious injuries in the smash. One has been taken to a hospital in London, while the other has been transferred to a local hospital.

Other drivers involved in the collision have also sustained injuries, although these are not believed to be serious.

Emergency services remain at the scene as they deal with the incident.

‌



View 2 Images (Image: National Highways)

Both the London-bound and coast-bound carriageways have been closed between junctions 8 and 9, with the closures expected to remain in place overnight.

‌



Motorists have been urged to avoid the area and find alternative routes while emergency crews work at the scene.

In a statement, Kent Police said: "Officers are currently attending a collision on the M20 involving more than 30 vehicles.

‌



"The incident was reported to have happened at around 6.41pm on Saturday 7 November 2026 on the London-bound carriageway M20 between junction 9 and 8.

"Two people are reported to have sustained serious injuries. One of those injured has been taken to a London hospital while the other patient has been taken to a local hospital."

Article continues below

Police are appealing for anyone with information about the collision or dashcam footage to come forward.

Anyone who can help is asked to contact Kent Police via its live chat service, quoting reference 07-1245.

News.title: King Charles could make historic China visit in major royal diplomatic move
News.content:
King Charles could make historic China visit in major royal diplomatic move

EXCLUSIVE: Following King Charles' nine-day tour of the Caribbean, an aide has said royal officials would think “very carefully” about any request from the Government to send the monarch to Beijing

View 5 Images King Charles delivers a speech (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

The King could make a historic state visit to China to become only the second British monarch ever to set foot in the country, a senior palace aide has signalled.

‌



‌



In the wake of the King’s nine-day tour of the Caribbean, the aide said royal officials would think “very carefully” about any request from the Government to send the monarch to Beijing. The remarks come 40 years after the late Queen Elizabeth II’s landmark state visit in October 1986, which remains the only trip a reigning British sovereign has made to China.

‌



The aide said: “If the government said, ‘Will the King go to China?’ We (would )think about it very carefully. China is a hugely important country. It’s a very complex country. It would pose a lot of complexity in putting a programme together.”

‌



View 5 Images King Charles and Queen Camilla undertook a tour of the Caribbean (Image: Getty Images for Buckingham Palace)

As Prince of Wales, Charles never made an official visit to mainland China. His one major engagement on Chinese soil was in Hong Kong in July 1997, when he read his mother’s farewell speech at the handover of the colony.

His private journal of that trip, titled The Handover of Hong Kong or The Great Chinese Takeaway, was leaked to a Sunday newspaper in 2005. It showed he had called the ceremony an “awful Soviet-style” performance and branded Chinese officials “appalling old waxworks”. Charles won a case at the High Court to stop more extracts being published.

‌



He was accused of snubbing the state banquets for Chinese presidents Jiang Zemin in 1999 and Hu Jintao in 2005, and he stayed away from the 2008 Beijing Olympics, with his long friendship with the Dalai Lama widely presented aas the reason. When Xi Jinping came to Britain in 2015, the last state visit by a Chinese leader, Charles again missed the Buckingham Palace banquet.

He and Camilla did host the president at Clarence House for talks on climate change and clean energy. Prince William is the only senior royal to have visited China since 1986, touring Beijing, Shanghai and Yunnan province in March 2015.

‌



View 5 Images Prince William met Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing in March 2015

The Queen’s six-day visit in 1986, with the Duke of Edinburgh, came at the invitation of President Li Xiannian and two years after Britain and China agreed the return of Hong Kong. She met Deng Xiaoping, walked the Great Wall, saw the Terracotta Warriors in Xi’an and hosted a return banquet on board the Royal Yacht Britannia in Shanghai. She later received Chinese premier Li Keqiang at Windsor Castle in 2014 and hosted President Xi the following year.

‌



Despite no visit to Beijing being in the diary, the Royal Visits Committee, which includes members of the King’s senior team and senior government officials, that meet twice a year, are understood to be open to such a tour taking place. Former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer became the first prime minister in eight years to visit China in January, and Downing Street left the door open to President Xi coming to the UK.

Andy Burnham, who succeeded him in July, told Xi in their first phone call in September that he would engage “frankly and constructively”, and raised the case of jailed pro-democracy campaigner Jimmy Lai. The aide also said the King had changed the role of the sovereign. Where the late Queen was content simply to “be”, Charles had found a way to keep “doing” as monarch.

‌



“As Prince of Wales he clearly took the view that if [his mother’s] job was to be, then his job was to do until such time as he became King,” the aide said. “And one thing I spent a lot of time thinking about before accession was would the doing role just be a being role when the crown came to him, or would there be a way to blend the two? And I hope what we found is a way to blend the two."

View 5 Images Sir Keir Starmer pictured during a visit to Yuyuan Gardens in Shanghai, China earlier this year (Image: PA)

‌



“In a completely constitutionally compliant way, and with full support of the government, the King does still engage in issues, not anything which is party political, certainly, but where there is consensus, there is an agreement now that it is perfectly reasonable for the sovereign to do that."

“Now the late Queen didn’t do that, which isn’t to say one way is right, one is wrong. They’re just different ways of doing it well. But for me, when the King’s time... whenever that may be, God willing many decades, thoughtful commentators will spot that that was a big step change.”

‌



The aide was with Charles when the Queen died at Balmoral in September 2022, and said they saw a change in him “within five minutes”. They said: “Not a huge transformation because all of those years as Prince of Wales, he had done the most amazing job, and of course, the late Queen didn’t travel for the last years of her reign.

“So, in a sense, the King’s visits then as Prince of Wales were state visits in all but name. And you’ll have noticed that as soon as the Queen stopped travelling, the marching band started turning out at the foot of the steps, so in a sense nothing has changed. But in a sense, everything has changed.

‌



“And the thing I think that’s changed more than anything is the fact that when you’re in the top job, the other people who are in the top job in their country treat you a little bit differently.”

Recalling the King’s state visit to the United States in April, the aide added: “I remember sitting in the Oval Office with the King and the President, where it was very striking that there was absolutely a frankness in the conversation, but a warmth in the conversation."

‌



View 5 Images King Charles during a visit to Kingston Seawall amid the tour (Image: Chris Jackson/Getty Images)

“When the King is delivering difficult messages, he does so in a very particular tone. There is a warmth in his delivery, a warmth in his tone, which is a genius way of landing difficult issues, because people are sort of reassured a bit by the tone of what you’re saying, and then when they listen to the words, they’re much more likely to observe them.”

‌



That approach was tested to the limit over the past fortnight in the Caribbean, where calls for apologies for slavery and demands for reparations followed the King through the Bahamas, Guyana and Antigua and Barbuda.

Charles opened the tour by recognising the “great suffering of the past in these islands and beyond”. He stopped short of the formal apology Caribbean leaders had demanded, and faced calls from island nations to become republics.

Article continues below

Aides insist the King will not fight a growing tide of republicanism and will look for new partnerships “without rancour”, as he did when Barbados became a republic in 2021.

A senior palace aide said: “The King and the royal family are there to serve the people of these regions for as long as they wish. But if they don’t wish it anymore, then we really are fully open to that. The family serves when it’s wanted and if not, then a new arrangement can be found.”

News.title: Trump begs UFC boss Dana White to become his new press secretary in bizarre post
News.content:
Trump begs UFC boss Dana White to become his new press secretary in bizarre post

The US President appealed to Dana White, the CEO of the Ultimate Fighting Championship to take on the role of Press Secretary of the United States after he fired the previous one after five days

View 2 Images President Donald Trump (R) shakes hands with Ultimate Fighting Championship President and CEO Dana White in August (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Donald Trump has begged a group of current and former UFC fighters to be his press secretary.

‌



‌



In a bizarre message on social media the US President appealed to Dana White, the CEO of the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) to take the role. In the post on Truth Social he asked the longtime UFC promoter and manager to bring assistants with him "even ⁠though some are not from our ⁠country."

‌



The post read: “I am pleased to announce that the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior, has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States.

‌



“I have requested that he bring with him assistants, even though some are not from our Country, of Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, Amanda Nunes, and Kayla Harris.

“We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left. Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other. Dana, please take the job! President DONALD J. TRUMP”.

‌



View 2 Images Trump's social media post (Image: @realDonaldTrump/TruthSocial)

Minutes after Trump’s Truth Social post Mr White posted a screenshot of the announcement and a picture of himself at the press gallery lectern with the caption “On to the next chapter” on his Instagram story.

Article continues below

The news comes after Trump’s last press secretary, Katie Zacharia, lasted five days before the president fired her.

On June 14, Trump hosted a UFC fight on the grounds of the White House to celebrate the U.S.’s 250th anniversary.

News.title: Major update after teacher left fighting for life in Dubai following baby's death
News.content:
Major update after teacher left fighting for life in Dubai following baby's death

Zoey Campbell-Lowndes is fighting for her life after losing her baby - she is currently in a Dubai hospital where she needs a treatment that will cost £14,000 per dose, her family have said

View 2 Images Zoey Campbell-Lowndes was 30 weeks pregnant when she and partner Kevin got the tragic news (Image: gofundme)

A British teacher fighting for her life in a Dubai hospital after losing her baby needs vital medicine that costs £14,000 per dose, her loved ones have said.

‌



Zoey Campbell-Lowndes has woken from a coma, but remains “extremely poorly”, her family said.

Zoey, from Prestwich, was 30 weeks pregnant when she and partner Kevin got the tragic news that their baby boy had passed away, the Manchester Evening News reports.

After undergoing a caesarean section to deliver the baby, Zoey's health deteriorated 'significantly', her loved ones said. She was transferred to the intensive care unit of a hospital in the city.

Birth plan insurance covered the baby, but not medical emergencies involving Zoey, her family said. Her medical bills had already passed £100,000 as they launched an appeal for help.

In an update, Zoey's loved ones said she is now out of a medically induced coma but 'remains extremely poorly' and faces a further bill more than £50,000 more for the treatment she needs.

View 2 Images Zoey Campbell-Lowndes and partner Kevin (Image: gofundme)

"Her blood levels are still not improving as well as the doctors had hoped, and she now urgently requires further specialist treatment," a GoFundMe statement reads.

"The doctors have advised that Zoey needs a medication called Eculizumab, which costs an incredible £14,000 per dose. She requires a minimum of four doses, potentially increasing to six. This means we are now facing a further £56,000 in medication costs alone, on top of the money already spent and the ongoing hospital and treatment costs that continue to build.

“We are doing everything we possibly can to get Zoey the treatment she needs. If anyone has any contacts, knowledge or ability to help us source Eculizumab elsewhere at a reduced cost, please get in touch with us. Any help or advice would mean so much.

"We never imagined finding ourselves in this position, but we are desperate to give Zoey every possible chance of recovery. Please continue to donate and share Zoey’s story. Every contribution, no matter how small, genuinely makes a difference. Thank you from the bottom of our hearts for continuing to stand by Zoey and our family. Please keep her in your thoughts and prayers."

The initial family statement on the page last month said: "What should have been a time of excitement and preparation for welcoming her little boy into the world has instead become an unimaginable tragedy.

"While our family is trying to come to terms with the heartbreaking loss of Zoey’s baby boy, we are also facing the terrifying reality of not knowing what will happen next. All we want is for Zoey to receive the medical care she desperately needs and to have every possible chance of recovery."

For more information, or to donate, click HERE.

News.title: King Charles and Queen Camilla joined by Kate and William at Festival of Remembrance
News.content:
King Charles and Queen Camilla joined by Kate and William at Festival of Remembrance

The King and Queen have been joined by the Prince and Princess of Wales and other royals at the annual Festival of Remembrance at the Royal Albert Hall this evening

View 5 Images Charles and Camilla led royals at the important festival on Saturday night (Image: Aaron Chown/Press Association)

The King and Queen led a charge of royals at the moving Festival of Remembrance this evening, with Prince William and Kate, the Princess of Wales dazzling alongside them.

‌



‌



A whole host of royals, including the Princess Royal and Sophie, the Duchess of Edinburgh, took their places in the royal box at the Royal Albert Hall to watch the annual Royal British Legion event.

‌



Last year, future King Prince George attended the event for the first time alongside his mum, Kate. The 13-year-old, who started at Eton College in September, has been slowly moving into a more senior role over recent months.

‌



But he was absent from the festivities this year, with his mother and father attending alone with their fellow senior family members.

5 View 5 Images King Charles III and Queen Camilla attending the annual Royal British Legion Festival of Remembrance at the Royal Albert Hall in London (Image: Aaron Chown/Press Association) 5 View 5 Images Kate and William were also among the massive throng of royals (Image: Aaron Chown/Press Association)

‌



While most of the guests donned black for the evening, including the Queen and Princess of Wales, the King and his eldest son dressed in lock-step. The pair both wore navy blue suits, the King's with pinstripes and the Prince's without. Both, and everyone else in attendance, had Remembrance poppies pinned to their lapels.

Tonight’s festival reflected on those who served in operations in Bosnia, the Gulf War and the Iraq War. Personal stories brought to light the memories of those who served through their letters, known as ‘Blueys’ – the distinctive light-blue airmail letters sent home to loved ones.

‌



5 View 5 Images Britain's Sophie, Duchess of Edinburgh arrives to attend The Royal British Legion Festival of Remembrance event at the Royal Albert Hall (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images) 5 View 5 Images The Princess Royal attending the annual Royal British Legion Festival of Remembrance at the Royal Albert Hall in London (Image: Aaron Chown/Press Association)

‌



The theme of this year’s festival was Places of Remembrance, and the event explored how places people associate with those who have been lost can hold profound personal meaning. The festival comes just hours before the King, who is patron of the Royal British Legion and has just returned from his Caribbean tour, will lead the nation in a two-minute silence at the National Service of Remembrance at the Cenotaph in London tomorrow morning.

There, Charles and Prince William will lay wreaths in memory of the nation’s war dead alongside Princess Anne and Prince Edward. The King’s wreath of poppies will be mounted on an arrangement of black leaves, as is traditional for the sovereign, and will bear his racing colours of scarlet, purple and gold.

‌



A wreath laid on behalf of Camilla, by her equerry, will bear her racing colours, inherited from her father. Meanwhile William’s wreath will feature the Prince of Wales feather and a ribbon in Welsh red.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Camilla, Kate, the Duchess of Edinburgh, the Duke and Duchess of Gloucester and the Duke of Kent will also attend, watching proceedings from the balcony of the Foreign Office.

Earlier this week, the Duchess of Gloucester, on behalf of the Queen, opened the 98th Field of Remembrance at Westminster Abbey. There, the Duchess planted a cross before the Last Post was sounded and then met service personnel and their families.

News.title: Russell Brand — latest updates: Prisoners 'banned from talking' to rapist as he's fed 'prison slop'
News.content:
According to sources, 'no one is allowed to see or speak to' Russell Brand in HMP Wandsworth where prisoners spent '23 hours inside cells' a day and the food is branded 'slop'

Prisoners are said to have been banned from speaking to Russell Brand after he was transferred to prison ahead of his sentencing for rape and sexual assault convictions.

The convicted rapist is set to start a potentially lengthy prison term on Monday after he was convicted of raping one of his fans and sexually assaulting three women on Thursday. While he is being held in custody after being denied bail at Southwark Crown Court, it has been claimed by insiders that prisoners have been warned not to speak to him.

One source, who had just visited her son inside the jail, said: “My son said Brand is downstairs from him. He said no one is allowed to see or speak to him.”

Another female visitor added: “Apparently Brand requested to go on the main wing, but they decided to put him in isolation.” Another source said she was told: "Brand doesn't like the food and is struggling to eat it. It's slop."

News.title: Baby's body found inside freezer in basement in Spain
News.content:
Baby's body found inside freezer in basement in Spain

Local authorities have launched an investigation after the body of a baby was found in a freezer belonging to a deceased woman in a basement in the Spanish town of Allariz in Galicia

View Image Allariz sits in a green valley surrounded by lush mountains and a river (Image: Getty Images)

Police are investigating after making a horror discovery inside a freezer at a family home in Spain.

‌



‌



An investigation was launched by police after a baby's body was discovered inside a freezer in a basement apartment in western Spain.

‌



The Civil Guard have launched a probe after the shocking discovery was made in the town of Allariz in Galicia.

‌



The child’s body was found by a relative of the woman, now deceased, who had owned the freezer. The relative found the remains after opening the appliance, which was located in the basement of her home, specifically in the storage room in the garage area.

Authorities from the nearby city of Ourense are investigating after the discovery on Monday, La Voz de Galicia reports.

‌



The body was transferred that same day so that forensic experts could establish the cause of death.

Local reports say that the remains are those of a foetus of just over 32 weeks gestation. Experts are reportedly working to determine if the child’s death occurred during childbirth or was a miscarriage.

‌



Pathologists are also seeking to determine when the baby died, with the date of death possibly as long ago as two decades. Cops are said to be taking statements from family members and neighbours as part of their ongoing investigation.

Investigators are also working to establish a link between the woman who owned the freezer and the deceased child. DNA samples taken from close relatives could determine the genetic trace and clarify this point, as well as whether there is a biological link with the family.

Article continues below

The investigation, ordered by the Ourense courts, is ongoing.

News.title: Martin Lewis urgent call for anyone born between 1986 and 2008 'soon as possible'
News.content:
Martin Lewis urgent call for anyone born between 1986 and 2008 'soon as possible'

'So one reason for putting a pound in as soon as possible is you get that clock ticking'

View Image Martin Lewis said people of the right age need to take action 'now' on Lifetime ISAs (Image: BBC)

Martin Lewis has given an urgent warning to anyone born between 1986 and 2008 - get a quid on! The personal finance expert spoke out after the Andy Burnham government made a key change in the budget.

‌



‌



Chancellor John Healey announced major updates to the Lifetime ISA (LISA), including a reduction to the withdrawal penalty for expensive properties and an eventual plan to replace the scheme with a new First-Time Buyer ISA.

‌



Mr Lewis said in a new video on Facebook: “If you’re aged 18 to 39 and you don’t have a lifetime ISA, I’d strongly suggest you get a quid in one now, even if you already own a home.

‌



“And the reason for this has all got even stronger since the budget.”

The Lifetime ISA will close to new applicants on April 6, 2029, when the new First-Time Buyer ISA launches. If a person uses theirr LISA to buy a first home that exceeds the £450,000 price cap, the withdrawal charge has been reduced from 25% to 20%. This means they get back the original savings plus interest, losing only the government bonus instead of a portion of your own money.

A Lifetime ISA (LISA) is a UK government-backed savings or investment account designed to help people aged 18 to 39 save for their first home or for retirement.

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Mr Lewis explained: “We now know that in April 2029, the Lifetime ISA will be replaced by the first-time buyer ISA. But as long as you’ve opened one before then, you can still use and get the bonus on the Lifetime ISA after that.

‌



“Now, with the Lifetime ISA, you can put up to four grand a year, and you get 25% added on top. So that’s up to £1,000 free each year and that can be used towards a first time buy a property under £450,000 or towards saving for your retirement. You can take the money out at age 60 with no penalty. However, there is a rule with the Lifetime ISA that you can’t get the bonus as a first-time buyer unless you’ve had the LISA open for a year. “
