‌



He said this means: “So one reason for putting a pound in as soon as possible is you get that clock ticking. Even if you’re not ready to buy now, as long as it’s more than a year away, once you are, then you can just dunk the £4,000 in and you get the £1,000 bonus straight away and you could buy with it.”

Mr Lewis added that if someone is buying a property over £450,000, they won’t face a penalty to get their money out for the deposit. He added: “You won’t get the bonus, but you’ll get back what you put in plus interest. So, the risk of having a lifetime ISA is less. If you do get a lifetime ISA and you want to use the first-time buyer ISA, you will be to get the bonus on both. You just won’t be able to contribute to both in the same tax year.

Article continues below

“So, you can see why it’s worth having if you’re going to be a first-time buyer.” For homeowners, Mr Lewis said: “I generally put pension saving as better for retirement than lifetime ISAs. For some people, especially basic rate self-employed people, the lifetime ISA can be a decent option. And as the new ISA that’s replacing it doesn’t have a retirement saving option, just in case it’s good for you in 2030, 7, you may as well put a pound in now so that you have the facility then to save in a lifetime ISA for your retirement if it becomes worthwhile. And that is just the tip of the iceberg.”

News.title: Briton among six killed in 'far-right' shooting in Krakow
News.content:
A gunman believed to have been inspired by far-right ideology has killed six people and injured more than a dozen others in an attack in the busy centre of Poland's second largest city.

Police said the attacker drove onto Main Market Square in Krakow, a popular tourist attraction, on Saturday afternoon and began randomly firing at people.

The attacker, who was equipped with military-style weapons and attire, was injured in a gunfight with police, one of whom was critically injured in the process.

The 25-year-old Polish man - described by one minister as "ultra-nationalist" - has been taken to hospital for surgery.

Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk said another three bodies were found during a search of the suspect's home around 125 miles (200km) away from Krakow.

Tusk said there were "strong indications" the two women and one man were the suspect's immediate family members.

He said: "Until now in Poland we haven't had such drastic cases of terrorism... that's what we have to call this cruel attack on people's lives here in Krakow."

Four women and two men were killed in the square. Three were Polish, one was British and two have not been identified, officials said.

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said: "I'm shocked and saddened by the appalling shooting in KrakÃ³w today."

"My thoughts are with the families of those who have lost their lives, everyone injured and all those affected by this senseless violence. The United Kingdom stands in solidarity with the people of Poland," he added.

The rampage began shortly before 15:00 local time (14:00 GMT) in the historic centre of Krakow, an ornate square which has long been a draw for tourists.

Footage showed the attacker's vehicle speeding through the centre of the city, and people fleeing as the sound of gunfire rang out.

The glass front of shops were shattered by bullets and a tram was shot at during the attack, which police say lasted for around three minutes.

Images from the scene showed overturned tables and scattered belongings left behind as people ran for their lives.

Armed police officers pursued the attacker's car until it crashed, at which point they engaged him in a firefight.

Distressing footage authenticated by BBC Verify captured the moment a police officer confronted the suspect as he lay on the ground.

The officer, who is visibly injured, can then be seen falling to the ground.

News.title: Andy Burnham wants to get closer to the EU - but he shouldn't expect a smooth ride
News.content:
First, Burnham inherited the broad deal that's likely to be signed. The UK and EU were originally meant to mint a new and, they hope, improved agreement back in May, then in July, and well, political upheavals mean one thing for getting things done â delay.

But that means the outlines of a new agreement have been clear for many months, an approach based on "closer alignment" as Sir Keir Starmer proclaimed to us at the start of the year.

So if the prime minister hails agreement, spare a thought for those who started the work to get it this far many months ago.

One source familiar with the negotiations told me, "They are 90% there", with agreements designed to make life easier for food producers, a deal on emissions trading which could help manufacturers, and new arrangements for youth visas (although it's understood there is still haggling over putting a cap on the numbers).

An EU source close to the process said: "The bone of contention is a cap â we proposed 150,000, the UK proposed 50,000 â but we would expect to reach a compromise", even though it has been "very tense" on both sides.

A last-minute call from the EU to cut tuition fees for its students is expected to be parked for now with more months of discussion to come. Another fine tradition - agree what you can, but file some tough stuff away for future chat.

There are dilemmas too on the EU's so-called "Made in Europe" plans â draft laws to protect its industries from being hammered by Chinese competition. The purpose is clear â to help the economy grow, with the prime minister quoting figures that suggest closer ties to the EU without going back in could add 0.4 percent to GDP.

But as the tabloid-friendly row over salty snacks illustrates, making it easier to do business with the bloc doesn't come without a cost, and a political awkwardness.

News.title: 'Dana, please take the job!' - Trump asks UFC boss to be White House press secretary
News.content:
US President Donald Trump has asked Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) boss Dana White to be White House press secretary, in a social media post.

"Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other," Trump wrote on Truth Social. "Dana, please take the job!"

It was unclear whether the president's public job offer was genuine, although White said later on Saturday: "I got a lot of jobs already."

The vacancy for White House press secretary has been open since mid-October, when Katie Zacharia exited after just a few days on the job.

Trump's post on Saturday afternoon comes after his fellow Republicans were routed in the US midterm elections, losing their congressional majorities.

The president called White "a violent Fighter and Warrior" and asked that he bring a number of high-profile UFC fighters with him on the job "even though some are not from our Country".

"We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left," Trump wrote, alongside photos of the six fighters.

Following Trump's post, White posted an Instagram photo of himself behind the lectern in the White House press briefing room.

"On to the next chapter," White wrote, though it was unclear if the post was tongue-in-cheek.

"Hell yeah! Do it, @DanaWhite!" White House communications director Steven Cheung posted on X, as he shared the president's message.

White was ringside for a fight in London on Saturday night between British former world champion Chris Billam-Smith and Jamaican-born Briton Cheavon Clarke at the Copper Box Arena.

Asked about the Trump offer at a news conference afterwards, the UFC chief executive said he was flying to Washington for a meeting with Trump on Monday.

"I'm sure we'll have something to talk about after that," he said, without being drawn on whether he was interested in taking on one of the most gruelling jobs in the political arena.

CNN cited a source familiar as saying that White had declined the idea.

As he noted in the news conference, he already has a number of time-consuming commitments.

As well as leading UFC and Power Slap, a regulated slap-fighting promotion league, he has just launched Zuffa Boxing, a professional promotion company.

And last year he was unveiled as one of three new board members of Meta, the owner of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp.

News.title: Germans wrestle with what to do with Hitler's destroyed Eagle's Nest retreat
News.content:
Perched on a ridge high up in the spectacular scenery of the German Alps lie the burned-out ruins of a mountain house called The Eagle's Nest, which is now at the heart of an intense debate about Germany's Nazi past.

Known in German as Kehlsteinhaus, the retreat was built by the Nazis in 1938, and frequented by Adolf Hitler and other high-ranking Nazis and their guests. After World War Two it was classified as a historical monument recalling the Nazi era.

Last month it was gutted by fire in a suspected arson attack, and some believe it should be completely destroyed, the site returned to nature and all memory of its Nazi past forgotten.

But others want it either partially or completely rebuilt, wary of the risk of turning it into a site for Neo-Nazi pilgrimage at a time when Germany is witnessing the resurgence of the far-right.

Germany has an "everlasting responsibility to communicate, to deal with our Nazi past", said Isabel Heinemann, professor of contemporary history at Munich's Ludwig-Maximilians-UniversitÃ¤t (LMU).

But rebuilding the site completely, she warned, would mean putting "highly ideologised or highly ideological architecture" back in place.

News.title: Royal Family join veterans and families at Festival of Remembrance
News.content:
King Charles III led senior members of the Royal Family as they paid tribute to British service personnel at this year's Festival of Remembrance.

The Prince of Wales and Catherine, Princess of Wales, joined the King and Queen Camilla at London's Royal Albert Hall to commemorate those who lost their lives in service, on the eve of Remembrance Sunday.

The audience stood and a fanfare played as the royals entered the concert hall for the annual event, which was also attended by bereaved families and serving personnel.

The King will lead the nation in two minutes of silence on Sunday to remember those who died serving in the two world wars and other conflicts.

He will be joined by other senior royals and political leaders at the annual National Service of Remembrance ceremony at the Cenotaph in central London, where they will lay wreaths.

Some 10,000 veterans will take part in the Royal British Legion's march-past, representing more than 300 different armed forces and civilian organisations.

News.title: Gaza wedding festival sees 250 couples married at the same time
News.content:
Amid the ruins of destroyed buildings and displaced people's tents, Gazans gathered to celebrate a mass wedding for Palestinian brides and grooms.

The ceremony, organised by the UAE's humanitarian mission Operation Gallant Knight 3, brought together brides and grooms from across Gaza for a celebration of what organisers described as love and new beginnings in the besieged enclave.

A ceasefire came into force in Gaza in October last year, but Israeli air strikes have continued almost every day.

The Gaza war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.

Israel responded by launching a military campaign against Hamas in Gaza, during which more than 74,640 people have been killed, according to the territory's health ministry.

News.title: My parents chose to die together and I was left to grieve alone
News.content:
Some people might find this article upsetting.

Early one morning in June 2024, Bas pulled up next to his parents' campervan, parked on a sunny marina in the north of the Netherlands.

His father and mother, Jan and Els, had spent most of their married life on water. Now in their 70s, they could no longer manage a houseboat. Their campervan, positioned close to the yachts and dinghies, was the next best thing.

Jan and Els got into their son's car. Bas started the engine. This would be the final time he drove his parents anywhere. For Jan and Els, this journey - to the local hospice - would be their last.

At 10:30 that morning they would be administered lethal medication by doctors and die together in what is known in the Netherlands as duo-euthanasia. It's legal and it's rare, but every year more Dutch people choose to end their lives this way.

News.title: Labubu hype seemed unstoppable, now the fluffy monster mania is dying
News.content:
For years, Labubu dolls seemed unstoppable.

Collectors young and old energetically snapped up "blind boxes" - sealed, mystery packages containing the quirky monsters - often paying $15 (Â£11) or more.

Those unable to get the characters they wanted were often prepared to pay much more on the resale market.

The hype around the creatures convinced a mega-fan from North Carolina, who goes by the name Ensito, to leave his tech job in 2024 to create Labubu content full-time, travelling as far as Italy and Spain to seek out the latest releases.

Ensito has spent more than $50,000 (Â£37,000) to build his collection of more than 400 Labubus, a figure he tells the BBC he's "embarrassed to say".

He even had a row of custom Labubu-like jagged teeth made by a dentist to wear at events.

But in recent months, Ensito's once-viral posts about the furry monsters have struggled. "Those videos used to be able to hit 10,000 really quickly but I'm struggling to do that now."

Ensito's focus has shifted to other trends like Hello Kitty and squishies.

It's a sign that the craze which made parent company Pop Mart worth more than US toy giants Hasbro and Mattel put together may be running out of steam. Analysts believe the Beijing-based brand is struggling to capture excitement beyond a single viral moment.

Pop Mart recently reported that global sales in the three months to the end of September had fallen by as much as 50% on the previous year.

The drop was particularly steep outside mainland China, with US revenue down by at least 70%.

News.title: Veterans shouldn't sleep rough this Christmas, Burnham says
News.content:
No one who served in the UK armed forces should have to sleep on the streets this Christmas, Andy Burnham has said.

Downing Street said the prime minister will personally write to councils across England on Armistice Day (11 November) to urge them to draw up specific plans to offer accommodation for veterans sleeping rough ahead of the festive period.

He will say that, going forward, national and local government should work under the "simple principle" that "no one who has served our country should ever be left to sleep rough on our streets".

Burnham will ask local authorities to use part of the additional Â£874m already announced to tackle homelessness specifically for housing veterans.

"People who stepped forward prepared to put their lives on the line for the rest of us should never lack a roof over their head," Burnham said in a statement issued on Saturday.

"When they need help, the country owes them more than warm words. It owes them a bed every night, a proper plan and someone in their corner from day one."

The PM will ask councils to work with local organisations and charities to tackle homelessness amongst veterans.

Downing Street said an additional Â£8.7m in funding would be allocated to eight organisations across the UK to help housing providers offer assistance to veterans with complex needs, including those with health or addiction problems.

Among them are Veteran Housing Scotland, Launchpad and SSAFA, the Armed Forces Charity.

The pledge, announced ahead of Remembrance Sunday, is part of Burnham's wider plan to offer everyone currently sleeping rough a bed this winter.

The most recent official figures estimated that there were 4,793 people sleeping rough, external on a single night in autumn 2025 in England - a record high. The number of people recorded as sleeping rough has been on the rise since 2021.

The government has committed Â£4.4bn in total to end rough sleeping.

Burnham previously faced criticism from the Conservatives for failing to end rough sleeping while he was the mayor of Greater Manchester.

He argued that Manchester's scheme attracted rough sleepers from the surrounding regions, adding that "it's only if everywhere does it at the same level that you can actually end rough sleeping".

Liberal Democrats defence spokesman James MacCleary MP said the funding was an "important first step" but that "a one-off cash injection won't fix a crisis years in the making".

He urged Burnham to guarantee long-term funding for councils to tackle homelessness "for good" and to put in place measures to prevent veterans "falling through the cracks in the first place".

The prime minister is urging any veterans who are sleeping rough, or those supporting them, to call a UK-wide helpline on 0800 9520774 to be connected directly to housing and other specialist support.

News.title: Thousands watch elaborate carnival cart procession
News.content:
Rock shows, Del Boy and his three-wheeler from Only Fools and Horses, and a circus big top were among the themes showcased during a spectacular illuminated carnival procession.

Thousands of people watched the event in Bridgwater, Somerset, where clubs spend the entire year preparing carts for the show.

Dan Prosser from the Renegades Carnival Club said the preparations were "more like a lifestyle than just a hobby," adding his non-carnival friends think his devotion to the event is "absolutely nuts".

The carnival ended with 210 people - including local MP Sir Ashley Fox - taking part in squibbing, where a large firework, strapped to a solid block of wood on the end of a pole, is lit.

News.title: Two men arrested after boy injured in sword attack
News.content:
Two men and a boy have been arrested after a teenager was injured in an attack involving a sword near two schools in Gloucester.

St Peter's High School and Willow Primary Academy, in Tuffley, were put into lockdown after the incident at 08:50 GMT on Friday.

Police said a 17-year-old suffered a wound "believed to have been caused by the sword".

A 19-year-old was arrested overnight on suspicion of assault occasioning actual bodily harm and affray. An 18-year-old was held on suspicion of possession of an offensive weapon, assault occasioning actual bodily harm and affray. Meanwhile another 17-year-old boy was arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender.

News.title: Roman settlement dating back 2,000 years found under new-build estate
News.content:
Homes have now been built over the excavation site on Gladstone Way, but not before dozens of items including pottery, coins and the jewellery were removed.

The area was also mapped and showed the settlement extended underneath the village of Mancot, which sits between Hawarden and Queensferry.

Matthews said, in spite of its position overlooking the important Roman city of Chester, very little associated archaeology had been found in north-east Wales until recently.

He said it meant that archaeologists and historians in the area had long debated whether it reflected a "poor relationship" between the Romans and the native population of the time.

But finds such as this one and others in Greenfield and Rossett in Wrexham, were making them realise it "probably wasn't the case".

Matthews said the Mancot site "possibly" originated in the Iron Age period, before the arrival of the Romans, and "continued to have successive occupation for a very long period of time".

This idea was strengthened by two coins found there - one from the reign of the emperor Commodus, who was in power from AD 177 to 192, and another depicting Constantine, who reigned about 200 years later.

News.title: Rob Brydon's battle to stay in character playing Peter O'Toole
News.content:
Actor and comedian Rob Brydon has said it was difficult to stay in character while playing the role of a legendary actor portraying a man who was frequently too hungover to do his job.

He was speaking to BBC Radio 4's Today programme about his role in new radio drama, Peter O'Toole Is Unwell.

It encompasses O'Toole's critically acclaimed stage role in Jeffrey Bernard is Unwell in the West End in 1999, along with his universally panned performance of Macbeth in 1980.

Brydon, who grew up in Baglan, Port Talbot, said taking on the role "felt like a challenge once we got into the studio" and he battled "to stay on the saddle" to remain in character.

The 61-year-old, known for his role as Uncle Bryn in Gavin and Stacey, said he initially thought "I could probably get close to his voice but there were a lot of words" written by award-winning playwright Terry Johnson.

The title of the audio drama is a riff on Keith Waterhouse's play Jeffrey Bernard Is Unwell, in which O'Toole played the title role of journalist Jeffrey Bernard to rave reviews in 1999.

It is said to derive from the words used by The Spectator magazine when the journalist had missed the deadline to file his column.

News.title: Evacuations in Liverpool city centre after car crash causes gas leak
News.content:
A gas leak caused by a car crashing into a restaurant in Liverpool city centre has led to road closures and the evacuation of neighbouring buildings.

The incident happened at about 12:30 GMT on North John Street when a Peugeot car hit the window of Tiger Rock Restaurant, Merseyside Police said.

The driver stayed at the scene and there is no indication that this was a deliberate act, the force said.

Three people who had been in the restaurant at the time of the crash were assessed for minor injuries, Merseyside Fire and Rescue Service said.

A spokesman said the impact caused a gas leak so a cordon has been put in place by firefighters and the police, with a structural engineer and a gas engineer due to attend.

Neighbouring buildings have been evacuated as a precaution and road closures are in place at the junction of Dale Street and North John Street, and also the junction of North John Street and Lord Street.

Buses have also been temporarily diverted with all Wirral Metro services terminating at Whitechapel, and starting their return journey from Sir Thomas Street.

News.title: Victims in rape cases must not feel like they are on trial, Burnham says
News.content:
Andy Burnham has said the government needs to make sure that victims in rape cases do not feel like they are on trial.

His comments come after Metropolitan Police boss Sir Mark Rowley told the BBC that what he heard reported from Russell Brand's trial came very close to "victim blaming".

The government needs to "constantly look" at how rape trials are conducted to better support alleged victims in court, the prime minister told Times Radio, although BBC News understands there are no plans to change the law around rape trials.

Actor and comedian Brand was found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault after a four-week trial in London.

During an interview with BBC Radio 4's Today programme on Friday, it was put to Sir Mark that Brand's defence barrister Ian Winter KC "told jurors none of the complainants had in his words 'resisted, screamed or even tried to leave'".

Sir Mark replied: "I think what I've heard reported heads towards, it's getting very close to victim blaming, which is something we've thought very hard about in policing and make sure we don't do."

He said he would support a call from the Victims' Commissioner for a legal duty that would require judges to direct juries on rape myths and misconceptions in every rape trial.

"It shouldn't be possible for inaccurate statements to be made to a jury to suggest that because a rape victim didn't behave in one way that somehow undermines their case," Sir Mark explained.

In a Times Radio interview on Saturday, Burnham said he would "look closely" at the police chief's comments.

He said the government needed to look at how to "make sure they do not leave the woman feeling like she is on trial in court".

"[I'm] always prepared to make changes," he said. "We need to encourage more women to come forward to report rape, we need to get the conviction rate up.

"All of this is part of our broader agenda as a government combatting violence against women and girls."

Pressed on whether this might lead to a change in the law, the prime minister replied: "I wouldn't rule anything out... I will study what's happened here in great detail."

Brand, who has starred in films including Forgetting Sarah Marshall, will be sentenced on Monday and is expected to face substantial jail time.

He was found not guilty of two other counts of rape, and one count of attempted indecent assault after the jury deliberated for eight-and-a-half hours.

The 51-year-old was refused bail and will spend the weekend in custody.

It has since been revealed that Brand is also facing further rape allegations made by two women and has been questioned by officers in relation to the complaints. The Met said its investigation "remains ongoing".

Sir Mark told BBC Breakfast he "wouldn't be surprised if many more came forward".

In the wake of Brand's trial, Victims' Commissioner Claire Waxman said rape trials must be conducted "in a way that challenges myths and misconceptions about sexual violence".

In a social media post, Waxman wrote that "victims need confidence that the justice process is fair and based on evidence, not myths and false assumptions about rape and trauma".

Speaking to the Today programme on Saturday, director and founder of the Centre for Women's Justice Harriet Wistrich agreed that juries need to understand "underlying behaviours" without "running to judgement" over how a victim behaved in a particular way.

But former Conservative MP Anna Soubry, who has now returned to her work as a barrister where she often defends rape and sexual offence cases in the Crown court, told the BBC "people are being misled" by Sir Mark's comments.

"Every single judge in those cases must give, and does give, a very firm direction to the jury on exactly these points," she said.

As a result, she said she was " really disappointed" in the police chief and stressed "we've got to trust our juries" who are able to have an understanding of the nature of sexual offences.

If you have been affected by any of the issues raised in this story, information and support can be found at the BBC's Action Line.

News.title: We thought mum abandoned us - then we discovered she'd been murdered
News.content:
"We didn't have anyone to support us really in our lives. We struggled growing up," added Mehmet.

They were unaware that their mother had been beaten to death by her partner before hiding her body in the cellar of their home for about a year before disposing of her remains in household waste bins.

The court heard Dunkley had maintained his account that Lashley had disappeared for decades, despite being spoken to by police multiple times.

He said she had left her youngest child, who was not Dunkley's son, alone in their flat. Dunkley took the nine-month-old to social services and he was later adopted.

Judge Chambers said the "most significant aggravating factor" in the case was that Dunkley had killed the mother of a baby, who she had still been breastfeeding.

Mehmet said Dunkley killed his mother "in such a horrible way and then lied to us for 27 years", and that learning about her death had made him feel guilty about the resentment he had felt in the past.

"I feel bad in a way now that I felt that way towards mum," he said.

News.title: Horrific mass shooting in Krakow as gunman kills six in Polish tourist spot
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A British national is among six people who were shot dead in Krakow on Saturday by a gunman authorities believe was inspired by far-right ideologies.

Poland’s defence minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz described the horrific attack in the city’s main market square as an “act of terror”.

Following the attack, the bodies of two women and a man were later discovered at the suspect’s home.

Police said the gunman drove into the Krakow’s historic quarter and began randomly firing at people, killing four women and two men. One is a British citizen, and at least three of the women are Polish, authorities said.

At least 16 people were also injured, including another British national.

The suspect, a 25-year-old Polish man, was shot and detained by armed officers during a gunfight which left one officer critically injured.

open image in gallery Emergency services arrive at the scene following the shooting ( AFP/Getty )

Later on Saturday, Polish prime minister Donald Tusk announced the discovery of three bodies at the home of the suspect almost 100 miles from Krakow. They were likely the man’s family members, Mr Tusk said.

The Polish interior minister Marcin Kierwinski said the attacker held “very radical views” and “was fascinated by far-right ideologies”.

In a press conference, Polish police commander-in-chief Marek Boron said: “There are 16 people injured including two police officers and the perpetrator himself – 11 of those are Polish citizens, five citizens of foreign countries.

“There are six fatalities, four women and two men – three Polish persons, one citizen of Great Britain and two persons who are not yet identified.”

open image in gallery Investigators at the scene of the shooting on Saturday night ( Reuters )

“We are undertaking activities at the place where the perpetrator lived, so I think we will know more what those investigations bring.”

As it emerged that a British citizen was among the dead, prime minister Andy Burnham paid tribute to the victims of the attack.

Mr Burnham said: “I’m shocked and saddened by the appalling shooting in Krakow today.

“My thoughts are with the families of those who have lost their lives, everyone injured and all those affected by this senseless violence. The United Kingdom stands in solidarity with the people of Poland.”

open image in gallery A police officer stands guard at the site of the shooting ( Reuters )

The gunman opened fire in Krakow’s Main Square, in the centre of the old town, at around 3.30pm with an automatic weapon.

Police said the suspect wore military-style fatigues and a bulletproof vest, and used a military-type long gun.

After being subdued by police, he was taken to hospital for surgery.

Krakow mayor Łukasz Gibała said the city will be in official mourning until Wednesday. He vowed that Krakow will remain open to visitors despite the tragedy. “The square will belong to us again,” Gibała said in a video posted to X.

Videos posted on social media by witnesses show people running away from the square to take cover on small streets nearby, as well as first responders trying to resuscitate victims.

open image in gallery Poland's prime minister Donald Tusk ( AP )

In one video, a police officer was seen repeatedly shooting the attacker, who was lying on the street, only to later slowly collapse himself to the ground.

The FCDO is advising British nationals in Krakow to “follow the advice of local authorities and monitor local media”.

In a statement, foreign secretary Ed Miliband said: “The UK Government deeply mourns the British national and other victims who have died after the appalling attack in Krakow.

“All of my deepest condolences go to the families of the victims. The UK stands resolutely in solidarity with the people of Poland.”

News.title: Trump offers press secretary role to UFC CEO Dana White
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

President Donald Trump said Saturday that he had offered UFC president and CEO Dana White the job of press secretary.

“I am pleased to announce that the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior, has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States,” Trump wrote on Truth Social.

White responded by posting an image of himself in the White House press room with the caption: “On to the next chapter.” Later, White noted that he had “a lot of jobs already” at a UFC press conference but said he would meet with Trump to discuss the role Monday, The Wall Street Journal reported.

The position has been vacant ever since Katie Zacharia was fired October 16, five days into the job, after a single, widely panned press briefing.

The offer signals a second potential shake-up in the White House since Tuesday’s midterm elections which saw Democrats regained control of both the House and Senate. On Friday, Trump announced that Stephen Miller would replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff.

open image in gallery President Trump offered the role of White House press secretary to Dana White, the president and CEO of the UFC ( AFP/Getty )

On Saturday, Trump also named six prominent mixed martial arts fighters he wanted White to bring on as assistants, including fighters from Russia and Brazil.

“I have requested that he bring with him assistants, even though some are not from our Country, of Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, Amanda Nunes, and Kayla Harris,” Trump wrote.

“We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left,” Trump wrote. “Dana will be a Press Secretary like none other. Dana, please take the job!”

White, a longtime friend of the president, has no experience as a government spokesperson, though he has gotten into explosive exchanges with reporters.

This summer, he helped organize UFC Freedom 250, the MMA event held on the White House lawn to celebrate Trump’s 80th birthday. White’s net worth is estimated to be about $600 million, according to Forbes.

open image in gallery During her debut briefing, Katie Zacharia took questions from just three reporters over the course of 14 minutes. She also mistakenly referred to husband as ‘my president’ ( Getty )

The White House has been without a press secretary since Zacharia was fired last month, following a debut briefing that lasted just 14 minutes and drew criticism from both Democrats and Republicans.

“No wonder that poor young woman — she was a perfect, beautiful woman — when she walked into that press room and they started screaming at her, she freaked out,” Trump said. Defending herself, Zacharia said she was not given enough time to prepare.

Her predecessor, Karoline Leavitt, served as the president’s chief spokesperson for 19 months before leaving in August to spend more time with her family.

During his first term, the president had four press secretaries: Sean Spicer, Sarah Huckabee Sanders, Stephanie Grisham and Kayleigh McEnany.

News.title: Little Rascals star turned ‘radical Catholic extremist’ starts GoFundMe ahead of birth of sixth child
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Bug Hall, who starred as Alfalfa in the beloved 1994 film The Little Rascals, has started a GoFundMe to appeal for help with his rapidly expanding family.

41-year-old Hall, whose real name is Brandon Rowan, made headlines earlier this year when he opened up about his decision to flee Hollywood and live off-grid, becoming a self-described “radical Catholic extremist.”

Now, he’s reaching out to friends, family and fans to ask for financial support.

On the GoFundMe page, Hall wrote: “It's now six years since I self-cancelled, and I have avoided doing one of these in all that time. I always said this was my choice, and so I didn't want to offload the glorious burden of it unless there was no other choice. Well here we are.”

He continued: “We've made it onto the new land in record time, but I'm a few materials short of having things working right, and I've fallen a little behind on the few bills we have (phone, propane for the camper, and an unexpected electric hookup service fee).”

open image in gallery Bug Hall, pictured in September 2016, is now living ‘off grid’ and expecting a sixth child ( Getty )

Hall went on to say that while his family is “overjoyed to be where we are” and “even enjoying roughing it”, financial realities are hitting hard.

“Baby six is less than a month away, and I really need some help getting the last few things buttoned up beforehand,” he wrote.

Hall concluded his appeal: “My hope is to finalize everything here over the next two weeks so I can take some work until the baby arrives. Times are hard for everyone, and I'm no more deserving than anyone else, but I ask in your charity that you help where you can, whether monetarily, by sharing this, or by prayer and sacrifice for the Hall-Barnetts of the Holy Cross.”

Hall left Hollywood in 2020 along with his wife and five kids, moving to Texas, Michigan, and Ohio, before settling on an 80-acre plot of land near Mountain View, Arkansas.

According to reports earlier this year, the former child star had taken a vow of poverty and gave away the fortune he made from his acting career. He also sold most of his belongings ahead of plans to build their “off grid” family home complete with its own electric and plumbing systems.

Hall described himself as a “radical Catholic extremist” and “medieval moralist” in a video he posted to his public YouTube channel in April 2025. His worldview has been praised by followers of the so-called “trad Cath” movement.

News.title: A strong earthquake with a preliminary magnitude of 5.7 strikes Japan, meteorological agency says
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A strong earthquake shook central Japan early Sunday, shattering store windows, causing people to flee buildings and leaving at least 22 people injured, according to local media.

Japan’s Meteorological Agency put the quake’s magnitude at 5.7, while the U.S. Geological Survey reported it at magnitude 5.5. Smaller aftershocks were reported.

A wide area near Aichi Prefecture was affected, including the city of Hamamatsu, the ancient capitals of Kyoto and Nara and nearby prefectures of Yamanashi, where Mount Fuji is located, as well as Gifu.

Japanese TV footage showed shattered store windows and scattered shards of glass on the streets. A bookstore was left with mounds of books that had flown off the shelves. The injuries included people who fell from stairs while they were trying to flee.

The quake, which struck at 1:04 a.m., was located about 40 kilometers (25 miles) below the earth's surface in Shizuoka Prefecture. Aichi and Shizuoka are neighboring regions. They are far enough from Tokyo that the quake was not felt there. The most violent shaking was felt in Aichi, according to official seismic assessments.

The Shinkansen bullet trains were running at slower speeds in the affected areas as a precautionary measure. Sometimes quakes can damage the railways the trains run on.

Japan is located in an area that is prone to earthquakes.

News.title: King Charles to be joined by Burnham and thousands of veterans for Remembrance Sunday service at Cenotaph
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The nation will fall silent for two minutes as the King leads acts of commemoration to honour those who lost their lives in military conflict.

At London's Cenotaph during the National Service of Remembrance on Sunday, Charles will be accompanied by members of the royal family alongside key political figures to lay wreaths.

Around 10,000 veterans are expected to participate in the Royal British Legion’s annual parade, which will feature delegations from more than 300 military and civilian groups.

Those taking part in the march span every generation, ranging from young military cadets and grieving children to a small number of remaining Second World War veterans.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said: "I’m incredibly proud to be honouring those whose sacrifice continues to protect our way of life to this day.

"Remembrance Sunday gives us an opportunity, not only to mark that sacrifice and offer our gratitude, but also to reflect on its significance. To reflect on the selflessness and courage it takes to commit your life to protecting others.

open image in gallery Prime Minister Andy Burnham (Carlos Jasso/PA) ( PA Wire )

"I want to offer my personal thanks to those who served and those who continue to serve in our Armed Forces communities to this day."

Among those participating is 43-year-old Steve Hooper, a former RAF mechanical transport driver who served during the conflict in Iraq and will join the Invictus Games Alumni contingent.

He said: "I saw a lot of trauma in Iraq as an ambulance driver, and when I came back, I was struggling with sleep and having flashbacks. If it wasn’t for the support I received from the Royal British Legion through the Invictus Games, I don’t know where I’d be today.

"I am proud to be marching alongside my fellow team members as we reflect on our recovery journeys and remember all those who weren’t as lucky. I’ll also be thinking about the families who still live with the impact of service and conflict. For me, it’s a time to pause, acknowledge and remember."

Joining the parade for her very first time is Annie Duplock, a 103-year-old veteran of the Women’s Land Army.

Having misrepresented her age in order to register, Ms Duplock enlisted in the Land Army back in 1940 when she was just 16.

She spent four years working at a Leicestershire farm, where her long days were filled with harvesting crops, ploughing fields and milking cows to support the home front throughout the Second World War.

Speaking over eight decades later, she said: "I feel very honoured to be taking part in the parade and to represent the Land Girls. I’m very excited, although a little apprehensive as I don’t quite know what to expect.

"I think it will be a very emotional day, bringing back memories of all those who didn’t return home. It will be lovely to be there and remember them."

Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy said: "This Remembrance Sunday, we come together to reflect and honour the sacrifices that our Armed Forces made all those years ago in the First and Second World Wars and continue to make today.

"It is our duty to ensure that the immense courage of those who have served our country is never forgotten. They went to war to give us 80 years of peace.

open image in gallery Lisa Nandy paid tribute to the fallen soldiers (PA) ( PA Wire )

"We are about to raise the first generation for whom fighting a war really is part of history. Our future generations must know the significance of those who served in our national story, that they forged a path for friendship and cooperation that meant no-one in our country has had to fight a war since.

"Today, we remember them, in grief and in gratitude, mindful that their legacy lives on in the freedom we enjoy today."

Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said: "I grew up with my grandfather and great-grandfather’s war medals proudly on display in our living room. Defence runs in my blood and I feel intently the importance of remembrance to those who have served and their families.

"This weekend is a moment to pause and reflect on the enormous debt we owe to our Armed Forces, to pay tribute to those who made the ultimate sacrifice defending our freedoms, and to thank the personnel keeping us safe tonight.

"We have a moral duty to stand by our veterans and the military families who sacrifice so much. They are the best of us, and we owe them our support as well as our gratitude and admiration."

Chief of the Defence Staff Air Chief Marshal Sir Richard Knighton said: "Today we honour the courage of all those who have served and died in conflict.

"For the Armed Forces community, remembrance is a deeply personal time during which we reflect on the service of our predecessors and remember the colleagues we have lost.

open image in gallery Wes Streeting also said the UK owes an ‘enormous debt’ to its Armed Forces ( Reuters )

"That same spirit of service continues to drive the men and women who serve today."

Mark Atkinson, director general, Royal British Legion, said: "As we come together on Remembrance Sunday, we pay tribute to all those who have served and sacrificed, from generations past to those still serving today.

"This year we have paid tribute to those who served in more recent conflicts, including the challenging operations in Bosnia, the Iraq War and the first Gulf War, and recognised the families who continue to live with the impact of that service.

"From risking their lives in war zones, providing support during emergencies and humanitarian disasters, and spending time away from loved ones, we owe those who serve in the Armed Forces, and the families who stand alongside them, our gratitude. We encourage the nation to pause, reflect and remember their service and sacrifice."

News.title: Top polling analyst believes this Democrat is runaway favorite for 2028 presidential pick
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A leading polling analyst has named his preferred candidate for the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination.

Nate Silver, who correctly predicted that Democrats would reclaim control of both the House and Senate in the midterm elections, revealed his choice Saturday at the Crooked Con political conference.

Georgia Senator Jon Ossoff, fresh off his re-election victory, would be “a slam dunk number one pick,” Silver said, according to The Daily Beast.

“He won by what was like 16, 17, 18 points or something,” Silver said. “He seems like the uniformly ‘compromise candidate’ between the progressive and the more centrist factions of the party. And he seems very talented.”

Silver, who founded FiveThirtyEight and publishes the Silver Bulletin newsletter, also suggested that the 39-year-old senator’s looks could work in his favor. “Is he looksmaxxing or something?” he asked.

open image in gallery Polling analyst Nate Silver said Senator Jon Ossoff would be ‘a slam dunk number one pick’ for the Democratic presidential nominee in 2028 ( Crooked Media, X )

A Georgetown graduate and former Capitol Hill staffer, Ossoff was first elected to the Senate in 2021, becoming the nation’s first Jewish senator and the first Democrat elected to a full term in Georgia since 1996.

He has built a reputation as a moderate Democrat and outspoken critic of the Trump administration, drawing widespread attention this summer for pressing a Trump nominee on the outcome of the 2020 election.

On Tuesday, he won re-election with 59 percent of the vote, defeating Republican challenger Mike Collins, who received 41 percent. In his victory speech, he said the midterm results were proof “the American people have rejected the failed lame duck president Donald J. Trump.”

Over the past two weeks, his odds of winning the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination have surged on online prediction platforms. He has emerged as the front-runner on both Kalshi and Polymarket, overtaking New York Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and California Governor Gavin Newsom.

open image in gallery On Tuesday, Ossoff won re-election with 59 percent of the vote, defeating Republican challenger Mike Collins, who received 41 percent ( Reuters )

Silver is not alone in seeing Ossoff as a potential presidential contender.

“He’s their new Obama,” Fox News host Laura Ingraham wrote of the senator this summer.

“Ossoff would be a very interesting candidate,” Hank Sheinkopf, a former adviser to Bill Clinton, told The Observer this month. “Because he’s in the center, he represents a southern state, his rhetoric fits the moment, and he looks the part. He could be a real player.”

Some strategists have said that Ossoff’s stance toward Israel could undermine his chances of winning the Democratic nomination.

The senator has described himself as “a committed supporter of the State of Israel,” while criticizing Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and accusing Israeli forces of violating the law in Gaza. Speculation about Ossoff’s political future became a line of attack during his Senate campaign.

Collins accused his opponent of treating the Senate as a stepping stone to the presidency, telling supporters ahead of Election Day: “All he cares about is using us as a platform.” He had previously labeled Ossoff a “globetrotting trust fund kid.”

Ossoff, in turn, said Collins held “disqualifying ties to white nationalism and neo-Nazi ideology.”

Despite growing White House buzz, Ossoff has said his focus remains on the Senate. “I have zero interest in running for president. I'm not running for president,” he said last month.

Political chatter and early polling are not always reliable predictors of success. Two years before the 2016 presidential election, Jeb Bush was widely viewed as a front-runner for the Republican nomination. He ultimately dropped out after failing to win a single primary.

News.title: ‘We heard about 20 shots’: Witnesses describe terror of Krakow shooting as Briton among six killed
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Terrified witnesses have described the moment a gunman opened fire in Krakow’s main market square, killing six people, including a British national.

Police said the man drove a car into the tourist spot on Saturday just before 3pm, and then began firing randomly at people as panic broke out.

Armed officers rushed to the scene and engaged in a shootout, with two officers injured, including one in a critical condition after suffering three gunshot wounds.

Among the four women and two men killed, one was a British national, Poland’s police chief Marek Boron told reporters on Saturday evening. Three others were Polish while the remaining two are yet to be identified.

The suspect, a 25-year-old Polish citizen who was shot and taken to hospital, had been “influenced by far-right ideology”, said Polish interior minister Marcin Kierwinski.

Polish prime minsiter Donald Tusk later said that two women and one man were found dead during searches of the suspect’s home. They are believed to be his close family, Mr Tusk said.

Witnesses of the shooting have recalled the moment they heard gunshots and ran for cover. One person reported hearing “about 20 shots”.

The main market square is typically busy with traditional horse-drawn carriages and is popular with tourists.

open image in gallery Police privacy screens are installed in a cordoned off area after a shooter opened fire in a market square in Krakow, Poland, Saturday, 7 November 2026, leaving people dead and injured, according to authorities ( AP )

“We were walking to the store and heard gunshots. Suddenly we turned around, people started running, tourists from other countries didn’t know what was happening. We heard about 20 shots,” Aleksander told Poland’s Faktowi.

He said that he “ran into the store, the lady closed the door, and we waited a moment”.

“I’ve never witnessed such panic. People were running into stores to hide,” he said.

Caitlin Shasby from Newcastle flew to the city on Saturday and said that she had heard the shots ringing from her hotel.

“We heard shots from hotel room but didn’t realise what it was until we received a call from the hotel confirming there had been a shooting,” she told the BBC.

She said that police were outside the hotel “barricading” the street.

open image in gallery Police guard the access to an area in the historic centre of Krakow ( AFP/Getty )

Witnesses told TV Republika that they saw black Subaru drive up to the location.

“I saw the guy, he started loading his machine gun,” one witness told the news station.

“I don’t think he was firing blindly, these were deliberate shots. He had a sort of police mask on and goggles on. Then he shot at the church and fled towards Grodzka Street. Everyone was running away from there, people in horse-drawn carriages.”

One man described how several people cowered for safety in a police station after the shots rang out.

“I saw shots being fired from the driver’s side window, and smoke was coming out,” the man, who said his name was Konrad, told Interia.

open image in gallery A woman reacts at the site of a shooting near the main market square of Krakow ( Reuters )

“I ran to the police station in the main market square; when I burst inside, it was full of people hiding on the floor.”

A 67-year-old man called Julek told Reuters that he had narrowly missed being shot himself.

Julek saw a dark car appear suddenly before the driver started shooting at a group of people and drove off.

“If we had been two minutes earlier, we might have been shot,” he said.

The victims of the shooting have yet to be identified.

Mr Kierwinski told journalists on Saturday evening that the suspect was interested in far-right ideology.

“Everything points to the fact that ‌the shooter ‌was influenced by far-right ideology, a ⁠matter that will also be subject to investigation,” he said. “Police officers are on-site, as are ‌agents from ​the Internal Security ‌Agency, both ⁠here at ⁠the scene and at ‌the individual’s ​family ‌home.”

Police spokesperson Andrzej Fijolek told private broadcaster TVN ⁠24 that the assailant used an AR-15 rifle and that he had a firearms licence.

A period of national mourning will take place on Sunday and Monday.

News.title: Lando Norris takes pole at Interlagos after chaotic qualifying session
News.content:
McLaren’s Lando Norris claimed pole for the São Paulo Grand Prix for a third consecutive year as he emerged victorious from a marathon, rain-affected qualifying session at Interlagos lasting two and a half hours.

But there was further frustration for his compatriot George Russell, who lashed out at his Mercedes pit wall after being told to abort a push lap in Q3 which he felt would have been good enough to finish qualifying in first place.

Whether Russell was right was debatable, but you could understand his frustration. The Briton has endured a miserable season, dropping from second to fourth in the drivers’ championship in Mexico last weekend after suffering yet another power unit issue.

Russell ended up leaving the Mexico paddock early while team-mate Kimi Antonelli celebrated becoming the sport’s youngest ever champion.

News.title: Man City look to be crumbling after guilty verdict
News.content:
Is this the day the xG gods reward Nottingham Forest? Oliver Glasner’s team sit 19th having won one game all season, but there is no doubt that their performances have been significantly better than results and they might need their luck to turn against Man City team full of firepower.

Despite all of the positive indicators in Forest’s underlying data, Glasner caused some alarm with his comments after last weekend’s defeat at Brentford.

The Austrian said: “We have to accept it’s not good enough. If we lose four of the last five games, it’s not good enough. And that’s why for me, it’s now time that we change things, that I change things, and that’s what I will do.

“I feel now maybe I made too many compromises in some stuff, and it’s always compromises. It’s a clear way. I will tell [the players] what we want to do, what we have to do, and if the players buy in, I think we can have a turnaround, and if not, the sixth manager [since the start of last season] will come in.”

Dangerous words perhaps when you work for Evangelos Marinakis, but John Percy reported this week that Glasner was backed by his players in a squad meeting.

City are smarting from back-to-back defeats by Aston Villa and Brighton, but they created more than enough in both games to claim some sort of result. Nevertheless, there is a persistent sense that their defensive unit remains too marshmellow-like over the course of 38 games, and Forest have the counter-attacking threat to test them.

Glasner has happy memories of playing City, beating them in the 2025 FA Cup final with Crystal Palace, but his Forest reign is in urgent need of a signature victory and performance.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Rees-Zammit delivers in best position but work to do for sloppy Wales
News.content:
Maybe it is an indication that Wales are improving that this latest close victory over Japan was greeted with a shrug instead of euphoria.

A year ago, almost to the day, Steve Tandy, the Welsh head coach jumped around and hugged his staff, after a one-point win over the Brave Blossoms and there were reports of red-shirted fans in this stadium crying in joy and relief.

Yet that was Wales’s first home success in 10 Tests and, despite the form since hardly raising itself anywhere near levels of excellence, much more was expected on this occasion.

Yes, Tandy’s men prevailed and it was a huge positive to watch player-of-the match Louis Rees-Zammit in great nick on the wing. Nobody should overestimate the Bristol man’s display because the game knows that he can operate even better, but after this there can now be no doubt that he is a wing rather than a full-back. The 25-year-old conjured five line breaks, beat 13 defenders and made 121 metres.

Yet most notably, Rees-Zammit scored his first try for his country in eight matches and that is exactly what he was put on the green-green grass to do. After assisting in fellow wing Josh Adams’s opening try – this other resurgent British and Irish Lion bagged a brace – Rees-Zammit showed his predatory instincts to go over after a wonderful deft offload from centre Eddie James.

News.title: Odegaard winner spares officials from bizarre VAR row
News.content:
Newly-promoted Hull City stunned Arsenal at the Emirates thanks to goals from Geovanni and Daniel Cousin in September 2008, but you will find long odds on them repeating the feat this afternoon.

With Manchester City playing at Nottingham Forest in the later kick-off, Mikel Arteta’s team have the chance to extend their lead at the top of the Premier League and make it 27 points from a possible 30 going into the international break.

Victory at Anfield last weekend was achieved with steel and resolve, but the more intricate side of Arsenal’s attacking play will be under the microscope against opponents likely to defend deep and in numbers.

With that in mind, it was noteworthy that Kai Havertz, Martin Odegaard, Bruno Guimaraes and Myles Lewis-Skelly started the Champions League win at Slavia Prague on the bench, with only Odegaard coming on.

Declan Rice played the full 90 minutes, and one wonders if this is a rare chance for Arteta to leave him out of a Premier League starting XI.

Hull are 12th and have lost only two league games, a performance which far exceeds the gloomy pre-season forecasts for their chances. However, they are winless since the end of August and have not kept a clean sheet since a goalless draw with Aston Villa on Sept 4.

There is one other three o’clock kick-off: Fulham host Newcastle United at Craven Cottage, with Matthias Jaissle under increasing pressure.

Newcastle were booed off at St James’ Park on Monday after their limp defeat by Everton, and have looked far too easy to play through all season, with their defensive statistics making for grim reading.

Alvaro Arbeloa was in Jaissle’s position a few weeks ago, but Fulham appear to have turned a corner and were impressive in a 1-1 at Villa Park last time out. There were reports of dressing room unrest, but Fulham rank highly for possession and chance creation so it appears the Spaniard is putting his stamp on things.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Spurs to make formal complaint over Jayden Bogle decision
News.content:
Very happy against an in-form side. The first-half was [even], they were in front, we were in front but the second half, it was never in doubt. We were pushing, making chances and we were relentless. After a difficult period with key players out we showed great spirit and unity today. It was a fully deserved win and we are happy.

Sometimes [substitutions] work like this! Noah was a lat call. He has been a whole week out of training. Credit to the physios and our medical department because the doctors said at the beginning of the week that he had no chance of the weekend. In the end they said if I was disciplined and didn’t put him on the pitch for more than 15-20 minutes he could play. And a first assist for Harry [Wilson] and an ice-cold finish from Noah.

If you accept all Tottenham’s invitations to stop the pass with your pressing, this is what they want to bypass you. You have to close the centre and be spot on to allow them possession in areas where they can’t hurt you but be brave when you have the [right] position to press and also in our possession.

I haven’t watched it back. I know there were a couple of situations, a hand ball and this one but I can tell you that Jayden Bogle has no bad intention.That I can guaranteed. It looked unlucky and an unlucky outcome. We hope Mathys [Tel] will recover quickly and we wish him all the best. Jayden is not a nasty player, he is perhaps the softest in the whole league. I call him my butterfly.

We were unlucky at Arsenal and not to get anything at Sundeland and Bournemouth. Against Manchester United we were far the better side but you can see how quickly momentum can slip at this level and for that it’s good to have the winning feeling back and for that credit to my boys.

News.title: Brutal truth is Scotland never looked like beating All Blacks
News.content:
“They [New Zealand] are playing some excellent rugby right now and it is our first game of the season, which is always the toughest challenge for us too. It is a different New Zealand team. It is a team that is playing much more ambitious rugby. They are informed, they are cohesive. They played a lot of Test matches over the summer. We are going to have to find ways to win, find ways to stay in the fight because they will have a lot of possession too.”

New Zealand won all three of their home fixtures back in July in the first half of the Nations Championship, beating France, Italy and Ireland to claim a maximum 15 points. They faced Australia in two Bledisloe Cup fixtures last month, with the All Blacks easing to victory in both matches, scoring 93 points. They will go on to face Wales and England after this game. The All Blacks have travelled to the northern hemisphere without captain Ardie Savea, who is sidelined with a shoulder injury.

“Scotland are a quality side,” New Zealand head coach Dave Rennie said. “They are very well coached and have built a lot of depth over recent years. They play a very similar brand of footy to us and we know we will need to be at our best on Saturday [today]. Murrayfield is an iconic place to play so it will be a special occasion to kick off our northern tour.”

It has been an emotional week for the All Blacks as they continue to come to terms with the tragic loss of their long-time head of security Logan Cadwallader, who died at the team’s Edinburgh hotel earlier this week.

Kick-off from Murrayfield is at 2.10pm.

News.title: Feinberg-Mngomezulu leads Springboks’ nine-try obliteration of Italy
News.content:
What a difference a decade makes. In November 2016, Italy beat South Africa for the first, and so far only, time. Now the Springboks have obliterated Italy – and the roots of this victory can be traced back to that defeat 10 years ago.

That historic result sparked a major rethink in South Africa, a rethink that ultimately led to Rassie Erasmus replacing Allister Coetzee as head coach in early 2018. Erasmus has overseen a remarkable transformation of the Boks since: from an embarrassing loss in Italy to back-to-back world champions.

This win in Turin was built on what Erasmus’s Boks are known for: a potently powerful set-piece and a back line that can deliver mesmerising moments. The one disappointment for their head coach will be how they failed to match the intensity and ruthlessness of their first-half performance in the second 40 minutes.

“It’s almost impossible to put 80 minutes together at 100 per cent,” he said afterwards. “But when you win 66-7, I don’t think you can start nitpicking problems in the second half. That said, we have to play much better than this if we want to be competitive against France and Ireland.”

The Boks were 45-0 up at the break having scored six tries. The majority came off the back of their driving line-out, which they were able to launch to great effect inside Italy’s 22. Morne van den Berg, Malcolm Marx (two) and Siya Kolisi were all beneficiaries of the power of their maul in the first half. Damian Willemse also enjoyed an easy run-in when Jasper Wiese released him into space, but the stand-out finish came from Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu inside 10 minutes.

The 24-year-old fly-half is undoubtedly one of the most exciting players in world rugby and he showed his full repertoire here: deft hands, pinpoint vision and metronomic kicking. The opening try was special, too: his dummy carved out the space for him to break through Italy and he then had the pace to beat any chasing defenders to the corner, where he acrobatically finished one-handed.

News.title: Ireland send out ominous warning with second-gear walloping of Argentina
News.content:
Is it time to fire up the emerald green bandwagon? Not quite yet. But this was not a bad start to Ireland’s autumn; a 42-12 walloping of Los Pumas with Andy Farrell’s team still nowhere near their best. That should be highly encouraging for those of an Irish persuasion.

A year out from the World Cups of 2015, 2019 and 2023, Ireland had enjoyed banner seasons, eyeing up global glory. They never made it past the quarter-finals.

The build-up this time has been tougher going – the Aviva, unusually for this time of year – was not even full for this Nations Championship encounter. But perhaps Ireland will be better for it. They had far too much on a crisp Friday night in Dublin for an Argentina team who were missing a few of their stars, notably Bath’s Santiago Carreras and Lyon prop Thomas Gallo, but still packing 750 caps’ worth of Test experience in their starting XV.

Farrell was missing a few big names himself. Caelan Doris and Jack Conan were out injured, with the Englishman opting to hand Sean Jansen and Nick Timoney starts in the back row. Farrell also chose to start Craig Casey rather than Jamison Gibson-Park – arguably their best player of the last 18 months – at scrum-half, with Sam Prendergast starting again at 10 given Jack Crowley’s absence.

All in all there was a slightly experimental feel to proceedings, making Argentina potentially dangerous visitors. But Ireland had far too much in reserve. Hugo Keenan grabbed a hat-trick and took the player of the match award. Robert Baloucoune was consistently excellent. Mack Hansen’s return on the wing was hugely welcome. Tominey stood out in the back row.

Farrell said he was delighted with the result, if not the entire performance, making special mention of the likes of Keenan, Hansen, Ryan Baird and Andrew Porter, all of whom were returning from long injury lay-offs.

“The game’s never going to be perfect. But if you look at the bigger picture, to win 42-12 against a really good side in Argentina, I don’t think too many teams have done that,” Farrell said. “You have to be pleased.”

Asked whether he was happier with the 42 points scored or the meagre 12 conceded, Farrell added that it was probably the latter: “We want to be known for our defence. It shows our mentality.”

Los Pumas scored the first try of the game, Mateo Carreras getting the jump on Casey in the corner to field a Tomás Albornoz crossfield kick.

Sports.title: Valencia vs Real Madrid suspended as players carry stretcher across pitch after medical emergency in stands
Sports.content:
FOOTIE WORRY Valencia vs Real Madrid suspended as players carry stretcher across pitch after medical emergency in stands







Next

REAL MADRID’S clash with Valencia was temporarily halted following a medical emergency in the stands.

The match referee stopped the game so that medical attention could be brought to the spectator.

Players from both teams had the situation explained to them by the official in charge.



Valencia stars Pepelu and Jose Gaya made sure to help as much as they could.



The duo, alongside a pair of medical staff, ran with the stretcher to bring it across to the stand as quickly as possible.

Valencia medical staff and stadium paramedics then gave the fan proper attention.

After a delay of a few minutes, the action was able to get back underway.



Real Madrid had led 2-0 at the time of the stoppage.

Federico Valverde fired Jose Mourinho‘s side into the lead shortly before the half hour mark, with Arda Guler doubling his side’s advantage on 36 minutes.

Not long after the second half delay, Kylian Mbappe notched a third to make the points safe.

Gaya, 31, was sent off on 79 minutes and Real Madrid went on to win 3-0.



The match was always going to be played under an emotional backdrop, as both sides joined forces to pay tribute to Jesus de Miguel.

The late Tenerife striker tragically died aged 30 on Tuesday following an accidental collision during a match the previous evening.

Games across Spain this weekend have been marked by touching tributes.



Stars from Valencia and Real Madrid – including the likes of Mbappe and Jude Bellingham – wore T-shirts honouring De Miguel.

The match was also paused on nine minutes so that players, officials, staff and supporters could come together to take part in a minute’s applause.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick has no idea whether he’ll still be Man Utd boss after Aston Villa clash with sacking season approaching
Sports.content:
Next

MICHAEL CARRICK has not been told he is certain to be in charge of Manchester United after their Premier League fixture with Aston Villa on Sunday.

United could be in the relegation zone at kick-off after one win and four defeats from their nine league matches.



Carrick’s position remains in serious doubt after United resisted sacking him in the wake of the 3-0 drubbing by Bournemouth two weeks ago.

United do not play for two weeks after the Villa match due to the November internationals, which is traditionally a time where clubs change managers.



Carrick revealed that he has received no assurances he will remain the United head coach beyond this week but plans are in place for the period.

He said: “No, no. Just carry on as absolute normal.

“Maybe three or four senior players will be in and around [the training ground], but we’ll certainly train next week and maybe have the weekend off.

“We’ll see how that develops, who’s left behind, who’s with us and what they need. But there’ll certainly be training next week.

“Whatever happens, what’s going to happen is going to happen in terms of the game (against Villa), and we’ve got to prepare right, looking forward to it.

“I said the other night I was really looking forward to the game going into it, I genuinely was. I wasn’t making anything up there for you.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

“Playing at home on the back of the other night, the supporters hopefully looking forward to coming and energised and feeling good about what they might see.

“And we’ve got to repay that.”

Carrick is not planning to get away from the United maelstrom during the pause in the schedule. Ole Gunnar Solskjaer returned to his native Norway five years ago after a stay of execution but was sacked after a 4-1 thumping by Watford in United’s first game back following the autumn internationals.

Carrick and his family have lived in Cheshire for 20 years and both of his children have grown up in the area.

His wife, Lisa, has taught pilates in Alderley Edge, their son, Jacey, is in the United academy while daughter Louise has been in attendance for home games this season.



At the end of last season, Carrick joked a summer holiday was not in the offing due to his children’s school exams. He is not expecting a drastically different break this month.

“Not really different to normal,” he added. “Generally not.

“I think international breaks are always a time when talking about the players that aren’t going away and for the staff, I think there is a little bit to re-energise and freshen up.

“I think some of the players that go away in internationals, they get freshened up in a different environment, so there is an element of that, but I don’t really need it. I’m fine as I am.”

Sports.title: Youri Tielemans’ Man Utd boast has massively backfired as Red Devils host Aston Villa sitting 11 points adrift of them
Sports.content:
Next

YOURI TIELEMANS said after his £35million arrival at Old Trafford three months ago: “There are still clubs above Aston Villa and Manchester United is one of them.”

The Belgium captain’s new side are five points below his former employers Villa in the Premier League, with Michael Carrick’s outfit also 11 places adrift of them in the Champions League group phase.



Tielemans is in line to face his previous club this afternoon but the 29-year-old midfielder’s summer move has epitomised United’s malaise this season.

It was an opportunistic buy when a deal for Ederson collapsed as United prised him away from the Midlands by triggering the release clause in his contract.



A reactionary swoop for a player with plenty of miles on the clock — but it has taken its toll.

Tielemans, who claimed at the World Cup his body “switched off”, was the only United player to start the first 12 games this term.



And his leggy performances did not help the team’s woeful run of results.

United have been accused of a lack of running this season but Tielemans is a calm, composed player rather than a bundle of energy in the middle.

Even his old boss Unai Emery admitted he had to be patient with Tielemans when he joined the Villans from Leicester in 2023 — and the Spaniard has backed his former star in the engine room to be a success due to his “mentality”.

Emery said: “We’ll face Youri Tielemans — and he knows us, of course.

“He’s a fantastic player but when he was here, he needed time to adapt to us.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“After that, he performed well for Villa. Now, at Manchester United, he will maybe need some time to adapt.

“But if he plays against us, he will fight with his qualities and mentality. He has a very strong mentality.”

Tielemans has had several United midfield partners already.

He partnered Andrey Santos on the opening weekend of the Premier League and United were bullied in a 2-0 loss at promoted Hull.

He was then paired with Kobbie Mainoo and it did not work.



Tielemans also replaced Bruno Fernandes as the No 10 amid the United captain’s poor run of form before Tielemans got benched for the games against Chelsea and Roma.

He could be reunited with Mainoo today against Villa, the club he helped qualify for the Champions League twice and scored in their Europa League final triumph over Freiburg in May.

That would ordinarily assure Tielemans of applause from the away end.

But, although he did apologise for calling United a bigger club in those pre-season comments, he may get a mixed reception.

Tielemans was better off the bench in Tuesday’s 3-2 Champions League comeback win over Roma, which ended United’s nine-game winless run.



Boss Carrick has indicated that the past few weeks have taken their toll on players whatever age they are.

Tielemans turns 30 next May and is an experienced campaigner, having made his Anderlecht debut aged 16 and played in three World Cups. This is his ninth season in England.

Yet none of that can prepare players for the intense spotlight and scrutiny that comes with troubled times at United — as Tielemans and his team-mates have found this season.



Asked about how his squad have coped, Carrick said: “As an elite athlete, you know we’re always striving for close to perfection.

“You never get perfection but you always want to be getting to that limit really and playing right on the edge.

“With that, I’d say a huge chunk of that is your mindset, your mentality, your confidence.

“So it is about coping with that, that’s a major part of it.

“But it is something that we have to all take into account. Speaking to the players, from my perspective, of understanding where they’re at with it — for sure, it’s important.



“That feeling, momentum in sport, is massive. Momentum within games, momentum day-to-day, week-to-week, game-to-game, it’s huge.

“Sometimes it’s difficult to quantify where that is but with your feelings and emotions, it’s important.

“Then your memory can click in and you realise, ‘Oh yeah, this is what it feels like, this is how it should be’.

“That’s just a form of why players or teams have good spells then struggle in other spells. It’s all got to come together.
