“But feeling, confidence, and that emotion — sometimes not even thinking you’re at your best, you just trust and play on instinct.



“And I think we did a lot of that the other night against Roma.”

Sports.title: Regis Le Bris admits Granit Xhaka may be battling a hangover after Xabi Alonso and Chelsea’s failed transfer bid
Sports.content:
Next

REGIS LE BRIS concedes Granit Xhaka may be battling a hangover after Xabi Alonso’s failed bid to lure him to Chelsea.

But Sunderland’s boss insists his Swiss Superman’s warrior spirit remains intact.



Xhaka, 34, was top of Alonso’s Stamford Bridge wishlist following the Spaniard’s arrival in West London this summer.

The Blues chief was desperate for a sensational reunion with the talismanic playmaker who inspired his unbeaten Bayer Leverkusen side to the Bundesliga crown.



Yet the Black Cats dug in their heels and blocked the move, keeping the 34-year-old on Wearside.

The form of Xhaka, who later reiterated his commitment to Sunderland, has nose-dived since that saga with the midfield maestro looking a shadow of his former self.

Alonso instead swooped for Jordan Henderson, a Mackem who came through the ranks at his hometown club before a big-money move to Liverpool in 2011.

With Sunderland sitting bottom of the league, few would begrudge Xhaka looking across the pitch against top-four chasing Chelsea’s Henderson with envious eyes this afternoon.

Asked whether the transfer drama has affected Xhaka and potentially fractured the dressing-room harmony, head coach Le Bris admitted: “[It’s] hard to say. It’s always complex. It’s one element in the equation, so I don’t know, to be fair.”

Opposite number Alonso declined to discuss his pursuit of Xhaka. But the Blues manager acknowledged the key role the midfielder had played in Leverkusen’s success.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Alonso said: “We spoke a lot in that time in Leverkusen with Granit because he was a key part of that team.

“He glued many, many pieces together in the middle with the back three. Mostly with the players around him. It was a very good time together and I’m looking forward to seeing him on Sunday.”

Xhaka struggled previously in tough times as Arsenal skipper, having a run in with fans before being stripped of the armband.

However, he was rehabilitated under Mikel Arteta but Le Bris says he has not needed to perform any such act himself.

He said: “What I know is what I see every day, the involvement of Granit, his standards, training standards, his willingness to play for Sunderland.



“Thursday, we planned to play 60 minutes, but at half-time he told me, ‘I’ll go all the way. I will help the squad.’ This is Granit.

“So after that, he is human, he will have ups and downs. You are not the same player when you are 34 that you were at 23. His game is evolving as well, but his commitment is superb, no doubt about that.”

Meanwhile, Xhaka’s Sunderland team-mate Trai Hume is adamant their current slump has nothing to do with Xhaka’s flirt with Chelsea.



The Northern Ireland defender said: “No, it’s had no effect on us as players. Granit has obviously been a big player for the club since he’s come. He’s our captain, our leader, and just like us, he knows he can be better and we know we can be.

“He demands more from us. We need to step up to the levels we know we can hit but haven’t reached this season. We know as players we are a good team and we have to reach the levels of the Premier League.

“Unfortunately we haven’t reached that so far but that’s what we need to address and improve.”



Xhaka was a statement signing in the summer of 2025 after Le Bris had led Sunderland to promotion. Eyebrows were raised when the Black Cats managed to snap him up for £17m and he proved to be worth every pound of that by leading them to Europa League qualification last term.

However, it could quite easily have been Henderson lining up in red and white this afternoon instead.

The England international was desperate to return to the Premier League following miserable spells in Saudi Arabia and at Ajax.

Despite denials at the time, Le Bris has now admitted that owner Kyril Louis-Dreyfus and director of football Florent Ghisolfi did hold talks with Henderson over an emotional homecoming.

Though he is delighted with how things turned out after they opted for Xhaka instead while Henderson went on to join Brentford before moving to Stamford Bridge this summer.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

He said: “Absolutely! Granit is superb as well. Jordan is a great player, first of all. For the connection with the club, it’s not my part. It was with Flo and Kyril, they had conversations.

“I thought that it could have been a good signing for the club, a good symbol, a great player, a great leader. But the market is a market.”

Sports.title: Robbie Savage’s son Charlie scores as Peterborough capitulate in father vs son FA Cup clash
Sports.content:
Next

ROBBIE SAVAGE’S son Charlie delivered a brutal blow to his dad in a sensational first round 5-0 FA Cup tie.

Reading led 3-0 at half-time in the box office clash, leaving an exasperated Peterborough boss Robbie in the dugout.



But nothing could hurt more than the former Forest Green boss‘ own son putting the nail in the coffin after netting the third goal.

Charlie was all grins after receiving the ball inside the box, taking it for a quick walk before bouncing it in at the far post.



Daniel Kyerewaa had already put the frighteners on the Posh with a 26th-minute goal before Jack Marriott doubled their lead 12 minutes later.

And Charlie then delivered the goal that was written in the script in the dying moments of the first-half.

Real salt was rubbed into Robbie’s wounds with Jamie Reid scoring twice to round the a 5-0 thrashing.

Before the game, Robbie waited in the blue corridors of The Weston Homes Stadium to welcome his son into the den.

With ‘Proud to be posh’ emblazoned on the wall, the proud dad held out both arms but his smile was even wider.

When he saw Charlie, Robbie grinned: “Good luck, kid.”



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

While still making time for a hug, the 23-year-old smirked: “I can’t speak to you.”

But the pair have not been speaking all week, Robbie revealed.

As the League One boss plotted the downfall of Reading, both Charlie and Robbie decided that it would be unfair to both sides that they chat away about tactics or anything else.

Speaking to SunSport, Savage Snr said: “Because we’re trying to beat Reading, who’re flying in the league.

“I’ve not been able to speak to him all week. After his last match, as a dad, I’ve not been able to say to him: ‘How did you do?’

Sports.title: Tenerife to support tragic Jesus de Miguel’s daughter until she turns 18 after striker’s death colliding with opponent
Sports.content:
Next

TENERIFE have pledged to financially support Jesus de Miguel’s one-year-old daughter until she turns 18.

De Miguel tragically died on Tuesday morning following an accidental collision during a match against Andorra the previous evening.



Tenerife CEO Antonio Manuel Porro Granados has revealed that the club are determined to support De Miguel’s family – and his baby daughter Carla in particular.

Porro Granados told The Athletic: “Our plan is to stand by the girl and make sure the entire Tenerife family supports her. We want to be there for her at least until she reaches adulthood.



“This is a commitment we have made at the initiative of our majority shareholder, Rayco Garcia, and one that we all fully support.

“It is a commitment that Tenerife, as a club, is making to the family and to their daughter, Carla.



“We will provide the maximum possible support in every respect, beyond what we are legally obliged to provide.

“We are also exploring other ways of increasing the financial support, so that, at least in material terms, the circumstances do not affect their lives quite so much — although, of course, it is impossible for them not to have an impact.”

The late striker’s passing has sent Spanish football in mourning, with several tributes paid across matches this weekend.

Players across LaLiga – including the likes of Kylian Mbappe and Jude Bellingham – have worn T-shirts with De Miguel’s No9 on the back, as well as the message “Siempre en nuestro recuerdo” – meaning “Always in our memory” in English.



Matches have also included periods of silence, as well as minutes of applause.

Television broadcasts have featured a QR code linking to a GoFundMe page supporting De Miguel’s family.

Tenerife’s scheduled match this weekend was understandably postponed as the club comes to terms with its tragic loss.



The LaLiga 2 club did open its doors to fans to pay their respects on Saturday, however, with many flooding in.

Flowers and scarves were left at the stadium, while a large photo of De Miguel was draped over a stand, with the message “Eterno Demi 9 1996-2026”.

A replica De Miguel shirt was also placed on the pitch alongside a bouquet of flowers.

A post-mortem revealed that De Miguel had died following an “accidental chest trauma”, having collided with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during the closing stages of Monday’s match.

Owono was sent off for the challenge, before the game was ultimately abandoned.



The Andorra goalkeeper, 25, was left devastated by what happened.



He released an emotional statement on Thursday, which read: “These are being the most difficult days of my life.

“I am struggling to find the words, and it is very hard for me to process anything that has happened.

“I feel immense pain over the loss of Jesus. I am thinking of him, his family, and all the people who loved him.

“I know there will be many matters to address, and I will face whatever comes with complete respect.

“But right now, honestly, I cannot think of anything other than Jesus and the grief we are experiencing.



“Rest in peace, Jesus.”

The Spanish Footballers’ Association (AFE) has pledged to support Owono through counselling.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Athletic report that a source close to a team-mate of the goalkeeper said: “Owono is destroyed, locked in his house and disconnected from the world.

“Right now, he doesn’t even know who he is.”

Sports.title: Tottenham ‘to submit formal complaint over Jayden Bogle red card decision’ that forced Mathys Tel off injured
Sports.content:

TOTTENHAM are set to lodge a formal complaint after Leeds’ Jayden Bogle was NOT sent for an early shower.

The 26-year-old defender escaped unpunished after colliding with Mathys Tel, catching the forward’s ankle with his studs.



Spurs reportedly view the first-half clip as cause for a red card and will be writing to the refereeing body Pro Ref to seek a proper explanation.

In the 79th minute, Noah Okafor put the Yorkshire outfit ahead to move into eighth, while the North Londoners slipped to tenth.



Spurs went without a goal for the fifth league game this season, having also waited until their fifth game for a Prem goal.

VAR reviewed the clash at the time, but referee John Brooks was not sent to the pitch-side monitor, leaving Bogle unscathed.



Ex-Premier League assistant referee Darren Cann noted that the Leeds star was both “lucky” and “fortunate” to still be on the pitch.

He said: “Bogle’s challenge meets the criteria for serious foul play as he endangers the safety of an opponent.”

When play resumed there was just nine minutes remaining of the first-half.

And the messy pause caused Roberto De Zerbi & Co to lose their rhythm and composure to recover a comeback.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Post-match, the Spurs boss refused to pinpoint the defeat on Brooks and VAR.

Speaking to TNT Sports, he said: “I have big confidence in the referee. Nothing changes if he goes to the monitor.

“If they didn’t take the right decision I don’t know.

“We have to keep the eyes on the performance where can improve.



“We deserved to lose the game in the second half and didn’t play like we can.

Spurs will host 14th-place Ipswich first after the international break as they continue to climb up the table – slowly but surely.

Sports.title: Brits would happily sacrifice World Cup and Euros to get rid of dreaded international breaks, study finds
Sports.content:
RED CARD Brits would happily sacrifice World Cup and Euros to get rid of dreaded international breaks, study finds







Next

BRIT footie fans would happily sacrifice World Cups and European Championships to get rid of the dreaded international breaks, a study finds.

With another pause in Premier League football arriving next week, 37% would ditch seeing their national teams play on the world stage to keep the domestic game running.



Four in 10 (40%) are lost and irritable during the international break, 25% feel something is missing from their lives and 21% dread the empty fixture list.

A quarter (25%) watch other sports to fight the boredom, while 19% reluctantly spend time with their partner and 17% clean the house.



More than half (59%) would pick their club over country in the age-old debate, according to a poll of 2,000 British football fans commissioned by Snickers.

And it appears club football fans would go to extreme lengths in order for their team to win the Premier League.

More than one in five (22%) would do the washing up every day for a year, 19% would give up takeaways, 16% would hand over control of the TV remote to their other half and 12% would shave their heads completely bald.

Running a marathon (11%), sacrificing a summer holiday (10%) and letting friends choose an embarrassing tattoo (7%) would also be on the agenda if it guaranteed their team lifting the top-flight trophy.



Snickers has launched its International Breakvent Calendar, featuring 13 windows to help fans count down the days until the return of club football, teaming up with former Burnley, Everton and Nottingham Forest manager Sean Dyche, who takes on the role of the brand’s gaffer.

Dyche said: “There’s nothing quite like the build-up to matchday, the routine, the anticipation and that feeling when your team finally takes to the pitch.

Top things British football fans would do to guarantee their team wins the Premier League, according to a poll from Snickers 1. Do the washing-up every day for a year – 22%

2. Give up social media for a couple of months – 19%

Sports.title: Bleak Man City reality hits home as Liam Delap fires Nottingham Forest to statement win
Sports.content:
Bleak Man City reality hits home as Liam Delap fires Nottingham Forest to statement win

NOTTINGHAM FOREST 3-1 MANCHESTER CITY: Liam Delap scored two wondergoals to give Oliver Glasner's side a morale-boosting victory over their downbeat visitors

View 3 Images Liam Delap scored twice to sink Manchester City at the City Ground

He gave it the full Cristiano Ronaldo celebration. And had every right to. No-one is ever going to confuse Liam Delap with the five-times Ballon d’Or winner but this was something special.

‌



‌



With around a quarter of the contest remaining, Nottingham Forest’s chances of holding on to a one-goal lead seemed slim to none. And slim was packing his bags. But Delap, a product of City, then started and finished a counter-attack with the bravado of a world-beater.

‌



It was some moment. Left foot, bullet-quick, arrow-straight, postage-stamp territory, City Ground in glorious uproar as the mist really did roll in.

‌



Delap’s sensational hit - his second of the match - gave Forest a thoroughly deserved win but this was another uninspiring City performance. Three Premier League defeats on the spin suggest a side waiting for their fate to be decided elsewhere.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources .

‌



The initial reaction of the players to the independent commission’s guilty verdicts appeared to be one of defiance. It is hard not to think that defiance has dissipated somewhat.

Ex-professionals and pundits queue up to tell us the spectre of extreme sanctions will not affect the mentality of the squad but this is unprecedented. No-one really knows how it will impact their psyche. This is a group of footballers who strongly suspect whatever they produce on the pitch is likely to be rendered irrelevant by heavy punishment should the club’s appeal be unsuccessful. How can that not have the slightest impact?

‌



Whether it is a factor or not, one thing was for sure based on much of the evidence from this match. City’s aggression has disappeared, City’s snap has gone, City’s desire has diminished.

They lost every even contest in the early stages. They were outmuscled. They showed no great appetite for a fight. First things first. Forest were outstanding in those early stages. Yes, Josko Gvardiol was culpable ahead of the opening goal but the determination and drive of scorer Jair Cunha was magnificent. And yes, another unacceptable surrender of possession preceded Forest’s second but Delap’s buccaneering run and finish was something to behold.

‌



View 3 Images Manchester City were beaten again by Nottingham Forest (Image: Gareth Copley)

Oliver Glasner’s game-plan was brutally effective in its simplicity. Every time a City player had the ball in the opposition half, he was confronted by a ferociously committed Forest man.

‌



They did not give the talented trio of Jeremy Doku, Rayan Cherki and Iliman Ndiaye a moment’s peace. And upfront, Delap comprehensively unsettled Marc Guehi and Ruben Dias.

Guehi’s form for City has been alarmingly poor - it was no shock he was hooked at half-time - and, of course, it does not help that Gianluigi Donnarumma is in one of those spells that is particularly unfortunate for a goalkeeper. Any decently-struck shot that comes his way goes past him. Not ideal.

‌



They were very good hits from Cunha and Delap but Donnarumma’s efforts to keep them out looked to be little more than token.

View 3 Images Delap fires home his first goal against Manchester City (Image: Alfie Cosgrove/NurPhoto)

‌



Inevitably, City improved but Forest were relatively untroubled throughout the first half and Enzo Maresca inevitably made a couple of changes at the interval.

To begin with, they had minimal effect, though. Sloppiness ran through City’s ranks. They needed a moment of inspiration, an instance of genius. And it came from the left boot of Cherki, fizzing the sweetest of shots into the top corner. He does not deal in the mundane, Rayan.

‌



With well over half an hour left on the clock, a full City comeback looked inevitable. But this was an evening when Forest dug fantastically deep, the example being set by captain Ryan Yates.

His work-rate set the standard but no-one was taking the man of the match honours away from Delap and Glasner afforded him the great ovation he deserved by substituting him late in proceedings.

Article continues below

It was just the performance Delap needed. For City, it was the performance of a team that knows the most costly defeats are likely to come off the pitch.

Sports.content:
Non-league clash postponed as ex-Forest starlet rushed to hospital in warm-up

Truro City's National League South clash at Folkestone Invicta was postponed when City player Yassine En-Neyah suffered a medical emergency in the warm-up

View 3 Images The ambulance drove on to the pitch to take En-Neyah to hospital (Image: Tom Sandberg/PPAUK)

Truro City's trip to Folkestone Invicta was postponed due to a medical emergency for one of the visiting players.

‌



‌



City star Yassine En-Neyah, a Nottingham Forest youth product, was rushed to hospital in an ambulance after the episode prior to the National League South clash.

‌



The 26-year-old is said to have collapsed on the pitch before the ambulance drove on to the playing surface in order to take him to hospital.

‌



Both sides released a short statement confirming the postponement, before a further post from Truro confirmed En-Neyah was the player involved and that he was receiving further treatment.

"Yassine En-Neyah required medical assistance during the warm-up and was transferred to the William Harvey hospital in Ashford for further treatment. We will provide a further update in due course.”

Sports.title: Leeds beat Spurs to leave Roberto De Zerbi fuming at red card controversy
Sports.content:
Leeds beat Spurs to leave Roberto De Zerbi fuming at red card controversy

LEEDS 1-0 TOTTENHAM: Jayden Bogle was lucky to stay on the pitch as VAR decided his reckless challenge on Mathys Tel was not worth of a red card

View 2 Images Noah Okafor scored the winner for Leeds against Spurs (Image: Annabel Lee-Ellis/Press Association)

Roberto De Zerbi was left seeing red after Jayden Bogle escaped a card of the same colour in this crushing defeat for Tottenham at Elland Road.

‌



‌



De Zerbi stormed down the tunnel at half time, having seen VAR refuse to deem Bogle's dangerous tackle on Mathys Tel worthy of a sending off.

‌



The challenge, which saw Bogle stand on the Achilles of the Spurs winger and force him to limp out of the game, didn't even result in the Leeds defender getting booked.

‌



And De Zerbi's mood went from bad to worse when substitute Noah Okafor won the game for Leeds in the final 10 minutes, just 97 seconds after going on.

Spurs had arrived in Yorkshire high on confidence following three straight wins. The run had even lifted a team which made a shambolic start to this campaign, into the top half of the table.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

And in the process overtaking a Leeds side which had started to struggle, following a bright opening. Daniel Farke's men took on Spurs without a win in their last five league outings.

‌



But the German also knew his side had the longest unbeaten home run in the Premier League. One spanning 23 games and stretching back to March.

And Spurs were fortunate not to find themselves behind inside the opening five minutes. Mateus Fernandes did his best to handle a cross and concede a penalty, before VAR bailed him out, while Ao Tanaka blazed a shot just wide.

‌



Ethan Ampadu then sliced an effort well wide as Spurs continued to hang on. Having weathered the storm, Spurs threatened themselves when a lightening break from Tel down the left resulted in Omar Marmoush shooting straight at James Trafford.

Moments later Mohammed Kudus tested Trafford again, but these were rare moments of quality in a game badly lacking the stuff.

‌



Ten minutes before half time VAR took four minutes to review that challenge by Bogle on Tel. De Zerbi couldn't believe the outcome of the dithering.

Bogle then set up a chance for Lukas Nmecha, who headed straight at Antonin Kinsky from close range. A comical collision between team-mates Ampadu and Tarik Muharemovic kind of summed up the first half.

‌



View 2 Images Tel had to be replaced after the challenge by Bogle (Image: Annabel Lee-Ellis/Press Association)

Things could only get better. And they did. Ampadu had a shot blocked, while Micky van de Ven almost sliced an interception into his own goal.

‌



Dominic Solanke blocked a header from Dominic Calvert-Lewin close to his own line as Leeds continued to push for a breakthrough. Tempers continued to simmer, and De Zerbi was booked after objecting to a yellow card shown to Pedro Porro.

A break from Calvert-Lewin saw him tee-up Tanaka, who ballooned his effort over the crossbar when he should have scored.

‌



Ampadu then had an effort deflected wide, while substitute Conor Gallagher was a whisker from snatching a winner for Spurs at the opposite end.

But with 10 minutes remaining Okafor burst into the box to beat Kinsky and bring Spurs' recent momentum to a shuddering halt.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick laughs off Man Utd claim as Antonio Conte opinion emerges
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick laughs off Man Utd claim as Antonio Conte opinion emerges

Antonio Conte is one of the managers linked with the Manchester United job

View 2 Images Michael Carrick has been under pressure at Manchester United (Image: OLI SCARFF, AFP via Getty Images)

Michael Carrick has laughed off Sir Alex Ferguson comparisons as Manchester United have been told not to appoint Antonio Conte. The Italian is one of the names linked with the Old Trafford hot seat amid pressure on Carrick following a poor run of form.

‌



‌



Carrick was appointed on a permanent basis in the summer, but the side are currently on a run of seven league games without a win and sit in 17th place in the Premier League table. They are only out of the relegation zone on goal difference.

‌



Former Chelsea and Tottenham manager Conte is keen on the United job, having left Napoli in the summer.

‌



JJ Gabriel breaks silence on Man Utd exit with eight-word explanation for Real Madrid move READ MORE :

Unai Emery sends Jamie Carragher firm message over Aston Villa plans after legal threat READ MORE :

The pressure on Carrick eased somewhat following the midweek fightback against AS Roma in the Champions League. United recovered from 2-0 down to secure a 3-2 victory.

The result has prompted comparisons to the triumph over Nottingham Forest in the FA Cup third round in January 1990, which ultimately saved Sir Alex Ferguson's position. However, Carrick dismissed suggestions that history could be repeating itself.

"It's up to us to take it forward," he said. "As a one-off night, it was a fantastic night. I thought we played really, really well and deserved the game. It was nice to end like that. It was nice for the supporters to end like that and to have that feeling.

‌



"Nothing's done yet. Nothing's achieved yet, and it's one moment in time that we need to use to move forward. But we need more of it, for sure."

View 2 Images Antonio Conte has been linked with the Man United job (Image: Francesco Pecoraro, Getty Images)

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

He is, though, not ruling out the prospect of replicating the achievements Ferguson enjoyed at Old Trafford after that victory. "It's not impossible," he added. "Anything's possible.

‌



"You've got to build, you've got to be realistic. You've got to put things in perspective as well. The recent history that we've had and what we're trying to get to, it's not going to happen overnight.

"Success does take time, and we don't like having to spend time, but it does take a period of time to build. There are no shortcuts to it. In the end, that's where you get to, but it's definitely possible."

‌



Amid the pressure on Carrick and the talk around Conte, former Premier League defender Gallas has issued a caution to United regarding a possible appointment. He instead believes attention should be on implementing alterations elsewhere at the club.

Speaking to SeatPick, he said: "I don't know if Antonio Conte can fix Manchester United because from what I understand now the players in that dressing room are completely different from the players 10, 15 or 20 years ago.

‌



"If you bring in Antonio Conte, you know he has a big personality. You know he will ask his players to adapt to his system, but I don't know if the players at Manchester United can do this.

"It's a different generation. Now you have to adapt to the players at this club, not just the players adapting to you. It has to be a compromise. Before, it used to be that the players had to adapt to the manager. Nobody said anything. They had great results. Now life has changed."

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"A manager like Conte would have to understand that 'OK I have to adapt to this new generation, and if I do that, at the same time, I will need them to adapt to what I want from them,' and that's why you have to be sure about what you are going into. Manchester United also have to be sure about the manager they are bringing in because the message has to make sense and be understood by the players in the dressing room. Otherwise it will be the same problem again and again.

‌



"Ultimately, the problem with United is the players that they've brought to the club because they aren't at the level to play for Manchester United. With all the respect I have for other clubs, Manchester United are not Coventry City. They are not Crystal Palace. We are talking about Manchester United.

"They should only be signing the best players to play for the club but time and time again they have made big mistakes. Antonio Conte cannot change that. No manager can. You have to look higher up at the club first."

Article continues below

United are back in Premier League action on Sunday when they host Aston Villa at Old Trafford. Villa manager Unai Emery is another name said to be interesting United, but the midlands club won't let their boss go without a fight.

Sports.title: Pelé prayed with the Pope, had lunch with the Queen and sang with Frank Sinatra
Sports.content:
Pelé prayed with the Pope, had lunch with the Queen and sang with Frank Sinatra

In a fascinating new book about football legend Pelé, British author Andrew Downie details the three-time World Cup winner's glittering career — and escapades off the pitch

Andrew Downie discusses his latest book about the legendary Brazilian footballer Pele entitled ‘Epic’

An extraordinary new book has been written on the world’s most famous footballer — Pelé.

‌



‌



It has taken British author Andrew Downie eight years and 250 interviews to write the "warts and all" book on the Brazilian legend.

‌



He said simply: “Pelé prayed with the Pope, had lunch with the Queen, dinner with Andy Warhol and sang with Frank Sinatra.” He’s uncovered a wealth of new information on Pelé — who died in 2022 and reveals all in his new book called Epic.

‌



Andrew has discovered secret acts of great kindness carried out by the three times World Cup winner. And he has uncovered some never told stories from family and friends which show his great love of the game.

The 50 hardest Manchester United players to ever walk out at Old Trafford READ MORE :

View 6 Images Andrew Downie who took eight years to compile the book on Pelé (Image: Philip Coburn)

Andrew said: “For example when he played for New York Cosmos he would just wander through Central Park. He’d find a group of children kicking a football around and he’d just join in. “The most famous footballer in the world playing a game in the park — but he loved it.” And Andrew, 59, from Granton, Edinburgh, has found many people who Pelé helped. He said: “He really was so generous and he did it all under the radar.

‌



“He helped so many people — family, friends and charities and he did the vast majority of it without anyone finding out. He didn’t seek publicity and he didn’t want publicity .

“He kept many members of his financially afloat — thanks to his unfailing generosity. And I found out about the secret financial deals with FIFA boss João Havelange It’s fascinating.”

‌



View 6 Images Dedicated author Andrew Downie with football legend Pele

Andrew, who is a huge fan of Scottish side Hibs, now lives in the Spanish capital Madrid. He said: “Pelé was a national touchstone, an avatar for the successful, forward-looking country that Brazil wanted to be.

‌



“He was its Atatürk, Churchill, or Mandela, and he enjoyed the same reverence. Every one who knew him was sharply protective. “They called him ‘O Rei’, or ‘The King’, and they knew that contradicting the man who made Brazil was akin to treason. I did more than 250 interviews for the book, and just about every single person I spoke to professed to love him.”

View 6 Images Pele in the iconic Brazil shirt (Image: Getty Images)

‌



He explained why he felt compelled to write the book: “I was convinced that many of the tales told by Pelé and his friends had been heavily edited, if not completely made up.

“I’d seen and heard competing versions of hundreds of oft told stories, and I wanted to discover the truth and the details behind them. Pelé produced four autobiographies over a 53 year period and all four of his ghostwriters faced the same problem.

‌



“There were juicy stories to tell but few people willing to tell them. Pelé kept his private life hidden and no one close to him wanted top betray the King’s confidence.” Some of the many stories in the book centre on Pelé’s games for Santos against English teams.

View 6 Images Pele after 1970 World Cup final triumph (Image: Getty Images)

‌



He played against Chelsea in Jamaica in 1971 and against Newcastle in Hong Kong a year later. And in England he famously he faced Plymouth Argyle, Sheffield Wednesday, Stoke City, Aston Villa and Fulham.

In recent years there has been much debate about who was the best football player ever. Pelé, Diego Maradona, Lionel Messi or Cristiano Ronaldo. But Andrew has no doubt who is the Greatest of All Time.

‌



View 6 Images Andrew Downie's book: Epic (Image: Philip Coburn)

He said: “When I started writing about Pelé the plan was not to produce a manifesto declaring him the GOAT. “But seven years into the biggest project of my writing life, this could easily be considered a case for the defence, a document to be presented whenever Pelé’s feats are belittled.

‌



“The opening argument is that Pelé was the pinnacle because he was so far ahead of the ­game — the only man to win three World Cups and to score 1,000 goals, and the first to become football’s global superstar.

“The legends who succeeded him built their careers standing on the shoulders of a giant. As Michael Jordan once said, ‘I have used all the great players who came before me to improve upon my game. Evolution knows no bounds.” And he said the former Pope Francis knew who was best.

‌



View 6 Images Pele playing for Santos against Plymouth Argyle in 1973 (Image: WestwardTV)

He said: “In November 2023, two days after Messi won his eighth Ballon d’Or, an Italian reporter approached the pontiff for his thoughts. ‘Who do you prefer,’ he asked, ‘Messi or Maradona?’

‌



“The Pope’s reply surprised everyone. ‘I would add a third,’ he said. ‘Pelé. Maradona was great but he failed as a man. Messi is a gentleman, always correct. But for me, of those three, the real man was Pelé, a man of great humanity.”

Pelé died at the age of 82 on December 29, 2022 at the Albert Einstein Israelite Hospital in São Paulo. The cause of death was multiple organ failure.

‌



His final resting place was the Memorial Necropole Ecumenica in Santos which overlooks the city’s football stadium where he played so many times in his career.. Pelé was married three times throughout his life. He had seven children.

Approximately 230,000 fans, citizens, and mourners filed past his open casket during the 24-hour wake at the Urbano Caldeira stadium (Vila Belmiro) in Santos. He was born in 1940 christened Edson Arantes do Nascimento.

Article continues below

He began playing for Santos at the age of 15 and for the Brazil national team at 16. During his international career, he won three World Cup titles three in 1958, 1962 and 1970 – becoming the only player to do so and the youngest to win a World Cup, at just 17 years old.

Sports.title: Premier League star breaks his silence after bow and arrow incident and police operation
Sports.content:
Premier League star breaks his silence after bow and arrow incident and police operation

A Premier League player subject to a police operation this week over a very strange incident involving a bow and arrow has now broken his silence on social media

View 2 Images Amar Dedic was questioned by Northumbria Police (Image: Serena Taylor, Newcastle United via Getty Images)

Newcastle United player Amar Dedic has compared himself to the Lord of the Rings character Legolas after being quizzed by Northumbria Police for carrying a bow and arrows in public. Officers confiscated the weapon on Wednesday after pulling over a vehicle seven-and-a-half miles northwest of Newcastle upon Tyne in Darras Hall, one of the North East's most exclusive areas.

‌



‌



Two men - one of whom was Dedic, the other being his friend - were reported to the force after being seen near a reservoir in Northumberland with the weapon. Six police vehicles, including armed units, were deployed in response, and the footballer was interviewed after being located in the civil parish of Ponteland.

‌



Newcastle were reportedly not pursuing any disciplinary measures against their player in response. A spokesperson for Northumbria Police said on Wednesday that "enquiries are ongoing".

‌



Another Premier League star robbed DURING match as partner shares 'distressing' statement READ MORE :

Premier League star sparks huge police operation after being spotted with BOW AND ARROW READ MORE :

"Shortly after 1.55pm on Wednesday, we received a report of two men carrying a bow and arrows while walking along a track by the reservoir on Military Road in the Harlow Hill area.

"Officers attended and subsequently stopped a vehicle in the Darras Hall area and seized a bow and arrows. At this stage, it is understood they were for recreational use, and there was no threat to the public."

Dedic has since responded in the comments section of a Newcastle Instagram post, in which the club celebrated his latest call-up for Bosnia and Herzegovina. The club's post reads: "Amar Dedic has been named in the Bosnia and Herzegovina squad for their games against Sweden and Romania over the international break. Congrats, @amar_dc!"

‌



View 2 Images Amar Dedic commented on Newcastle United's Instagram post

Responding to the post, Dedic shared a GIF of Legolas, an elf portrayed by Orlando Bloom in The Lord of the Rings film trilogy. The footage depicts the fictional archer with a quiver of arrows slung across their shoulder.

‌



The defender's response has garnered over 20,000 likes and more than 300 replies at the time of reporting. Predictably, many included bow-and-arrow emojis after reports of the incident spread rapidly across social media this week.

Numerous other responses beneath the post are dubbing Dedic the "Bosnian Robin Hood", with one saying the "Sheriff of Nottingham will be relieved". Parallels have also been drawn with Marvel superhero Hawkeye, who wields a bow and arrow.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Dedic has made 10 appearances for Newcastle since arriving from Benfica during the summer transfer window for approximately £30million. The defender penned a five-year deal and had previously collaborated with head coach Matthias Jaissle at Liefering and Red Bull Salzburg in Austria.

‌



At international level, he has earned 31 caps for Bosnia. The full-back featured in three of their four fixtures at this summer's World Cup.

However, he has not played for them since then after re-aggravating a hamstring injury before this season's first international break. Bosnia went unbeaten through their first four Nations League games and are second in League B, Group 4.

Sports.title: JJ Gabriel breaks silence on Man Utd exit with eight-word explanation for Real Madrid move
Sports.content:
JJ Gabriel breaks silence on Man Utd exit with eight-word explanation for Real Madrid move

JJ Gabriel gave a brief interview to a Spanish newspaper in Madrid as his protracted and bitter move from Manchester United to Real Madrid edges closer to completion

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel is in Madrid waiting for his move to be officially completed (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

JJ Gabriel has given an indication of why he has taken such extreme measures to trade Manchester United for Real Madrid at the age of 16.

‌



‌



Gabriel is poised to join Real after going AWOL from United in September in an attempt to force through a move, having grown frustrated at the pace of his elevation to the first team. The teenager has enlisted the help of super agent Ali Barat to make his dream of a move to the Bernabeu come true.

‌



He attracted attention from Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain before settling on Jose Mourinho's Real as his choice. Despite remaining under registration with United, who he joined in 2022, Gabriel has cut all ties with the club.

‌



United are therefore considering legal action against Real in order to extract compensation beyond the fee of between £100,000 to £300,000 that FIFA usually insists upon in these situations. The Red Devils are yet to be contacted by Real, who have reportedly offered Gabriel a three-year contract worth more than £850,000 (€1m) per season.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Having previously been training in Barcelona, Gabriel has switched to Madrid while the process remains ongoing and he spoke to Spanish newspaper Marca alongside his dad after a session with his personal trainer. After joking about choosing Real over rivals Barca, Gabriel said: “My dream is to win the Ballon d'Or."

Extracting him from United and negotiating a deal isn't the only barrier for Real Madrid. Gabriel will also have to go into the club's reserves, Castilla, because he can't play in the Youth League this season as he's under registration with United.

‌



Players under the age of 18 are usually not allowed to move so early, but Gabriel - who was born in England but has Irish and Cypriot heritage - has a European Union passport.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



View 2 Images JJ Gabriel starred for Manchester United's youth teams before jumping ship (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

Marca reports that Gabriel's move to Real might not be announced until January, when the club can officially register him in the transfer window. It means that, even when everything is agreed with Real, the saga will likely continue into 2027.

‌



Gabriel has been sent a warning by United legend Ryan Giggs, who has questioned his eagerness to leave the club. "So far in his career everything is going fine, why would you disrupt that? You’re on the right track," Giggs said on Rio Ferdinand’s YouTube channel.

"I trained at 15. I didn’t play for the first team until two years later, so you have to have that patience that people just don’t seem to have at the moment. And believe it or not, first-team football for Man United is completely different to playing in the youth team, playing pre-season for the first team, it’s completely different.

Article continues below

"That first game, yeah, you might do alright, but you have to do it for 40, 50 games a season. You’re going to get injuries, loss of form, bad results, so you have to be patient."

Sports.title: Can Verstappen, Hamilton come from the back in Sao Paulo 'reverse grid' race?
Sports.content:
A mixed up grid and rain on the forecast has set up the prospect of a thrilling Sao Paulo Grand Prix on Sunday.

For the third year in a row, Lando Norris will start on pole position in Brazil with new F1 world champion Kimi Antonelli alongside him on the front row.

Unusually though, there will be plenty of attention further down the field as power unit changes for Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton mean they start at the back, while Ferrari's Charles Leclerc starts 14th for a 10-grid place penalty.

And Mercedes' George Russell, who was left frustrated to not qualify first after a strategic error from the team, starts seventh following a five-place grid penalty for a new internal combustion engine, so several of F1's biggest names will begin the Sao Paulo Grand Prix - lights out at 5pm on Sunday with build-up from 3.30pm, live on Sky Sports F1 - out of position.

"It's almost a reverse grid race, no?" Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff told Sky Sports F1.

"Yeah, exciting. I think we want to lock in the points for the Constructors' Championship. But it's all floodgates open, the better. Let's race."

Sao Paulo GP: Top 10 Starting Grid 1) Lando Norris, McLaren



2) Kimi Antonelli,, Mercedes



3) Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls



4) Nico Hulkenberg, Audi



5) Isack Hadjar, Red Bull



6) Oliver Bearman, Haas



7) George Russell, Mercedes



8) Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin



9) Alex Albon, Williams



10) Oscar Piastri, McLaren

How far can Verstappen and Hamilton climb up the field?

Verstappen is no stranger to making his way through the pack at Interlagos after his remarkable victory from 17th in 2024 in the rain.

The Red Bull driver, who has won three times in Brazil, gained 11 places in the opening 11 laps before making the right strategy call to take a crucial victory.

Last year, Verstappen started from the pit lane and impressively charged his way to the podium in dry conditions, but he thinks it will be more difficult to get towards the front this time around.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the best overtakes from Max Verstappen's stellar performance at the 2025 Sao Paulo Grand Prix which took him all the way from the pit lane to the podium

"It's going to be a bit harder to overtake. The Overtake Mode doesn't really do a lot around here. Everyone is draining their battery from the last corner to Turn 1. Everyone has their wings open, so the effect is less than normal," he told Sky Sports F1.

"That will make it a bit harder to overtake once you get to the cars that are similar on lap times. The first few cars are not a problem. The others will be a little harder."

What is Overtake Mode in F1? Overtake Mode has been a replacement for DRS since the start of this year.



It’s a mode the car goes into when you are within one second of the car in front.



It allows the following car a higher car speed while still deploying maximum energy from the electric motor.



On a normal lap, when the car reaches 180mph, it has to, by regulation, ramp down its electric motor power. With Overtake Mode active, that speed tolerance raises to 209mph, so the following car is allowed to go faster.

Hamilton memorably went from 20th to fifth in the 2021 Sprint in Brazil, after he was disqualified from Qualifying, then won the Grand Prix after starting 10th.

However, Hamilton will not have the same car advantage from five years ago with Ferrari struggling this weekend compared to their recent form.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen reflected on a wet qualifying session in Sao Paulo

But, the high chance of rain means Hamilton, and Verstappen, will have the chance to showcase their extraordinary skill and could still find themselves towards the pointy end of the field with a special performance.

"It will be tricky conditions but I love racing in the rain," said Hamilton.

"I was basically using the qualifying as a test to make sure the engine is working, and making sure the car felt good. I feel good for tomorrow."

Leclerc has less cars to overtake from 14th and feels he learned a lot from the wet qualifying by experimenting with set-up tweaks which will benefit him in the race.

"It's going to be very tricky. My biggest strength in the junior categories has been wet driving. Since my nine years with Ferrari, we have never found a way around it," he told Sky Sports F1.

"I still believe if we manage to find the right window of this car, we can fight for much better than top six."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charles Leclerc says he's 'settled' feud with Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton after their clash in last week's Mexico City GP

Norris hoping for 'dark, gloomy day' to fight Antonelli

Perhaps quite fittingly, last year's F1 world champion Norris will start on pole from the new world champion Antonelli in the first race since the latter secured this year's title a week ago in Mexico.

McLaren have brought a new front wing, rear wing, beam wing and floor elements to their car this weekend and it appears to have made an immediate performance impact.

Norris and Antonelli traded lap times throughout Friday's practice sessions in the dry but the McLaren driver feels he needs rain to beat Antonelli on Sunday.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris reacted to claiming pole position for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix

"I expect a battle no matter what. If it's dry, I probably expect a bigger battle because I don't think we quite have the speed compared to them," he told Sky Sports F1.

"That's why I feel like we had a very good day today. We made the most of conditions where it's not so much about who has the best car, it's more who can push things to the limit and make the most of that opportunity.

"I'm hoping when I wake up it's a dark, gloomy day because we will have a better chance then."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Torrential rain brings out the red flag a minute after the Qualifying session begins in Sao Paulo

Norris pointed to Antonelli's impressive long run pace in the dry on Friday as the reason he's hoping for rain, whereas the Mercedes driver says he's open to any conditions.

"Hopefully, we can get off the line well, and let's see if it's going to be wet or dry," said Antonelli.

"In the dry, I felt very good over a single lap and on the long run, especially in FP2. So let's see. I'm looking forward to it.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell was seething after being told to back off at a time when he believed he could have pushed for P1 during the Q3 session in Sao Paulo

Mercedes have a big opportunity to win the Constructors' Championship with Antonelli starting in second and Russell in seventh, while the two Ferraris are outside of the top 13.

If Mercedes outscore Ferrari by three points, or more, they will seal their ninth title since 2014 but the result of the race itself appears to be more important to the drivers, and Russell is hoping for more rain following his impressive qualifying.

"I felt really confident in the rain. I think my pace, along with Lando's, was by far the best out there," he said

"In the rain here, it's always a challenge. I hope it is wet. I feel I've got a greater chance if it's wet."

Sports.title: Norris claims Sao Paulo GP pole after treacherous rain-hit qualifying
Sports.content:
Lando Norris claimed pole position after a hugely-challenging Sao Paulo Grand Prix qualifying in treacherous wet conditions, for a race that will see Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen start at the back of the grid.

On a rain-hit day at ever-unpredictable Interlagos, qualifying was suspended for over an hour and 20 minutes after a torrential downpour hit the drivers' first laps of Q1.

The rain eventually eased - but never particularly stopped - to allow running to take place, creating a thrilling and unpredictable battle for pole.

In the end it was Norris who impressively came out on top to seal a third successive Interlagos pole position for the outgoing world champion, on a weekend McLaren had already showed improved form in the dry following car upgrades.

Mercedes' George Russell was second fastest ahead of a race he already knew he carries a five-place grid penalty for an engine change, meaning he could not ultimately achieve pole position whatever he did.

He lapped 0.204s slower than Norris in Q3 and from second will drop to seventh on Sunday's grid.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell was seething after being told to back off at a time when he believed he could have pushed for P1 during the Q3 session in Sao Paulo

But the Mercedes driver felt he would have topped the qualifying timesheet outright had he not been advised by his race engineer to back out of what turned out to be his final representative timed lap of Q3, when he came up behind Alex Albon's slower Williams.

Russell's engineer, Marcus Dudley, clearly hoped this would pay dividends by giving the Briton a clearer run on his next lap but the call coincided with the rain worsening, meaning lap times quickly became slower and the final minutes of Q3 inconsequential as all drivers returned to the pit lane.

"I don't want to be P2. I want to be P1!" fumed Russell on team radio.

New world champion Kimi Antonelli qualified third but will move ahead of team-mate Russell to the front row alongside Norris.

Sao Paulo GP Qualifying: Top 10 1) Lando Norris, McLaren



2) George Russell, Mercedes*



3) Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes



4) Charles Leclerc, Ferrari**



5) Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls



6) Nico Hulkenberg, Audi



7) Isack Hadjar, Red Bull



8) Oliver Bearman, Haas



9) Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin



10) Alex Albon, Williams



*five-place penalty to be applied



**10-place penalty to be applied

Charles Leclerc was fourth for Ferrari but he has a 10-place penalty for an engine change to serve so will drop down into 14th on the grid.

His team-mate Hamilton was also originally supposed to serve the same sanction but a problem with his fresh Ferrari engine in final practice triggered a complete power-unit change and locked him in to a back-of-the-grid start.

He will be joined on the back rows by old title rival Verstappen, who has also taken a new power unit in his Red Bull from Saturday's running. Hamilton starts 20th with Verstappen 21st.

Both drivers dropped out in Q2, Hamilton in 11th and Verstappen, who opted not to run in the second phase at all in order to save wet tyres for the race, 16th but neither result mattered given their overriding penalties.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen reflected on a wet qualifying session in Sao Paulo

Ferrari's heavier grid penalties increase Mercedes' chances of closing out the Constructors' Championship on Sunday.

Seven days after Antonelli's drivers' title triumph in Mexico, the Silver Arrows will complete a title double for 2026 with three rounds to spare if they outscore their Italian rivals by three points or more.

Front-running penalties promote midfield runners up grid

The grid penalties for Russell, Verstappen and both Ferraris - which were all confirmed in the sessions ahead of qualifying - mean Sunday's grid has a different complexion to normal in a season otherwise dominated by the 'big four' teams.

Russell and Leclerc's demotions move Liam Lawson - whose future at Racing Bulls remain in huge doubt despite his impressive season - to a joint career-best third on the grid after the New Zealander already impressed in the wet to qualify fifth.

Who has grid penalties at Interlagos? George Russell, Mercedes - 5 places

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari - 10 places

Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari - Back of grid

Max Verstappen, Red Bull - Back of grid

Sergio Perez, Cadillac - Back of grid

There were also strong performances in the rain from Audi's Nico Hulkenberg, who will start fourth, and Haas' Oliver Bearman, who will line up sixth.

With Verstappen at the back, Isack Hadjar will be the lead Red Bull driver in fifth.

Fernando Alonso showed his old mastery of the rain to put under-powered Aston Martin into Q3 for the first time this season, while Williams' Alex Albon also made his first top-10 appearance of a difficult year.

Alonso and Albon will line up in eighth and ninth places respectively.

That is just ahead of McLaren's Oscar Piastri - after he dropped out in Q2 following an error on the intermediates at the end of his last lap - and Brazilian debutant Rafael Camara in 11th.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rafael Camara ended his F1 debut in the barriers during Qualifying at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix

Camara, Haas' new signing to replace Esteban Ocon, hugely impressed on his F1 debut to make Q2 before blotting his copybook slightly by crashing into the barriers at the end of that second phase at Turn 12.

Arvid Lindblad will line up 12th after his Racing Bulls car was stopped by technical issues in Q2.

How Interlagos' unpredictable weather created thrilling qualifying

Rain has largely stayed away from the 2026 season but arrived with a vengeance at Interlagos on Saturday.

A big electrical storm following the end of final practice had already drenched the track, but conditions had started to improve, and the rain even briefly stopped, to allow qualifying to begin at its scheduled time.

But just as drivers were starting to queue at the end of the pit lane for the Q1 green light, the heavens opened again and as the cars were released onto the track conditions became treacherous almost immediately, forcing drivers to gingerly complete their out laps amid ever-worsening visibility and grip levels.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Torrential rain brings out the red flag a minute after the Qualifying session begins in Sao Paulo

Race Control swiftly threw the red flag, mandating drivers returned to the pit lane, which would eventually lead to a suspension of one hour and 23 minutes before the track was deemed suitable for F1 cars to return.

And while the rain did start to initially worsen again just as the session resumed, conditions steadily improved thereafter with a drier line eventually appearing around the lap and drivers able to switch from the full wet to the shallower intermediate tyres from mid-way through Q2.

Impressively, while there were spins and off-track moments, only two drivers found the barriers. However, to the disappointment of the home crowd, they were both the Brazilians in the field.

Gabriel Bortoleto slithered off the road in his Audi in Q1, although was able to return to the pits where he stayed due to car damage, while Camara hit the barriers to bring Q2 to a slightly premature end at the start of the final run up the hill.

In the end, despite a frustrated Russell's feeling of what might have been, it was polesitter Norris who tamed the conditions the best to earn the most hard-won of pole positions.

"It was about getting two laps in at the beginning, not making any mistakes, and that's exactly what we did, so it's been a very good day," said the McLaren driver.

Sports.title: 'Very disappointed' Russell says Mercedes error cost him Sao Paulo GP pole
Sports.content:
George Russell said he was "really disappointed" as he insisted a "misjudgement" by his Mercedes team had cost him pole position for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.

Russell drove impressively throughout a hugely-challenging wet qualifying session at Interlagos but ultimately missed out on pole position by two tenths to McLaren's Lando Norris.

The Mercedes driver had led Norris by four tenths of a second after their first runs in Q3, but was then told to abort his second run when he was being held up by the Williams of Alex Albon.

Mercedes thought that Russell would have time to complete another push lap, but the rain intensified moments later and prevented anyone from going faster for the seven minutes of the session that remained.

Russell reacted with fury over team radio, questioning the instruction for him to abort and insisting that regardless of the time he was losing behind Albon, he would have been able to better Norris' time.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from qualifying for the 2026 Grand Prix

As Russell is serving a five-place grid penalty in Brazil for taking a new internal combustion engine, he would not have started from pole in any case, and will now begin Sunday's race in seventh.

"I think it was just a bit of miscommunication," Russell said. "I need to speak with the team because we believed we'd get another lap before the rain came in.

"So, I was on a really strong lap and I was asked to back off because I caught up Albon, and then obviously the rain came.

"So, yeah, it was very disappointing. I need to understand how it happened and why we got that wrong.

"But I felt very strong, the whole session. Similar to Lando, I had more confidence in the wet than I had in the dry. But yeah, I definitely felt pole was there for the taking."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A deflated George Russell reacts to his qualifying session in Sao Paulo

Asked whether he considered overriding the instruction to abort his lap, Russell added: "They've got the weather forecast in front of them and I don't. And this is where you need that trust and you're relying on one another.

"Obviously, it was the wrong decision, and it was a decision that I think, as soon as it was made, I think we knew it was the wrong one because already they could actually feel the rain pouring harder."

Despite his clear frustration, Russell insisted his race engineer Marcus Dudley, along with other colleagues, weren't necessary responsible given the decision would have been led by the information they were seeing.

"We need to understand, we're relying on a lot of systems. We can't point the finger at somebody," Russell said.

Image: Russell was frustrated to miss out on pole position in Brazil

"We need to understand why we made that decision and were our systems telling us what we needed to know because you're relying on the radar.

"But it doesn't make it any less frustrating for me. It's not my engineer's fault. He's relaying information.

"He's ultimately the one who passes the message on. But he's got 12 people talking to him, giving him that information to relay on, so we just need to understand why we made that decision."

Wolff unsure Russell would have got pole with aborted lap

Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff said he didn't think Russell would have been able to beat Norris to pole on the aborted lap due to the time his driver was losing behind Albon.

"If we were to have a crystal ball to know whether you should back off or not, that would be helpful," Wolff told Sky Sports F1.

"It was a difficult one, a 50-50 call. He was running into Albon.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Martin Brundle believes Kimi Antonelli winning the world title could trigger an 'overdrive' for George Russell, or it's 'game over' for the Mercedes team-mate

"He was 18 milliseconds up on Norris at that stage. I don't think it would have been enough for pole, but he drove perfectly all session and merited to be on pole.

"He deserved it but you can't make that call. It's 50 per cent right or wrong. George was in a league of his own today."

Russell's frustrations follow his team-mate Kimi Antonelli, who qualified third, being crowned world champion at last weekend's Mexico City Grand Prix.

The Brit was excused from his media duties after the race in Mexico as Wolff described him as "distraught", with Russell revealing in Brazil that he had found the situation hard to deal with, especially after a technical issue saw him drop back from second on the grid on the opening lap.

As Russell expressed his anger at the instruction to abort the lap in Brazil, Wolff came on the radio in an apparent attempt to diffuse the situation as he told his driver second was a strong result.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player With Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli having won the world title at the last race, George Russell reflects on what's been a tough season for him

Asked for his feelings on Wolff's radio communication with him, Russell said he understood that the Austrian was attempting to protect the wider morale of the team.

"When you're a driver, you're the one who feels it the most," Russell said. "And going back to his (Wolff's) leadership skills, we've got to remember, we collectively made a misjudgement today, and there's members of my team who are going to be feeling as bad as I am currently.

"So, it's important to remember that and we need to just keep the morale high.

"It was a very solid performance, and I guess we take the positive from that. There are no points for a pole, but it would have just been a nice little one to add to the tally."

Would Russell have got pole?

Sky Sports pundits Karun Chandhok and Bernie Collins were split on whether Russell would have claimed pole had he completed the lap behind Albon.

Chandhok said: "In George's mind, he felt like he should have carried on.

"I don't think he would have beaten Lando to be honest. He was so close to Alex and would have had to follow him. I don't know if he would have got pole.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On this day in 2022, George Russell secured his maiden Formula One win as the Mercedes driver triumphed at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix

"I can see the frustration but personally, I think he would have lost more time being stuck behind Albon and I don't think he would have beaten Lando."

But Collins said: "I can see why he's disappointed.

"I think he would have been on pole on that second lap because his fastest first and second sector, with Albon's fastest third sector is enough for pole.

"His middle sector on that lap was actually seven tenths up."

Sports.title: Clarke hands Billam-Smith first stoppage loss in stunning upset win
Sports.content:
Cheavon Clarke scored a stunning stoppage win over Chris Billam-Smith at the Copper Box Arena in London.

He not only knocked the former world champion down for the first time in Billam-Smith's career, he put him over twice and handed the Bournemouth star a first stoppage defeat.

Halted on the ropes, as Clarke's right hooks streaked in, Billam-Smith at once shook his head to protest as the referee waved it off.

Clarke, after a thrilling win over Jack Massey last time out, was looking for a big-name scalp that would launch him into the top class of the division. He got it.

Billam-Smith had been seeking to exact some personal vengeance too. Clarke had beaten him in a pivotal national amateur championship final 10 years ago. The Bournemouth man had subsequently converted himself from amateur nearly man to elite professional champion. But, a decade on, Clarke once again handed him a bitterly painful defeat.

They began the first round busily with frenetic work. Clarke, full of energy, winged shots over. His head swung in too wildly, but it was a right hand over the top that gave Billam-Smith pause for thought.

Image: Chris Billam-Smith is a former WBO cruiserweight world champion.

Clarke popped Billam-Smith with a left hook as the former champion charged after him. Rolling under a left hook, Clarke moved off. He snuck his right round Billam-Smith's guard. Billam-Smith swallowed another right but dug in an uppercut with his backhand.

A right flew in and Clarke grabbed him in a clinch. He then answered with a crack right to the jaw himself. But Billam-Smith, renowned for his toughness, took it stolidly.

In the third round Clarke blasted an excellent right uppercut between Billam-Smith's elbows. He touched his chin with the left hook and reached Billam-Smith with a long cross.

Manoeuvring for position in a clinch, Clarke whipped his left hook over. Billam-Smith bulled into him in a physical, frenetic fight, finishing the fourth round swinging hooks.

Early in the fifth round Clarke went for Billam-Smith. They traded hard hits.

Image: Cheavon Clarke was coming off a thrilling victory over Jack Massey in last fight

The clinching, a frequent feature of the fight, appeared to leave them both frustrated. Clarke popped in a clean jab, but Billam-Smith ground forward onto the front foot.

Billam-Smith hit out with thudding power in the sixth round. Clarke sighed out a breath and stepped back, briefly losing the shape of his boxing.

But in the seventh round it was stunning to see Clarke bomb Billam-Smith over with a right. The Bournemouth man struggled back to his feet and Clarke swarmed forward. As Billam-Smith tried to escape from the ropes, Clarke knocked him down again.

He attacked Billam-Smith once more on the ropes. Billam-Smith's leg stuttered, but he had his feet under him when referee Lee Every moved in to end it.

'I'd love to run it back'

"I'm fine. It was a good shot. He buzzed me, obviously," Billam-Smith said afterwards. "It was a great shot. I made a mistake, but I felt like I was winning the fight.

"Fair play to Chev. We've had three fights now and he's got them all. I'd love to run it back and get him eventually."

Clarke beamed: "Underdog to who? Not us!

"I don't care about a label. I'm Chev Clarke and that's all that matters."

Sports.title: 'We squashed it' - Hamilton reveals details of talks with Leclerc after fall out
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton says he and Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc have "squashed" their incident at the Mexico City Grand Prix after holding talks in Brazil.

Hamilton, Leclerc and team principal Frederic Vasseur held talks on Thursday night to discuss the incident which saw Max Verstappen take advantage of the opening lap Ferrari squabble last Sunday to win the race.

Hamilton has subsequently been critical of Leclerc in interviews and said that discussions were required to more clearly define their rules of combat to avoid costly repeats in future.

Hamilton will start at the back of the grid for Sunday's Sao Paulo Grand Prix due to a power unit change and spoke to the media for the first time on Saturday since his talks with Leclerc.

"Me and Charles sat and spoke and we squashed it, and we're moving on," he told Sky Sports F1.

"We still have a huge amount of respect for each other and I'm glad we had a chat and now we move on.

"We've been getting along just fine as normal. Sometimes in those scenarios it takes having a conversation and there's been no demands from either side, it's both just giving our points and areas we can do better and support each other. I'm hoping to have better races moving forwards."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen reflected on a wet qualifying session in Sao Paulo

Leclerc, who starts 14th after a 10-grid place penalty for a new internal combustion engine, had a similar opinion to Hamilton.

"Obviously, there's been a lot of things, probably too much things in the last week," he said.

"We've spoken. I think everything is settled, and I'm looking forward for the rest of the weekend now."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charles Leclerc says he's 'settled' his disagreement with Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton after their clash in last week's Mexico City GP

Vasseur: The guidelines are still the same

The Mexico incident comes two months after Leclerc admitted he was at fault for his opening lap battle with Hamilton in Monza, where the latter was forced wide into the gravel and lost several positions.

Vasseur says he reminded Hamilton and Leclerc that the team comes first and the drivers must "keep that in mind".

"The guidelines are still the same. They accumulated perhaps a bit of frustration because they are starting each weekend side by side, and you have a kind of accumulation of fact," he said.

"But at the end of the day, the guideline is always the same - it's that they need to respect each other.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ferrari Team Principal Fred Vasseur answers questions about Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc after a public spat between the two

"They are two competitors with the fighting spirit for sure, but they need to have a respect for the other one.

"But mainly and firstly, they need to respect the brand, the team, the people working at home, the people working at the on track.

"I think we are putting a lot of effort on this, and the message was clear and will stay clear."
