Jaissle called it a soft decision. Newcastle, who saw Bernd Leno twice thwart Harvey Barnes before half-time, moved on and improved in the second half. They pressed with more intensity and created opportunities for Barnes and Wissa.

Fulham had no out ball with García unable to impose himself against Burn and Malick Thiaw. Palacios came on and was at fault when Newcastle broke the deadlock. The Spaniard played an aimless pass across his own half and was punished by Murphy, who seized possession before driving forward to cut inside and crack a brilliant shot past Leno from 25 yards.

It seemed Newcastle were about to ease the pressure on Jaissle. Fulham had other ideas. Arbeloa praised the defiance. Palacios linked with Alex Iwobi and found Muniz. The ball bounced around the six-yard box and Muniz forced it past Hornicek.

Fulham poured forward in search of a winner. Lewis Hall almost restored Newcastle’s lead, only for Leno to deny the left-back. A draw was fair.

Sports.title: European football: Mbappé eases Real Madrid past Valencia to move joint top
Sports.content:
Kylian Mbappé scored for the seventh match running as Real Madrid pulled provisionally level on points with La Liga leaders Barcelona after a 3-0 win at 10-man Valencia on Saturday.

Reigning champions Barça visit Atlético Madrid, third, on Sunday, aiming to move back clear of the chasing pack. José Mourinho’s Madrid largely dominated at Mestalla stadium as they secured an eighth win in a row across all competitions.

Federico Valverde and Arda Guler’s first-half goals put Madrid in the driving seat and Mbappé added a third in the second half, bursting on to a dangerous pass by Guler to dart past Stole Dimitrievski and squeeze home his 13th league goal of the campaign.

Bayern Munich secured a 2-1 victory over Mainz in the Bundesliga on Saturday but the form ⁠of goalkeeper Manuel Neuer will again be in the spotlight after another error almost produced an equaliser for the home side ⁠in the first ⁠half.

View image in fullscreen Bayern Munich’s Manuel Neuer (right) injures himself as Lee Jae-sung scores before it was ruled out by VAR. Photograph: Michael Probst/AP

Neuer became Bayern’s ​oldest player at 40 years, 225 days, overtaking Bernd Dreher, but was forced off with a recurrence of a foot injury ⁠that had kept him out of recent matches, replaced before half-time by Jonas Urbig.

Neuer was left flailing at a cross that resulted ⁠in Mainz’s Lee Jae-sung putting the ball in the back of the net with Bayern ​leading 1-0, though the effort was ‌ruled out for offside.

Neuer’s mistake ‌against Augsburg last month, which resulted in the fastest-ever Bundesliga goal after eight seconds ‌by Robin Fellhauer, was the latest in a growing number for the keeper once regarded among the best in the world.

According to Sofascore using Opta data, that error was his fifth that led to a goal in his previous 17 Bundesliga games, or one every 3.4 matches. In 248 appearances before that, he made just 10 ‌such errors, or one every 24.8 games.

Neuer has played twice since that Augsburg fixture, which ended 2-2, missing four games with the foot injury. ​He returned for this week’s 2-0 Champions League win at Atlético Madrid.

The Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane could not find the net against Mainz but did provide two assists for Joshua Kimmich and 18-year-old Lennart Karl as Bayern extended their unbeaten away run in the league ⁠to 31 games.

View image in fullscreen Harry Kane was not on the scoresheet but provided two assists. Photograph: Kai Pfaffenbach/Reuters

They maintained their lead at the top of the Bundesliga ​from Borussia Dortmund with ​both clubs on 21 points from ​nine games. Bayern have a superior goal difference.

Dortmund were given a ​scare by promoted Elversberg ‌but won 2-1, ​thanks to two ​goals from Felix Nmecha.

Third-placed RB Leipzig, who are three points behind the leaders, won 5-2 at home to Augsburg, while Jonathan Burkardt scored a 93rd-minute equaliser for Eintracht Frankfurt as they drew 2-2 at Paderborn in a battle between two mid-table sides.

Werder Bremen missed the chance to climb into the top four when they lost 1-0 at Stuttgart, where an early goal from Maximilian Mittelstädt settled the contest.

Illia Zabarnyi scored the only goal of the game as a weakened Paris Saint-Germain claimed an unspectacular 1-0 win over Troyes in Ligue 1 to make it 11 consecutive victories in all competitions.

View image in fullscreen Illia Zabarnyi points up in delight after scoring the winner for PSG. Photograph: Firas Abdullah/EPA

The Ukraine defender Zabarnyi headed in Senny Mayulu’s cross to break the deadlock in the 39th minute at the Parc des Princes, and that proved sufficient to beat their newly promoted opponents who lie in the bottom three.

PSG’s neighbours Paris FC won 1-0 away to Auxerre thanks to a second-half goal by the in-form striker Lassine Sinayoko.

Mali forward Sinayoko, a summer signing from Auxerre, opportunistically turned in an assist by Pablo Pagis, who was called up to the France squad for the first time by Zinedine Zidane on Friday. Sinayoko, 26, is the top scorer in Ligue 1 with nine goals in 10 games. Liam Rosenior’s Paris FC are second, three points behind PSG.

Roma moved up to second Serie A with a 3-0 win over Sassuolo at the ⁠Stadio Olimpico.

Sassuolo held out until the 27th minute when the Roma defender Mario Hermoso ⁠drove forward towards the area. His attempted pass to Donyell Malen was intercepted but he gathered the ​loose ball, took a touch to make ‌space and fired into the ‌roof of the net.

Three minutes later, Malen’s shot took a touch off a Sassuolo defender before Sebastian ‌Walukiewicz turned the ball into his own net. Sassuolo’s goalkeeper Arijanet Muric kept his side in the game with saves from Leonardo Balerdi and Matías Soulé before the break but Rodrigo Mora’s 58th-minute goal put the game out of reach.

Sports.title: Truro City game at Folkestone called off after Yassine En-Neyah has medical emergency in warm-up
Sports.content:
Truro’s National League South game at Folkestone Invicta was called off after the visitors’ midfielder Yassine En-Neyah had a medical emergency and was taken to hospital.

The 26-year-old was transported to the William Harvey Hospital in Ashford for treatment but was responsive on Saturday night, according to an update from the Cornwall club.

“He is stable, sitting up and chatting, but will remain in hospital overnight under observation,” a Truro City statement read.

“The club would like to place on record its thanks to Truro City’s medical staff, their counterparts at Folkestone Invicta, along with all club personnel from the home club.

“Both the National League and Football Association have also offered their help and support. There have also been many well wishes from Truro City fans and the wider football community too.”

En-Neyah joined Truro from Waterford in 2023, having once been on the books at Nottingham Forest. The Morocco-born player was raised in Ireland and spent time in the youth systems of Corduff and Bohemians, before he joined the Forest academy in 2017.

Truro lie third in the National League South table, four points behind the leaders Ebbsfleet United but with a game in hand.

Sports.title: Manchester City break clear of Chelsea in WSL after Bronze’s freak own goal
Sports.content:
An own goal by defender Lucy Bronze ⁠against Everton cost Chelsea top spot in the Women’s ⁠Super League as ⁠they ​were held to a 1-1 draw at home, allowing Manchester City ⁠to leapfrog them with a 5-0 drubbing of West Ham.

Bronze headed ⁠the ball back across the goal to tee ​up Sandy Baltimore ‌to score ‌from close range in the 28th minute, but ‌five minutes later her attempted clearance rolled into her own net to put Everton level. The visitors held on for a draw as Chelsea dropped points for the ‌first time since the opening day of the season.

Manchester City made the most ​of that slip-up as Bunny Shaw’s superb goalscoring form continued, the Jamaican striker netting a hat-trick as her side cantered to a comprehensive win against West Ham, with Aoba ​Fujino ​and Iman Beney also on target.

The WSL’s top scorer gave City the lead six minutes before the break. City then ran riot after the interval as Shaw grabbed another couple for the match ball while Beney and Fujino scored their first goals of the campaign.

West Ham were happy to sit in and soak up the pressure from their opponents, and Constance Picaud-Inconnu was relieved when she parried Kerstin Casparij’s effort straight back into danger but no one was on hand to tap home. The visitors had the woodwork to thank for not going a goal down when Fujino’s effort hit a post.

It seemed only a matter of time before City made the breakthrough and they did just that five minutes before the break. Hemp stole possession as West Ham tried to play out from the back and the ball was worked to Shaw to finish expertly.

View image in fullscreen Sandy Baltimore opens the scoring for Chelsea against Everton. Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/Reuters

City doubled their advantage eight minutes after the break as Shaw directed Hemp’s cross past Picaud-Inconnu. Fujino hit the crossbar but was not to be denied minutes later to make it 3-0.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Beney added a fourth five minutes after coming on with a deflected strike from the edge of the box. Shaw completed her hat-trick with 16 minutes to play when she latched on to a through ball from Grace Clinton before grabbing her 12th goal from nine WSL games.

Sports.title: Tottenham summer signing branded a ‘fraud’ as alarming streak continues
Sports.content:
Jamie O'Hara ripped into Omar Marmoush and Dominic Solanke as their woes in front of goal continued during a 1-0 defeat to Leeds United.

Marmoush joined from Manchester City in the summer on an initial loan.



4 Marmoush's start to life in north London has not been great

However, the loan will become permanent in the summer for an initial £50million and a further £10m in add-ons.

But his performances will have to improve if Spurs fans are to think he is worth the money.

The Egypt international, who has started eight league fixtures for Roberto De Zerbi's side this term, has just one goal across all competitions this term.



Worryingly, his blank against Leeds meant he is still yet to score in an away Premier League fixture ever since he joined City from Eintracht Frankfurt in January 2025.

He lasted just 65 minutes against Leeds before Dejan Kulusevski came on, while Solanke started the game on thee bench and was brought on to offer nothing.



And O'Hara, reacting to the defeat on the GameDay Phone-In, was not happy.

"Solanke was non-existent when he came on," O'Hara said.

"Marmoush is, like, fraud levels right now.

"I don't know what he's doing. Did we sign him from Man City? Did we sign his twin brother? I don't know who this geezer is because he is absolutely garbage.



"You've got players like [Mohammed] Kudus who wants to put balls in the box and put it into good areas.

4 O'Hara absolutely lost it watching Spurs' winning run come to an end Credit: talkSPORT

"We are now hesitating to put the ball into the box because the strikers aren't going to score."

Day to forget

Tottenham arrived at Elland Road for the 12:30pm in great form.

They had won three Premier League games in a row after an awful start to the season.



One of those victories was a famous win against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, but they didn't really turn up.

Leeds used their superior physicality to bully Spurs, and after knocking at the door, Noah Okafor stepped off the bench to score the winner.

And after the game, De Zerbi fumed at his side's failure to win any duels.

4 Okafor's goal separated the teams but the scoreline didn't reflect Leeds' dominance Credit: Getty



He said: “We won no duels, no one-to-ones. There was space to play and we didn’t take the right decisions.

"We didn’t show personality or what we are, who we are. It’s a part of the journey. It’s not an excuse and it can be normal in football but we have to be honest.

“If you are not honest today the future is not good. If we analyse our second-half behaviour honestly then I think we can become a top team.

"We have the physicality and the quality but it’s not just about the physicality game. We didn’t show character, personality or courage.



“My players have the ability to come here, play better and maybe win. But maybe we are not ready yet to be consistent for many games in a row. We know where we have to work and improve.

4 Jayden Bogle did manage to avoid a red card for this tackle that would have changed the course of the game Credit: Premier League

“I was surprised by the second half as my players worked very well this week. We spoke all week about the intensity and the type of game we would find here in this stadium so it was not a surprise for us.”

But De Zerbi feels as if John Brooks should have sent off Jayden Bogle for standing on Mathys Tel's Achilles.



He said: “I was surprised because in the same position in the second half there were two different fouls, the yellow card for Pedro Porro is not possible. I don’t know if it is a red card or not on Mathys Tel but the parameter of the referee was not good enough for this in both situations.”

Spurs are set to submit a complaint to ProRef over the decision.

Sports.title: Fans left baffled as FA Cup clash marred by intense fog covering entire ground
Sports.content:
Football fans couldn't believe what they were watching as Altrincham's FA Cup tie against Notts County.

Or, given the intense fog that encapsulated the stadium, what they were not watching.



4 This was the view fans were left with watching on TV

4 This was the view of the penalty shootout

The contest finished 2-2 at full-time, sending it to extra time and then eventually penalties.

In the end, it was Notts County who won 3-2 in a crazy shootout as both teams missed spot kicks in the conditions.



TNT Sports commentator Adam Summerton did his best to cover the action as even the managers of both teams were questioning what was going on.

The prize for County is a place in the second round of the FA Cup as they ended the National League team's run.



Pictures on the broadcast of the match left several fans baffled as to how it was not stopped due to the conditions.

One fan on X said: "Maybe the camera makes it worse but how is this Altrincham vs Notts County still playing in this fog is ridiculous."



Another added: "I’m amazed anyone could see that Notts County equaliser at Altrincham."

A third said: "Nice to see the BBC are using the screens that VAR use during a game for the Altrincham vs Notts County match."

An additional supporter proclaimed: "Altrincham v Notts County is currently being played in a cloud."

A fifth continued: "The coverage of Altrincham v Notts County is farcical. You can’t see the other side of the pitch."



4 Fans at the ground saw the funny side and used their phone cameras to try and create some light

4 Banks thought he'd won it Credit: Getty

How did Altrincham v Notts County unfold?

Making it to the second round of the FA Cup is a big deal with the dream of a big Premier League tie just one win away.

And despite the terrible conditions, both sides put on a show.

It was the League One side who opened the scoring as former Newcastle United winger Callum Roberts set up Jacob Bedeau.



But a man who was in the ninth tier, Lucas Weaver, hauled Alty level.

He got on the end of a lovely pass by Matty Kosylo into the box, squared up his man, jinked inside and drove a low shot in at the near post.

The shock looked to be on in the 59th minute as Lewis Banks got the end of an excellent cross from the left.

Banks' first header was saved, but he tapped in the rebound.

However, as the fog became worse, Roberts hit a low first-time curling shot from the edge of the box.

But the teams couldn't be separated in normal time with a penalty shootout required.



James Belshaw was the hero for the League One side with two saves in the shootout before Rosaire Longelo stepped up to slam home the winner.

Sports.title: Arsenal equal all-time club record with victory over Hull
Sports.content:
Arsenal have matched their best ever start to a Premier League season following Saturday’s 1-0 win over Hull.

The Gunners provisionally stretched their lead at the top of the table to six points with a hard-fought victory over the Tigers at the Emirates Stadium.



3 Martin Odegaard was quickest to react to fire Arsenal's winner against Hull Credit: AFP

Mikel Arteta’s side were made to wait until the 72nd minute for their winner courtesy of Martin Odegaard.

The Arsenal skipper was on hand to slot home from close range after Noni Madueke’s effort was parried into his path by Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis.

The win took the Gunners up to 27 points from their ten league games this season – a record-equalling best for the club.



Arsenal’s previous points return from the same number of games came in the 2022/23 season.

That season, the north London club agonisingly missed out on the Premier League title to Pep Guardiola’s Manchester City.



City and Arsenal enjoyed an enthralling title race only for Guardiola’s men to pull ahead and claim the title by a five-point margin.

But it is reigning champions Arsenal who lead the way while having momentum in their favour in this season’s race for the crown.



Sergej Jakirovic’s Hull side put up a valiant fight at the Emirates and were looking good for what would have been an impressive point on the road.

VAR controversy

The match was plunged into confusion late in the first half when Kai Havertz was denied what appeared to be a clear penalty.

The Arsenal forward had shirt pulled by Hull defender Nobel Mendy only for referee Farai Hallam to wave away the appeals.

3 Referee Farai Hallam made the call not to award the penalty Credit: Getty



3 Mikel Arteta's side are on the right track for success this season

Hallam was subsequently instructed to consult the pitchside monitor where it was concluded that Havertz was in an offside position at the time he was impeded.

But it all proved insignificant in the end as Arsenal extended their unbeaten home run in all competitions to 11 games.

That sees the Gunners claim top spot going into the International break with key fixtures to come in the lead up to Christmas.



Next up for Arteta's side in the Premier League is a trip to Newcastle where they have won just once in their last four visits.

Further testing clashes follow with title rivals Manchester City, Brentford to play before the north London derby against Tottenham.

Arsenal also face home matches against Borussia Dortmund and Real Madrid in the Champions League.



﻿

Sports.title: William Saliba left out of Arsenal squad for alternative appearance this weekend
Sports.content:
William Saliba left out of Arsenal squad for alternative appearance this weekend

William Saliba is set to play for Arsenal's Under-21s against Aston Villa on Sunday, Mikel Arteta has confirmed.

The defender has not played this season since suffering a back injury with France at the World Cup, but was named on the bench in the Gunners' win at Slavia Prague on Wednesday.



4 Saliba was involved in an Arsenal matchday squad for the first time this season against Slavia Prague on Wednesady Credit: Getty

While Saliba did not feature in the Champions League victory, his presence led to hopes he could feature against Hull on Saturday.

Saliba absence explained

However, Saliba was not selected for the home clash, but it has now been revealed his absence isn't a cause for concern.

Gunners boss Arteta confirmed that was not due to any setback, but rather a plan to get the Frenchman back up to full fitness.



Saliba will take his next steps towards a return by being involved for Arsenal's Under-21s when they host Villa on Sunday.

Explaining this, Arteta said: “He needs some minutes.

“Obviously, the Champions League allows you to bring more players into the bench, but we believe that it’s the best thing to do, to play some minutes on the weekend with the Under-21s and then be fully fit for the international break.”



With the international break up next, means that Saliba will now have to wait until November 21 to make his return to the pitch.

The 25-year-old was not included in Zinedine Zidane's second France squad, as they prepare to face Italy and Turkey in the Nations League.



That's despite Arteta previously suggesting he would have been comfortable with Saliba being called up for international duty.

Selection headache?

Saliba's imminent return will come as a major boost for Arsenal, with the defender establishing himself as indispensable in recent years.

4 Saliba has yet to kick a ball for Arsenal this season Credit: Getty

4 The Frenchman has been out injured for over three months Credit: Getty



Widely considered one of the top-flight's best defenders, his rock-solid partnership with Gabriel played a key role in the Gunners' Premier League title victory last season after a 22-year wait.

The centre-back pair conceded just 27 league goals across the entirety of last term and Saliba was named in the PFA team of the year for the fourth consecutive time.

However, the France star might not find that he walks straight into the starting XI, with Arteta now facing a selection headache.

Saliba's absence led to the Gunners' £55million move for Ezri Konsa this summer, who has impressed since his arrival from Aston Villa.



The England star has made an immediate impact, most recently helping Arsenal keep three consecutive clean sheets in the Premier League.

This has led Manchester United legend Rio Ferdinand to suggest that Konsa should move to right-back once Saliba returns.

4 Ezri Konsa has quickly established himself at Arsenal Credit: Getty

Konsa has previously impressed when deputising in the role - doing so for England at the World Cup - and this would allow Arteta to accommodate all of his defensive talent.



Speaking on his YouTube channel, Ferdinand said: "I think Saliba is one of those guys that you have to find room for in the team. He's that good, he's top.

"I said to my son yesterday, 'watch Ezri Konsa', because everything he does is efficient. That's a great problem for Arteta to have.

"I wouldn't be surprised if Konsa goes back to right-back once Saliba comes back. I wouldn't be surprised because Konsa is top."

Sports.title: Wantaway Man United kid JJ Gabriel outlines Ballon d’Or ambition in Spanish media interview
Sports.content:
Manchester United prodigy JJ Gabriel is targeting future Ballon d’Or success and has hinted at an imminent move to Real Madrid.

The 16-year-old forward recently signalled his intention to leave Manchester United by handing in a shock transfer request.



3 Gabriel was said to be unhappy with his lack of game time at United Credit: Getty

A host of clubs have reportedly shown an interest in the starlet with talkSPORT reporting earlier this week that Real Madrid were leading the chase for his signature.

Gabriel appeared to drop his biggest hint yet regarding possible move to the Santiago Bernabeu by giving an exclusive interview to Spanish outlet Marca.

The youngster has not trained at United’s Carrington Training Centre since September and has instead spent his time training in Madrid.



In the interview with Marca, Gabriel discussed his favourite club between La Liga giants Real Madrid and Barcelona while discussing his future objectives.

Pressed on what his preferred club is, Gabriel replied: “Obviously Madrid” - to the amusement of his watching father Joe O'Cearuill.



A switch to the club is expected to be confirmed in January with Manchester United possibly netting a compensation of as little at £300,000 for the teen sensation.

Gabriel went on to reveal his personal ambition of one day winning the Ballon d’Or.



The decorated award handed out to the best player in the world has not been won by a Real Madrid player since Karim Benzema in 2022.

The Frenchman was the last active La Liga player to have won the award with Vincius Junior narrowly missing out in 2024 and Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal coming up short behind Harry Kane in this year’s edition.

“My dream is to win the Ballon d'Or,” Gabriel explained, having already made his mark on the UEFA Youth League with a hattrick prior to his transfer request.

3 Gabriel is hoping to one day follow in the footsteps of fellow Englishman Harry Kane by winning the Ballon d'Or Credit: Getty



Manchester United sources insist they have not entered into discussions with any club over a transfer but it appears that a move to the Spanish capital is imminent.

The forward is expected to start his Real Madrid career in the club’s Castilla team that functions in Spain’s third tier.

He will also feature in the UEFA Youth League.

Why does Gabriel want to leave Manchester United?

Gabriel wants to leave Manchester United due to frustrations over his development pathway. His camp have reportedly pinpointed a perceived delay in his integration into the first team.

The star’s representatives have lost faith in the long-term project at Manchester United, claiming the club has declined compared to Europe's current elite.



Gabriel was named the Premier League’s Under-18 Player of the Season last year aged just 14 years old.

3 Gabriel has been lauded for his superb displays across United's youth teams Credit: Getty

He went on to break records playing for United’s various youth teams and became the youngest player to feature in the Under-18s.

Sports.title: VAR chaos as Arsenal penalty refused for offside but rules expert says it should have stood
Sports.content:
VAR chaos as Arsenal penalty refused for offside but rules expert says it should have stood

Martin Keown blasted the farcical nature in which Kai Havertz was denied a penalty against Hull City.

Havertz had his shirt pulled by Hull defender Nobel Mendy as he looked to break clear late in the first half of Arsenal's 1-0 win over the Tigers.



2 Havertz pleaded his case to the official but to no avail Credit: AFP

Why did Arsenal not receive a penalty?

The incident was initially dismissed by referee Farai Hallam, but he was quickly instructed by VAR official Michael Oliver to review the incident on the pitchside monitor.

However, a review quickly showed that Havertz was in an offside position when Mendy tugged on his shirt, meaning the pitchside review would ultimately be redundant.

That's exactly how it played out when Hallam announced his decision to the Emirates Stadium crowd.



Hallam initially admitted Mendy's foul was indeed worthy of a penalty, sparking cheers from Gunners fans.

But those quickly subsided when he explained that because Havertz was in an offside position at the time, it was a moot point.



Martin Keown reacts to the non-penalty

The entire process left Gunners great Keown, who was on commentary duties for talkSPORT, furious.

"He should never have been asked to go to the VAR monitor, should he," Keown said.



"They should have determined that already if he was offside. That's ridiculous."

Keown added: "Wouldn't you have decided all of that in the VAR room before you ask the referee to go and look at it? It's ridiculous. I'd really love to hear the true story on that one."

Co-commentator Alex Crook added Liverpool fans would have felt Havertz's non-penalty would be 'karma' given Alexander Isak did not receive a penalty when Jurrien Timber committed a similar offence last Sunday.

2 Referee Farai Hallam was at the centre of controversy by not awarding a penalty Credit: Getty



Were Arsenal robbed of a penalty against Hull?

But in a further twist to the decision, BBC football rules expert Dale Johnson explained that Arsenal should have been awarded a penalty.

He said: "A player who is in an offside position only becomes active when they commit an offside offence.

"Kai Havertz must be 'attempting to play the ball, or challenging an opponent for the ball' - otherwise the shirt pull by Nobel Mendy takes precedence. The foul comes before any offside offence.

"Havertz did not commit an offside offence, and this should have been a spot-kick to Arsenal regardless of the offside.



"We saw this a couple of seasons ago between Newcastle and Bournemouth. Fabian Schar was just offside but pulled back as he moved to run onto a free-kick delivery. A penalty was awarded after a VAR review."

Regardless of whether a penalty should or should not have been awarded, Havertz has developed an uncomfortable habit of being offside.

By straying beyond Hull's defensive line, Havertz has been flagged offside a league-leading 15 times this term, seven more than Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin who sits second on the leaderboard.

Sports.title: Xavi Simons gives one-word reaction as Tottenham fear ‘bad’ Mathys Tel injury
Sports.content:
Xavi Simons has asked football fans to play a game of spot the difference.

Simons, who is recovering from an ACL tear sustained in April, watched on as Spurs slipped to a 1-0 loss away at Leeds on Saturday.

3 Spurs' three-game win streak was snapped by Leeds Credit: AFP

But one moment in particular caught Simons' attention and left him baffled as to how no further action was taken.

What sparked Xavi Simons' reaction?

Spurs players and fans, including talkSPORT's Jamie O'Hara, blew up deluxe when Leeds defender Jayden Bogle avoided a red card for an ugly challenge on Mathys Tel in the first half.

Replays showed Bogle planted his foot on the back of Tel's ankle, with the Spurs flyer requiring medical treatment following the miscued tackle.

Although a five-minute VAR check ensued, Bogle escaped a red card while Tel had to be substituted.

How severe is Mathys Tel's injury?

Unfortunately for Tel, the challenge could leave him sidelined for a period of time.

Speaking after the contest, Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi admitted it was a 'bad injury'.

"Now we have to make the medical check, and in the next day we will know what is the problem."

For Simons, he could not believe Bogle remained on the pitch given he committed a similar foul on Liverpool skipper Virgil van Dijk last season but was sent off.

The incident happened during Liverpool's 2-1 win over Spurs last December.

Simons was initially shown a yellow card for the challenge by referee John Brooks.

3 De Zerbi admitted he is worried about Tel's injury sustained against Leeds Credit: Getty

However, Brooks was instructed to review the tackle on the pitchside monitor, and it wasn't long before Simons' yellow card was upgraded to a red one.

It was the first red card of Simons' senior career and saw him immediately receive a three-match suspension.

What did Xavi Simons say about Jayden Bogle's challenge?

Given the similarity in tackles but variation in punishment, Simons expressed his frustrations on social media.

Simons shared screenshots of both challenges to his Snapchat story along with the caption: "Difference?"

Simons wasn't the only Spurs player to express their befuddlement at Bogle not being punished.

Speaking to talkSPORT, Spurs skipper Micky van de Ven said: "When I saw the impact from the side, I knew straight away.

3 Bogle has been sent off just once in his professional career Credit: Getty

"I went to the referee and said, 'This is a hard challenge.'

"I think it says enough that they're going to check it. So when the VAR needs so long to check it, you can always call the ref to have a look by himself."

Why did Jayden Bogle avoid a red card?

Despite Spurs fans wincing with every replay of Bogle's tackle, VAR official Tony Harrington backed up referee John Brooks' initial call not to send the Leeds ace off.

"I'm confirming the on-field decision of no red card," Harrington said.

"There's a lack of speed going into the challenge and he's stepping into the tackle.

"Confirming a reckless challenge."

Sports.title: ‘Horrendous feeling’ – James Trafford reveals how bad it got at Man City
Sports.content:
‘Horrendous feeling’ – James Trafford reveals how bad it got at Man City

James Trafford has revealed he left Manchester City for Leeds this summer for the sake of his mental wellbeing.

The England international sealed a dream return to the Etihad in the summer of 2025, two years after he first departed to join Burnley.

4 Trafford has kept four Premier League clean sheets in 10 games for Leeds this term Credit: Getty

However, disaster struck weeks later when the Citizens then signed Italy star Gianluigi Donnarumma in the same window.

This immediately saw Trafford relegated to second-choice, despite appearing set to become City's No.1 when he first joined.

It meant that after starting the first three matches of the campaign, Trafford made just one further Premier League start in the following 35 games.

The 24-year-old then left the Etihad for Leeds in a club-record £45million move in the summer transfer window.

Since then, Trafford has been a standout performer in the top-flight and started for England over Jordan Pickford during the most recent international break.

Trafford: I lost myself at City

With Trafford flying high at Elland Road, the goalkeeper has now opened up on his struggles during his year back at Man City, and admitted a move away for first-team football was crucial.

On his time at City, Trafford told Football Daily's The Football Interview: "What a horrendous, horrendous feeling. Not playing.

"You are ringing a lot of people and just venting. Like most people, you have a [bad] day at work and you ring someone up.

"I ring my dad, I ring my mum, I ring my missus, I ring my mates. I like ringing my mates and we can just have a good talk about it all. It's quite funny.

He continued: "I had to play regularly this season for my own mental wellbeing. You just lose yourself not playing.

4 Despite a lack of Premier League minutes, Trafford was City's first choice goalkeeper in domestic cup competitions last term and lifted two trophies Credit: Getty

4 Gianluigi Donnarumma's European pedigree immediately saw him replace Trafford as Man City's No.1 Credit: Getty

"Maybe I'm different, I don't know, but the feeling of not playing every week, it felt horrendous.

"I just had to play every week this season for that mental feel-good and to keep progressing with my career and edging me closer to achieving the dreams I want to achieve."

Despite his limited playing time, Trafford insisted there were valuable lessons from his final season at City, where he started in both of their Carabao Cup and FA Cup final victories at Wembley.

"Going into any season, I always have the highest of hopes and always the belief that it will go the best way it could," he added.

"Unfortunately, we didn't win all four trophies. It didn't go how I expected it to go, but it happens.

"In the moment, I just tried to make the best of it as I could. Looking back, I don't think it was a disappointing season in the end because I learned so much, I improved so much and I won two trophies in one year.

4 Trafford has earned four England caps to date Credit: Getty

"There were moments when I was very down, regretting things and feeling disappointed, but looking back, I'm very thankful for the experience. What an incredible year."

In the same interview, Trafford shares his hopes at making the England No.1 shirt his own, having served as back-up to Jordan Pickford at the 2026 World Cup.

His strong form for Leeds was rewarded in the last international break, where he started in back-to-back Nations League games.

On his hopes of becoming England's No.1, Trafford said: "It's my aim and it's something I've always dreamed of.

"I always believe that one day I could be. Every day I try to keep improving to put myself in the best position to be England's number one one day.

"I think everyone in the goalkeeping department with the national team wants to be number one because it's an amazing position to be in."

Sports.title: Much-improved Newcastle stop the rot with a 1-1 draw at Fulham - but 'slapstick' defending and wasteful finishing will leave Matthias Jaissle rueing a missed opportunity, writes CRAIG HOPE
Sports.content:
Much-improved Newcastle stop the rot with a 1-1 draw at Fulham - but 'slapstick' defending and wasteful finishing will leave Matthias Jaissle rueing a missed opportunity, writes CRAIG HOPE

Just when Newcastle looked set for victory after Jacob Murphy had borrowed Amar Dedic's bow to arrow them into a late lead, they turned the weapon on themselves.

After a week in which Dedic, Bosnia's answer to Robin Hood, had made headlines when pursued by police for wandering around the Northumberland countryside with his hunting gear, the Geordies were ready to rob the good folk of west London after Murphy found the target ten minutes from time.

Less than three minutes later and they were picking the arrow from their own foot. William Osula failed to protect possession and allowed Fulham to enter the penalty area. Then, with the ball bouncing around the goalmouth, it was home substitute Rodrigo Muniz who pounced to punish Newcastle's scruffy defending.

'Slapstick', visiting boss Matthias Jaissle later called it.

The German also said that his team deserved to win but you got the impression he was relieved to emerge without defeat, especially as the performance was improved on the back of a run of four losses in five.

Newcastle's second-half spirit also showed a response to a week of noise centred on dressing-room unrest, not to mention Dedic's police drama.

Jacob Murphy thought he had won it for Newcastle after scoring late on at Craven Cottage

Rodrigo Muniz netted moments later after sloppy defending from Newcastle, earning a 1-1 draw

Matthias Jaissle's side were much improved but must cut out the errors to win matches

And Jaissle was right in that his team could have left with three points had master archer Harvey Barnes not missed a hat-trick of chances.

MATCH FACTS AND PLAYER RATINGS Fulham (4-2-3-1): Leno 7; Castagne 6 (Tete 77, 5), Affengruber 6, Bassey 6, Robinson 5; Berge 6, Charles 6; Bobb 6 (Sessegnon 78, 6), King 7 (Palacios 72, 5), Iwobi 6; Garcia 4 (Muniz 65, 8) Subs not used: Lecomte, Andersen, Hugo Larsson, Manuel Angel, Kevin Scorer: Muniz 83 Manager: Alvaro Arbeloa 6 Newcastle (4-2-3-1): Hornicek 7; Dedic 6, Thiaw 7 (Schar 85, 6), Burn 7, Hall 6; Nico Gonzalez 5 (Miley 61, 6), Steur 7 (Fernandez-Pardo 74, 5); Murphy 8, Wissa 6 (Willock 61, 5), Barnes 6; Osula 5 (Elanga 85) Subs not used: Pope, Livramento, Botman, Bazoumana Toure Scorer: Murphy 80 Manager: Matthias Jaissle 7 Referee: Rob Jones Attendance: 27,367 MOM: Murphy

The winger is the player to whom they'd want those opportunities to fall, too. But twice before half-time, when denied by Bernd Leno from close range, and then again when lashing wide after the break, he failed to give his side the advantage.

Murphy corrected his team-mate's finishing when capitalising on a loose pass from Cesar Palacios and slamming into the bottom corner from 25 yards, but that joy was short-lived.

In truth, there hadn't been much joy to behold all afternoon. The draw keeps both sides in the bottom half of the table, and that is where they will likely stay.

The first half, in particular, had very strong last-on-Match-of-the-Day vibes.

Newcastle thought they had a 33rd-minute lead when Dan Burn stole in at the near post to flick home from Murphy's low cross.

What the officials had spotted at the far post was linebacker Yoane Wissa pinning defender Timothy Castagne, and so playing Burn onside. It was the right call, even if Jaissle disagreed

'I learned that word here, a 'soft' decision. In my eyes, it was not right,' he said. 'But I was pleased with our complete commitment and togetherness.

'We grew through the game and that was excellent, something to build on. We showed the fundamentals.'

DEDIC-ATION

Dedic twice came close to creating goals with teasing crosses from the right, and you wondered if he would have mimicked Barnes' trademark archer celebration had they been converted.

He was kept away from the media post-match, but Jaissle did say: 'He played well, right? It (the bow & arrow incident) didn't affect him. He was not aware of the rules. We don't need to make a big deal out of it.'

KING CONCERN

Fulham's Josh King was included in Thomas Tuchel's England squad on Friday, the club's first Three Lions call-up in eight years. He, however, now needs a scan on a tight groin before learning if he's fit enough to feature.

Did the 19-year-old play like a would-be England international? He was his side's best player in the first half, even if that was a low bar to hurdle. One volley would have raised the roof had it gone in, so sweet was the connection from 20 yards. Lukas Hornicek needed every inch of his 6ft 6in frame to dive and save. And that, too, was a recurring theme, Newcastle's reliance on the big Czech to bail them out when giving up chances.

Like Newcastle, however, Fulham simply weren't good enough to take them.

Sports.title: Martin Odegaard sends Arsenal six clear at the top: The stylists and aesthetes will moan - but Mikel Arteta can rest easy over the international break, writes RIATH AL-SAMARRAI
Sports.content:
Martin Odegaard sends Arsenal six clear at the top: The stylists and aesthetes will moan - but Mikel Arteta can rest easy over the international break, writes RIATH AL-SAMARRAI

Arsenal are building a wall around their precious trophy with ugly bricks. While the stylists and aesthetes among us can moan about such details, a quick glance at the league table will be sufficient for Mikel Arteta to rest easy during the international break.

There are certainly things for him to improve. Masses of them. And we can all share the disappointment that the sum of such gifted parts is often quite underwhelming. There's a relentlessness about that conversation.

But Arsenal are relentless in other ways, too. Which is to say they are finding ways to win, with this their ninth in ten games and arguably the least convincing of an unconvincing bunch.

If Manchester City weren't facing up to the possibility of an apocalyptic punishment, those performances would likely cause greater concern but it's a tangential argument. A purist's debate. And by extension it is pointless against the single factor that matters most – scoring more than the other lot.

In this case, grimy as it was, that crowning role fell to Martin Odegaard, who nudged the winner over the line in the 72nd minute after benefiting from a favourable rebound after Konstantinos Tzolakis had saved from Noni Madueke.

The latter is surfing ever faster on the wave of his current form and impressed throughout this match, but his wing play and the resilience of Arteta's back four warranted isolated praise.

Martin Odegaard secured Arsenal's fourth Premier League win in succession against Hull

The Gunners had been frustrated by the newly-promoted side before Odegaard pounced

For all of Arsenal's grumbles about the officiating, including a bizarre penalty claim for Kai Havertz in the first half, they were poor, even if most sides would trade an arm for four straight clean sheets and a healthy lead in the table.

MATCH FACTS AND PLAYER RATINGS Arsenal (4-2-3-1): Raya 6; Timber 7, Konsa 7, Gabriel 6, Calafiori 7 (Hincapie 69, 7); Rice 6 (Merino 63, 7), Guimaraes 5 (Zubimendi 89); Madueke 8, Odegaard 7, Tzolis 5 (Eze 69, 6); Havertz 5 (Gyokeres 63, 6) Subs not used: Arrizabalaga, White, Mosquera, Lewis-Skelly Booked: Manager: Mikel Arteta 6 Hull (5-3-2-): Tzolakis 7; Coyle 6 (Norton-Cuffy 60, 5), Ajayi 7 (Herrington 69, 6), Egan 7, Mendy 6, Stroud 7 (Giles 75, 6); Iroegbunam 7 (Mouzakitis 75, 6), Gourna-Douath 7, Slater 7; McBurnie 6, Cho 5 (Gelhardt 60, 6) Subs not used: Butland, Giles, Thomas, Hjerto-Dahl, Vaz Booked: Coyle, Gourna-Douath Manager: Sergej Jakirovic 7 Ref: Farai Hallam 7

For the majority of the first 45 minutes, this game was shaped by Hull, who hadn't won since August. They had drawn five of their previous seven games and given up winning positions in four of them, but Sergej Jakirovic is doing good work. Here, he had Arteta baffled for long stretches and elements of his blueprint will have been noted by future opposition.

Jakirovic's intentions had been clear, both on the team sheet and the pitch. He kept with his default setting for a back five, but switched from a 5-4-1 to 5-3-2 and introduced Mohamed-Ali Cho to partner Oli McBurnie in attack.

It was the first time this season that Hull's manager has used a front two and dovetailed with his midweek warning that camping on the edge of their area would lead nowhere but trouble. Instead, the aim was to squeeze, suffocate and chase the champions at every turn. That worked for an hour for Leeds and it did likewise for Hull.

Inside the first 70 seconds, they had forced a corner. A moment later, John Egan outjumped Gabriel Magalhaes and headed into the side netting.

Soon enough, David Raya was forced into a save by Regan Slater. In landing a shot on target, Hull had achieved a greater threat after 18 minutes than Liverpool delivered in the entire 90 at Anfield last weekend.

It was strong stuff. And ballsy. Arsenal had space to exploit at the other end but that was contingent on having the composure to pick the right pass. For an awfully long time, that eluded them.

Christos Tzolis and Havertz each offered the limpest of protests for early penalties and Declan Rice belatedly caused some threat with a half-volley. For a while, that was as good as it got, before a third penalty appeal arrived. This one was contentious.

Arsenal were denied a penalty following a shirt pull on centre forward Kai Havertz

Mikel Arteta demands a free kick in Arsenal's favour on a frustrating afternoon in north London

Arteta tells wasteful Arsenal to be more 'chaotic' Mikel Arteta warned that Arsenal must be more 'chaotic' and ruthless after wasting multiple chances in their 1-0 victory over Hull City. Martin Odegaard's second-half strike sealed a fifth consecutive Premier League victory for the Gunners going into the international break, though his side were initially frustrated by the stubborn visitors. 'I'm delighted with the win because to go into the international break after winning is one of the best things for a coach or a player,' said Arteta. 'I think we were the better team and had enough chances to make the scoreline much bigger. We weren't efficient enough to do that. 'We need to find ways to be more efficient, sometimes even more pragmatic. 'Sometimes my feeling is that we are trying to score a perfect goal against these low blocks. We need to be much more chaotic than that, and that's it. And score much earlier because obviously that's going to change the course of the game.' Arsenal also had a penalty shout turned down in the first period after Kai Havertz's shirt was pulled in the box by Nobel Mendy. The decision was not given on field, though the VAR told referee Farai Hallam to look at the pitchside monitor. Hallam announced that Havertz had been fouled, but the forward had been in an offside position. On the incident, Arteta said: 'I haven't watched it back. I was surprised because when they sent the referee to the monitor, Benji (White) was telling me it's a clear penalty. 'So I heard now that they decided not to (give a penalty) because of the starting position of Kai, that he was offside. So I don't know what the interpretation is. I'm sure they (Pro Ref) will make that clear to understand it. 'I need to understand the decision, what is overruling what in terms of the decision making and after that I can give you an answer.' By Isaan Khan

The offence traced to a clear shirt-pull by Nobel Mendy on Havertz, with referee Farai Hallam subsequently called to the screen to check if it merited a foul. Returning to the field and engaging his microphone, he confirmed it did but added that Havertz was in an offside position. The verdict: a Hull free-kick.

A word on Hallam – he was the referee who also overruled the VAR on his Premier League debut last season. It's good to see an official who backs his own judgment, so fair play, but was he in the right?

Such is the mess engulfing the laws on offside, an argument could be put forward that, according to the regulations, the foul must take precedence over the offside as Havertz wasn't yet challenging for the ball. A counterpoint: it's an absurd law that is far too subjective.

None of which helped Arsenal, of course. Not for the first time, they were struggling to utilise their creative talents, with Rice and Odegaard swamped in the middle and their supply lines to Tzolis almost non-existent. Madueke created his own threats, but with limited support. When Havertz had a decent opening late in the half, he took one touch too many and allowed Mendy to challenge. It was bleak.

Kicking his heels on the bench was Viktor Gyokeres, who had one of his finest Arsenal performances at Slavia Prague on Wednesday. His reward for a goal and an assist was one of those soul-crushing demotions for Premier League business, and he wasn't introduced here for more than an hour.

By then, Arsenal had asserted some control. Tzolis was drawing countless fouls, including one from Lewie Coyle that ought to have drawn a second yellow card as Hull's pressure strayed closer to brute force. Their grip on a point was loosening.

First, Madueke drew a save from Tzolakis and then he forced another after skipping around Elliot Stroud and pulling the trigger. This one proved decisive because the save rebounded to Odegaard. He poached the winner.

Madueke then ought to have killed the match, but opted to round Tzolakis instead of taking on the shot when through. The keeper won that battle; Arsenal won the game. Ultimately, not much else mattered.

Sports.title: Man City's slump cannot be excused by guilty verdict: Too many blunders, too much arm waving and football problems are piling up after 3-1 defeat by Nottingham Forest, writes JACK GAUGHAN
Sports.content:
Man City's slump cannot be excused by guilty verdict: Too many blunders, too much arm waving and football problems are piling up after 3-1 defeat by Nottingham Forest, writes JACK GAUGHAN

This run will not be about the verdicts. This cannot be about the verdicts. Footballers do not care about these things, the stuff out of their control. Besides, all of them are earning cut-price transfers elsewhere were Manchester City to suffer relegation anyway. And cut-price fees mean bulkier salaries.

So to them the current climate, the circumstances around City – their recent history and their immediate future – does not overly matter. Sure, there might be the odd one who is slightly more philosophical and inquisitive about appeals and appendices but the majority won't be giving it much or any thought.

City insist on their innocence publicly and privately; until that changes, their players and Enzo Maresca carry on regardless. There were the usual jeers here, there were ditties about cheating, but that surely cannot affect them.

Instead, the performances over the past few weeks, this a third consecutive Premier League defeat and now sinking six points adrift of Arsenal, cannot be excused by the findings of an independent commission. The problems are football problems.

This is a squad who appear uncertain about specific aspects of their game. Namely how to build from the back – and that is prompting individual mistakes. It happened against Ipswich Town and at Aston Villa. On the river Trent, it was no different.

The statistics say City dominated another game and they deserved more but the eyes tell another story.

Man City are a squad who now appear uncertain about specific aspects of their game

The statistics say City dominated another game and they deserved more but the eyes tell another story

Three defeats in a row have seen Enzo Maresca's side slip six points behind leaders Arsenal

Too many errors. Too much arm waving. Too much feeling sorry for themselves when decisions go elsewhere. Oliver Glasner is not stupid, he will have seen examples of this play out in parts of City's victories as well as reverses.

As Liam Delap raced into the corner to celebrate his second with 17 minutes left – a huge day in his career against the club which moulded him – Glasner was dashing down the touchline with unbridled joy.

MATCH FACTS AND PLAYER RATINGS Nottingham Forest (5-2-2-1): Sels 6; Munoz 6 (Netz 65, 6), Cunha 8, Milenkovic 8, Murillo 7, Williams 8; Yates 8 (Sangare 79), Schlager 8; McAtee 7 (Ndoye 65, 6), Gibbs-White 7; Delap 9 (Jesus 87) Manager: Oliver Glasner 8 Man City (4-1-4-1): Donnarumma 5; Khusanov 5, Dias 5, Guehi 4 (Nunes 46, 7), Gvardiol 4 (O'Reilly 46, 6); Anderson 5; Ndiaye 6, Cherki 6, Fernandez 4 (Foden 78), Doku 6; Haaland 5 Manager: Enzo Maresca 5 Referee: Sam Barrott 6 Att: 30,762

Forest displays have deserved more than their points total so far and this was vindication for their fifth manager in 14 months, who suggested he fancied sampling Nottingham’s nightlife afterwards. Delap was exceptional, some personal redemption after criticism.

The way in which Glasner nudged James McAtee further forward, stationed higher from the off in order to pressurise the visitors, spoke to an idea that City arrived here ready to be ruffled and have been wearing a look of fragility.

By the time this was eight minutes shy of half time and McAtee was nicking possession from Elliot Anderson, drawing a foul that sparked another onslaught on Gianluigi Donnarumma's box, Forest were already two clear – and had been for some time. Phil Foden warmed up on the touchline, laughing and hugging with Callum Hudson-Odoi.

Forest preyed on City insecurities. A midfield structure that is simply not working at the moment, easily railroaded. A defence allergic to the basics and an epidemic of individual mistakes – either as a result of nervousness or blase attitude on the ball.

Straight to the mistakes. A real collection, these: the first in the fifth minute and the others 13 minutes afterwards. Jair Cunha wheeled away after picking Josko Gvardiol's pocket, meandering forward into the box and side-footing into the far corner largely unchallenged. Gvardiol seemed to have the air of a man who felt invincible when gathering possession before being eased off it.

Later, as Delap thundered forward 45 yards unchecked to hammer past Donnarumma, you wondered about the communication between these City players. Anderson and Iliman Ndiaye left things to each other near halfway, Xaver Schlager gave his thanks – finding Delap – and the City academy graduate bulldozed clear. Marc Guehi waved him through, Ruben Dias dithered and Maresca bowed his head.

Liam Delap was exceptional for Nottingham Forest, some personal redemption after criticism

Remarkably, this was the first time in seven years that City had gone two down inside 18 minutes

Remarkably, this was the first time in seven years that City had gone two down inside 18 minutes. Dias looked aghast at Guehi, who was then hooked at the break alongside Gvardiol. Erling Haaland and Rayan Cherki both stood in the centre circle, hands on hips.

It later emerged via replays that Anderson had been arguing with Abdukodir Khusanov in the build-up to Forest's opener as well, proof that City were nowhere near close to producing what was expected when on the ball in their own half.

Glasner had the weapons at his disposal to make this work but even the Austrian must have been surprised at the way in which they tickled City's soft underbelly. They had not scored at the City Ground all season. All change when owner Evangelos Marinakis made his first trip to see a game since Glasner's appointment, which felt particularly handy, with Yates having delivered a spinetingling dressing room speech pre-match.

Anger permeated the eyes of some City players as the whistle went. Cherki stormed down the tunnel, animatedly discussing how to play through Forest with Fernandez when they re-emerged.

Their lifeline came after 52 minutes, a Ryan Yates deflection from Jeremy Doku's cross sitting up for Cherki to hammer home a half-volley off the bar. Doku soon almost squeezed another effort past Matz Sels and the mood shifted, City briefly creeping menacingly like the monsters they are portrayed as.

Maresca had introduced Matheus Nunes and Nico O'Reilly, with both affecting the upturn. An admission of selection errors, perhaps, although O'Reilly is managing an ongoing back issue and is set for therapy on it over the international break.

City will need some of that as a collective. Delap won the ball inside his own third, gliding past Anderson, and Forest's explosive counter ended with Delap spearing a shot in off the post after Morgan Gibbs-White carried possession unopposed for 60 yards. Delirium, Glasner darting to the corner flag.

The quirk of this is that City's failings mean Manchester United drop into the bottom three.

Sports.title: Non-league footballer in stable condition after collapsing in warm-up and being rushed to hospital, leading to match being abandoned
Sports.content:
Truro City's match against Folkestone Invicta was abandoned due to a medical emergency on Saturday after a footballer collapsed during the warm-up.

Yassine En-Neyah, 26, was rushed to hospital in an ambulance after collapsing while preparing with his team-mates on the pitch. It was later confirmed he was in a stable condition.

The former Nottingham Forest academy youngster had been named among the substitutes to face Folkestone in the National League South game in Kent.

A club statement on Saturday read: 'Truro City can confirm that this afternoon's match against Folkestone Invicta has been postponed.

'Yassine En-Neyah required medical assistance during the warm-up and was transferred to the William Harvey hospital in Ashford for further treatment.'

The club added a welcome on Saturday night, saying: 'He is stable, sitting up and chatting, but will remain in hospital overnight under observation.

Truro City's clash with Folkestone Invicta has been abandoned due to a medical emergency

Yassine En-Neyah - pictured before the game - was named on the bench to face Folkestone

Club Statement:



Truro City can confirm that this afternoon's match against Folkestone Invicta has been postponed.



Yassine En-Neyah required medical assistance during the warm-up and was transferred to the William Harvey hospital in Ashford for further treatment.



We will… pic.twitter.com/IyiF2VIFMz — Truro City FC (@TCFC_Official) November 7, 2026

'The club would like to place on record its thanks to Truro City's medical staff, their counterparts at Folkestone Invicta, along with all club personnel from the home club.

'Both the National League and Football Association have also offered their help and support. There have also been many well wishes from Truro City fans and the wider football community too.'

Truro City's players had earlier gathered around the rear of the ambulance where En-Neyah was being treated to shield him from view.

The Moroccan-born former Republic of Ireland youth international began his career at Nottingham Forest, making his professional debut in January 2020 as a substitute during an FA Cup third-round clash against Chelsea.

After being released by Forest in 2021, the winger has played for multiple non-league sides including Shelbourne, Waterford and Maldon & Tipree.

Having briefly represented Truro in 2023, En-Neyah returned to the Tinners for a second spell in 2024, where he has remained since.

When he signed his new Truro contract last season, En-Neyah admitted he didn't think twice about the decision to stay.

'Truro's been my home for the last couple of seasons and it was a very easy decision,' he told BBC Radio Cornwall.

'I feel home so I just want to continue working hard and help the club achieve greater things.

'It wasn't a case of having to think about it, it was just a matter of getting it done and continuing to work hard and do well for the club and for myself.'

Sports.title: Nightmare in Brazil for Lewis Hamilton and Ferrari as penalty leaves him at the back of the grid after chaotic, rain-swept day of qualifying in Sao Paulo
Sports.content:
Nightmare in Brazil for Lewis Hamilton and Ferrari as penalty leaves him at the back of the grid after chaotic, rain-swept day of qualifying in Sao Paulo

Lewis Hamilton’s chance of making up for recent frustrations with a strong run in the Sao Paulo GP took a major blow after power unit penalties sent him to the back of the grid for Sunday’s race.

It also meant that he made only a token effort in the sort of soaking wet qualifying session in which he normally thrives.

The man who benefited most from the conditions was Lando Norris, who couldn't have anticipated that he would secure pole in Brazil. The McLaren driver put in a superb performance to be fastest.

'Today was a good day, we're on pole,' said the outgoing World Champion. 'A nice surprise in some ways. A good reward for the team, a good reward for myself.'

Hamilton is one of four star drivers from the leading teams to take a penalty hit at Interlagos, a legacy of reaching the last few races of a long season amid mounting mileage on tired and fragile engines.

In Hamilton’s case the drop is more serious than had been anticipated by his team.

Hamilton is one four star drivers from the leading teams to take a penalty hit at Interlagos

Ferrari decided to change the internal combustion engine on the cars of Hamilton and Leclerc

Ferrari decided to change the internal combustion engine on the cars of Hamilton and Charles Leclerc, knowing that they would have to take the plunge at some point.

That saddled both men with an initial 10-place drop – costly, but not disastrous given that Interlagos is a track where overtaking is at least possible.

However, in Friday’s final FP3 practice session Hamilton’s fresh V6 failed after just a few laps, obliging the former World Champion to take another complete new power unit.

That move accrued more penalties and consigned him to the back, where he joins Max Verstappen, whose Red Bull has undergone a similar wholesale change.

George Russell also drops five places after the Mercedes man took a new V6, having been second fastest in the wet qualifying session. His front row spot thus goes to team mate Kimi Antonelli.

It is far from over for Hamilton or Verstappen, but making it to the top three will require some good fortune. The Dutch driver pointed out that overtaking will be more difficult without the DRS tool that is no longer on the cars in 2026, and Hamilton agreed.

'I think overtaking will be very, very, very hard,' said the Ferrari ace. 'I'm not sure you're going to see the same sort of races that you've seen in the past.'

The penalties for so many top runners open up the possibility for better than anticipated results for those not affected and who made the most of the wet qualifying session – notably Kiwi Liam Lawson, who starts a surprise third for Racing Bulls.

Sports.title: Dejected Dimitar Berbatov has his head in his hands as he realises Man United are now in relegation zone - but admits old side DESERVE to be there
Sports.content:
Former Manchester United legend Dimitar Berbatov has blasted his old side, saying they deserve to be in the relegation zone.

United plunged into the bottom three on Saturday afternoon, perversely as neighbours Manchester City lost 3-1 away to Nottingham Forest.

The Bulgarian looked devastated when he was informed of United’s predicament while working on beIN Sports' coverage of the City game but still sounded hopeful that United could turn their form around.

When his attention was drawn to the Premier League table, the two-time Premier League winner initially had his head in his hands before saying: 'I don't believe it, but the way United are playing sometimes they deserve to be there honestly.'

Berbatov then took up a more positive tune saying: ‘Tomorrow they still have a game.'

United host Aston Villa on Sunday and after winning against Roma in midweek have the perfect opportunity finally to end their seven-game winless run in the league.

Berbatov could barely look at the table after United plunged into the drop zone

Berbatov won five major trophies as well as Premier League golden boot in four years at Manhchetser United

The fixture could prove either to be the nail in the coffin for United manager Michael Carrick or afford him more time after a woeful start to the season.

Berbatov won his two Premier Leagues alongside Carrick and will hope his ex-colleague can find a way to keep his job.

If he fails to guide his team to a victory against Villa it could be bleak for Carrick, as he has not been given any guarantees over his future beyond Sunday's game against Aston Villa.

Club chiefs handed Carrick more time to turn the club's season around following the 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth a fortnight ago amid speculation he could be replaced by Eddie Howe or Julian Nagelsmann.

In the two games since then, Carrick's side have lost at Chelsea and staged a rousing comeback over Roma in the Champions League to secure a first win in ten games.

But now the onus is on Carrick to build on the momentum gained from their Champions League victory.

Sports.title: Sloppy Wales scrape past Japan 28-21 and show return to top tier of rugby is wishful thinking... world class Louis Rees-Zammit was the only shining light, writes ALEX BYWATER
Sports.content:
Less than 24 hours after Mike Skinner of The Streets took to the stage in Cardiff, it was supposed to be so easy for Wales to brush aside Eddie Jones’ poor Japan.

Steve Tandy’s side did just enough to stay positive, though another unconvincing win over the Brave Blossoms was further confirmation that Welsh hopes of returning to international rugby’s top tier remain wishful at best.

A year on from having to rely on a last-gasp penalty to succeed in the same fixture, Tandy’s side huffed and puffed. On this evidence, the basics of their game – such as defence, ball retention and set-piece – still require significant work.

This was No10 against No12 in the world and it looked like it. Wales – for whom Louis Rees-Zammit was outstanding – should have won far more comfortably. But they were held back by seven handling errors in the first quarter and a struggling line-out.

The way Japan made ground on the occasions they had significant possession was also a big concern with New Zealand next. Wales have had some of PREM Rugby’s best performers this season. But here, they were not the sum of their individual potential.

‘Scoring for Wales means everything to me. But as long as Wales win, that's the most important thing,’ said star man Rees-Zammit. ‘Today wasn't perfect but it's definitely something to build on going into the next two games.’

Louis Rees-Zammit was outstanding but Wales were hampered by their handling errors

Coach Steve Tandy was honest in his verdict, saying Wales 'can't hide from the performance'

There were Welsh positives. Victories have been in short supply in this World Cup cycle

Wales coach Tandy was honest in his verdict. ‘It’s good to start the campaign with a positive result, but I can’t run away from the performance,’ he said. ‘There are definitely elements to improve. I thought we’d be a lot better than that. We’ll definitely enjoy it as winning isn’t something we have done a lot of. This team is building.

'They’re hungry to get better quicker. But it takes time. We could have made Japan work a bit harder.’

There were Welsh positives. Victories have been in short supply in this World Cup cycle and this was one. Wing Rees-Zammit was in a different class to the rest, scoring a try and providing a constant bright spark for his team.

The giant centre pairing of Max Llewellyn and Eddie James showed some promise and Josh Adams proved he still has signs of life with a brace. The hosts scored three first-half tries.

Rees-Zammit got a crowd of 50,425 off their feet instantly with a clean break and never let his standards slip from that high standard. ‘Louis wants to be one of the best wings in the world. He’s gone up a level,’ said Tandy. ‘The best teams have players who can create something out of nothing.’

Archie Griffin, Adams and Rees-Zammit all crossed, though Wales' concession of tries to Ben Gunter and Warner Dearns was all too easy. The second half was of poor quality.

Wales were once a team capable of beating the very best. Sadly, they are now Test also-rans.

MATCH FACTS Wales - Tries: Griffin, Adams (2), Rees-Zammit Cons: Costelow (3), Edwards Japan - Tries: Gunter, Dearns, Fukuda Cons: Saito (2), Komura Referee: Paul Williams (New Zealand) Attendance: 52,425 Star man: Louis Rees-Zammit (Wales)

‘There were massive parts of that game we let ourselves down on,’ said Wales captain Dewi Lake, bloodied and sporting stitches in his forehead. ‘Stop kicking the f****** ball,’ shouted one fan near the press box after the break, as the frustration grew at Wales’ inability to pull clear.

Adams’ second after Blair Murray countered saw them home, but it was a good job he did so as Wales conceded again before the end. Japan boss Jones will return to Twickenham to take on his old team England next week.

He felt his team did not get the ‘rub of the green’ from referee Paul Williams. ‘That could have been a historic win for us. But you’ve got to be good enough to make the most of the opportunities given to you and we weren’t,’ Jones said.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick reveals club bosses have not told him if he will still have a job next week, with Man United languishing in relegation zone ahead of Aston Villa clash
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick reveals club bosses have not told him if he will still have a job next week, with Man United languishing in relegation zone ahead of Aston Villa clash

Michael Carrick has not been given any guarantees over his future beyond Sunday's game against Aston Villa at Old Trafford as Manchester United dropped into the relegation zone.

United bosses handed Carrick more time to turn the club's season around following the 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth a fortnight ago amid speculation he could be replaced by Eddie Howe or Julian Nagelsmann.

In the two games since then, Carrick's side have lost at Chelsea and staged a rousing comeback over Roma in the Champions League to secure a first win in 10 games.

United slipped into the bottom three after Nottingham Forest beat Manchester City on Saturday, and could be in last place by the time they kick off against Villa depending on the outcome of other games involving Sunderland and Crystal Palace on Sunday.

The situation could leave Carrick's position under threat during the two-week international break. Asked if he has been told outright that he will be in charge next week, the United boss replied: 'No. Just carry on as absolute normal.

'Whatever is going to happen is going to happen. I'm really looking forward to the next game, playing at home on the back of the other night.

Michael Carrick revealed that club chiefs have not told him if he'll be in charge next week

Sir Jim Ratcliffe (left), Omar Berrada (centre) and Jason Wilcox (right) have not informed their manager about their plans for the international break

'The supporters are hopefully looking forward to coming energised and feeling good about what they might see, and we've got to repay that.'

Carrick is preparing for a normal international break, and doesn't have any plans to spend more time with his family after a turbulent period at Old Trafford.

'Not really different to normal. Genuinely not,' he added. 'I think international breaks are always a time to re-energise and freshen up. Some of the players that go away to internationals get freshened up in a different environment, but I don't really need it. I'm fine as I am.

'We'll certainly train next week and maybe have the weekend off. We'll see how that develops, who's left behind, who's with us and what they need.'

Carrick insisted that he and Bruno Fernandes have put any issues behind them after the United captain criticised his tactics in the Champions League defeat to Como last month.

After he led United's fightback against Roma in midweek by converting a twice taken penalty, Fernandes confirmed that Carrick's decision to drop him for the Bournemouth game was due to a loss of form, and disputed that the two men had a clear-the-air meeting over his comments.

But Carrick said: 'There are always conversations, bits going on; acknowledging certain things of when things are going well, what we need to improve on as a group.

'Sometimes it's individually, sometimes it's group. We always have discussions. What's actually said in that discussion, I'll keep that to myself.

'But I think it's pretty clear we've moved in a good direction, and Bruno's commitment is undoubted for me (in terms) of what he brings to this team and this club.

'He showed that again this week by his actions, the way he's played and how he dealt with even retaking the penalty and the frame of mind he was in for that. I think that tells you everything. Bruno's as good as ever.'

Crowd erupts into violence at Joshua Buatsi vs Willy Hutchinson boxing clash

The Joshua Buatsi-Willy Hutchinson rematch card was overshadowed after fans began clashing with one another in the crowd

View Image A brawl broke out in the crowd during Joshua Buatsi vs Willy Hutchinson (Image: DAZN)

A massive ringside brawl broke out at the AO Arena during the undercard of Joshua Buatsi vs Willy Hutchinson. Security rushed to intervene early on in Jack Rafferty's clash against Hovhannes Martirosyan.

‌



‌



Having first faced off in September 2024 for the vacant WBO Interim Light-Heavyweight World Championship, Buatsi and Hutchinson meet again on Saturday evening in a hotly anticipated rematch.

‌



Buatsi was the victor by split decision in the first bout and Hutchinson had campaigned for some time to secure the rematch. The vacant WBC Light-Heavyweight World Championship is the prize.

‌



However, whilst sparks fly in the ring, as the undercard got underway in Manchester, they flew in the stands. Rowdy spectators threw punches at each other.
