Sports.title: Hutchinson Wins WBC Title, Rea Stops Taylor
Sports.content:
Willy Hutchinson defeated Joshua Buatsi by unanimous decision to win the vacant WBC light heavyweight title, building an early lead and surviving a late scare in their rematch at Manchester’s AO Arena.

The judges scored it 117-112, 115-113 and 115-113 for Hutchinson (21-2, 14 KOs), whose switching between orthodox and southpaw gave Buatsi problems throughout the DAZN main event promoted by Queensberry. Buatsi (20-2, 13 KOs) finished strongly but left himself too much ground to recover.

Hutchinson had the better of the opening six rounds, changing stance and landing enough to keep Buatsi chasing the fight. The Scottish fighter continued to hold a narrow edge through the tenth, putting the pressure on Buatsi to produce something decisive over the final two rounds.

Buatsi finally had Hutchinson in trouble during the last minute of the eleventh. It was the opening he needed, but Hutchinson survived the round and used the ring in the twelfth, working from southpaw and picking his moments to jab.

Buatsi pressed forward and may have taken the final round, but his late rally could not overturn Hutchinson’s earlier work. Referee Victor Loughlin oversaw the contest.

Jack Rafferty (28-0-1, 18 KOs) earned a narrow unanimous decision over Hovhannes Martirosyan (20-2, 12 KOs) in the co-feature, with a controversial final-round knockdown proving crucial on two scorecards.

Martirosyan’s greater activity gave him the edge through much of the opening eight rounds. Rafferty suffered a cut over his right eyebrow in the tenth but fought back to take a close eleventh, leaving the contest heading toward a tense finish.

With blood running down his face, Rafferty caught Martirosyan with a right hand in the closing seconds of the twelfth. A push followed as Martirosyan went halfway through the ropes, but referee John Latham ruled a knockdown and administered a count as the bell sounded.

Two judges scored the fight 114-113 for Rafferty, while the third returned a wider 116-111 card. The knockdown supplied the winning margin on the two closer cards.

Gully Powar (14-1-1, 2 KOs) defeated Zack Miller (17-2, 3 KOs) by technical decision after their vacant British featherweight title fight was stopped at 1:32 of the tenth round.

Powar controlled the opening six rounds and continued to get the better of Miller, who developed swelling on his forehead following a clash of heads in the seventh. Referee Mark Lyson consulted the ringside doctor several times before the contest was halted and sent to the scorecards.

Bradley Rea (23-2, 12 KOs) delivered an emphatic finish against Ezra Taylor (13-2, 9 KOs), scoring two knockdowns to win the WBA Intercontinental light heavyweight title at 0:58 of the second round.

Rea dropped Taylor with a left hook to the chin, prompting a count from referee Michael Alexander. Taylor regained his feet, but Rea immediately attacked with a flurry that sent him down again and brought the stoppage.

Unbeaten middleweight Stephen Clarke (11-0, 2 KOs) controlled all eight rounds against Harley Collison (3-10-2). Referee Steve Gray scored the contest 80-72 for the Liverpool prospect.

Nineteen-year-old southpaw John Joe Carrigan (5-0, 5 KOs) maintained his perfect stoppage record, finishing Cheikh Diop (6-2, 4 KOs) at 1:50 of the fourth round of their scheduled six-round contest.

Javokhir Ummataliev (3-0, 1 KO) outlanded Atacayte Santana (4-4-2, 1 KO) throughout their six-round light heavyweight bout. Referee Mark Lyson awarded Ummataliev every round for a 60-54 victory.

Tumi Phillips (7-1, 1 KO) defeated Angelo Dragone (10-17-1, 1 KO) on points over four rounds. Dragone looked to hit and hold in the opener, but Phillips became more assertive in the second and third before an even final round. Lyson scored it 40-37.

Tony Yoka (16-3, 12 KOs) earned a six-round points victory over Kostiantyn Dovbyshchenko (10-22-1, 7 KOs). The 2016 Olympic super heavyweight gold medalist outlanded Dovbyshchenko through the first five rounds before the Ukrainian increased his activity in the sixth. Gray scored it 59-55.

Alex Arthur Jr. (6-0, 1 KO) completed a comfortable six-round win over Jose Aguirre (2-32, 1 KO). The Edinburgh southpaw controlled the contest throughout, winning 60-54 on Gray’s card.

Sports.title: Cheavon Clarke Overwhelms Chris Billam-Smith In London
Sports.content:
Cheavon Clarke punished Chris Billam-Smith with cleaner punches before dropping him twice for a seventh-round TKO on Saturday at London’s Copper Box Arena. The finish came at 1:24, giving Clarke the biggest victory of his professional career and handing the former WBO cruiserweight champion his first stoppage defeat.

Clarke (13-2, 10 KOs) was ahead on our card entering the seventh, but Billam-Smith (22-3, 14 KOs) had just produced his strongest round. A well-timed right hand abruptly ended that recovery, sending Billam-Smith down for the first time as a professional. He beat the count, only for Clarke to attack again and force a second knockdown that brought the referee’s intervention.

The scheduled 10-round main event at Zuffa Boxing 12 carried personal history. Clarke had beaten Billam-Smith twice in the amateurs, including in the 2016 National Championships final. Billam-Smith wanted to settle that old score, but instead suffered a more damaging defeat against the same opponent.

Clarke’s accuracy was the difference from the opening round. The fight began with holding and short bursts of action, but he found the cleaner punches, including a right hand just before the bell. Billam-Smith improved in the second, closing the distance and landing heavier shots while absorbing another solid right.

That success did not become a sustained pattern. Clarke took control in the third with combinations, then edged a tighter fourth through two late right hands. Billam-Smith remained competitive, but his forward movement too often failed to produce enough clean offense.

The difficulty was getting close without paying for the journey. Billam-Smith needed to bring his hooks and body punches into range, yet Clarke repeatedly found him before he could establish that position. Following Clarke around left openings for counters and allowed the more accurate fighter to decide when to engage.

A heavy right in the fifth supplied another warning. Billam-Smith took it without visibly wilting and answered with effective punches late, but Clarke was still landing the more damaging shots. The former champion’s durability kept him competitive without solving the problems that were costing him rounds.

The sixth offered Billam-Smith a route back. He increased his output and connected with hooks to the head and body, finally making his close-range work more consistent. We had Clarke ahead 58-56 after six, with Billam-Smith having won the second and sixth rounds.

Then Clarke turned a points advantage into a decisive finish. His right hand in the seventh broke through with enough force to put Billam-Smith on the canvas. Once the former champion rose, Clarke gave him no opportunity to settle, following up until the second knockdown ended the contest.

Both fighters had entered after June stoppage victories, with Billam-Smith beating Ryan Rozicki and Clarke overcoming two knockdowns to stop Jack Massey. Those results suggested danger on both sides, but Clarke delivered the sharper work here.

For Billam-Smith, the defeat was more severe than another missed opportunity for amateur revenge. His pressure worked in spells, but Clarke’s timing prevented him from building on it. Clarke now has a stoppage victory over a former world champion, earned after controlling much of the fight rather than relying on one isolated punch.

Sports.title: Willy Hutchinson Beats Buatsi To Claim WBC Title
Sports.content:
Willy Hutchinson’s sharper early boxing earned him the vacant WBC light heavyweight title, although Joshua Buatsi’s late rally made their rematch a close fight on Saturday at Manchester’s AO Arena. Hutchinson won a unanimous decision by scores of 117-112, 115-113 and 115-113, avenging his September 2024 defeat.

Hutchinson (21-2, 14 KOs) controlled the opening rounds with his lead hand, counters and movement. Buatsi (20-2, 13 KOs) eventually found success with pressure and body punching, but his stronger second half could not overturn the lead on the official cards. Neither fighter scored a knockdown.

The Scot established his preferred distance quickly. Buatsi went downstairs from the opening round, trying to slow Hutchinson and create opportunities for heavier punches, but repeatedly took clean shots while moving into range. Hutchinson held his ground when necessary, then moved or clinched before Buatsi could sustain an attack.

That pattern continued through much of the first four rounds. Buatsi followed Hutchinson without consistently cutting off his escape routes, leaving himself with too much distance to cover. Hutchinson could pick a shot, make Buatsi miss, and move away before the reply arrived.

The fourth was closer, but Buatsi still struggled to put combinations together. His heavier punching carried a threat, yet Hutchinson was landing more regularly and giving him few stationary targets.

Buatsi began changing the fight in the fifth. He reduced the space more effectively and landed cleaner punches inside, forcing Hutchinson to engage rather than box entirely on his own terms. A counter appeared to briefly stun Buatsi, but his body attack was becoming a more consistent source of offense.

The sixth brought further success downstairs, with Hutchinson looking to hold after taking shots. The Scot answered with a strong seventh, using sharp movement and a dipping left hook to the body to leave Buatsi chasing again.

Buatsi’s problem was the cost of getting close. When he followed Hutchinson in a straight line, the lead hand intercepted him before he could set his feet. When he backed Hutchinson up and stayed within punching range, his body work became far more effective. He needed to produce those moments more often in the early rounds.

By the eighth, Hutchinson was looking wearier under the pressure. Buatsi landed better inside and continued working through a competitive ninth, during which both men slipped without a knockdown being scored.

The closing rounds belonged increasingly to Buatsi’s forward pressure. He raised his activity, landed to the body and made Hutchinson defend for longer spells. The Scot’s output declined as he concentrated on moving away and limiting the damage.

Buatsi finished strongly in the 12th, marching forward and landing downstairs while Hutchinson offered fewer replies. That late surge made the verdict tense, with two judges ultimately separating them by just two points.

Our round-by-round card favored Buatsi 115-113, reflecting how much ground he recovered after the difficult start. The official verdict rewarded Hutchinson’s earlier accuracy, though the 117-112 card was considerably wider than the other two.

Their first meeting featured two knockdowns for Buatsi and a split-decision victory. This time, Hutchinson avoided the damaging moments that had cost him and banked enough early rounds to leave with his first world title. Buatsi’s finish showed what his pressure could accomplish, but he left too much of that work until the second half.

Sports.title: Denzel Bentley Drops Mosley Jr., Wins Close Decision
Sports.content:
Denzel Bentley’s knockdown helped him secure a close unanimous decision over Shane Mosley Jr. on Saturday, giving the London middleweight a hard-earned victory in his Zuffa Boxing debut. Bentley won by scores of 96-94, 96-93 and 95-94 after 10 competitive rounds at the Copper Box Arena.

Bentley (23-3-1, 18 KOs) hurt Mosley in the second round, but the American recovered sufficiently to keep the contest close through the final bell. Mosley (23-6, 13 KOs) had talked beforehand about wanting a clear decision victory on the road. Instead, he left with a defeat in which one judge separated the fighters by just a point.

The knockdown was a significant part of the result. On the narrowest card, that extra point supplied Bentley’s winning margin, illustrating how costly a single defensive mistake can become in a closely contested 10-round fight. Bentley’s power gave him a scoring advantage that Mosley’s work across the remaining rounds could not fully erase.

Mosley deserves credit for preventing the early trouble from becoming a stoppage defeat. Bentley has the punching power to finish a hurt opponent, but he could not turn his success into a comfortable evening. The American remained competitive and forced Bentley to keep working rather than allowing him to coast behind the knockdown.

Bentley’s pressure was another factor. Mosley wanted to demonstrate that he could outbox him, but doing so required more than surviving the heavier punches. He needed enough clean work to persuade the judges in rounds where Bentley was advancing and looking to impose his power.

That was the difficulty with Mosley’s pre-fight ambition of winning a wide decision. A fighter can have competitive rounds against a puncher and still lose ground sharply when he gets caught. Once Bentley had scored the knockdown, Mosley had less room to concede close rounds.

The scorecards reflected a competitive contest rather than a dominant performance. All three judges favored Bentley, but none gave him a wide margin. The 95-94 card was particularly tight, and the other two scores also left little room for Bentley to take his foot off the gas.

For Bentley, the victory followed an unsettled period outside the ring. He entered this bout after losing his WBO middleweight title status amid the dispute over his mandatory obligation to Yoenli Hernandez. Beating Mosley gave him a positive start with his new promoter, although this non-title contest did not replace the championship he had lost.

Mosley arrived after stopping Serhii Bohachuk in his previous outing, making this a setback to the momentum he had built. His durability kept him in contention, but the early damage and knockdown left him chasing points in a fight where the margins stayed narrow.

Bentley earned the result through his power and pressure, with the knockdown providing the clearest scoring advantage of the night. Mosley made him work for the decision, but could not produce the clear road victory he had promised.

Sports.title: Chris Billam-Smith vs Chev Clarke Live: Round-by-Round Updates From Zuffa Boxing 12
Sports.content:
Middleweight Denzel Bentley (23-3-1, 18 KOs) scored a knockdown on his way to a close 10-round unanimous decision over Shane Mosley Jr. (23-6, 13 KOs). The judges scored the non-title contest 96-94, 96-93 and 95-94.

Mosley was hurt in the second round, with Bentley’s punching power providing an early warning for the American. Bentley’s pressure helped him through a competitive fight, although Mosley remained in contention across the distance.

The knockdown proved particularly valuable on the tight scorecards, including one that separated them by just a point. Mosley had targeted a clear decision victory, but Bentley left with all three judges’ votes after a much closer contest.

Heavyweight Da’Mazion Vanhouter (14-0, 11 KOs) dropped Ivan Balaz (9-2, 7 KOs) three times en route to a first-round TKO in their scheduled eight-round bout. Vanhouter attacked the body with heavy punches, giving Balaz little opportunity to establish his own offense.

All three knockdowns came inside the opening two minutes as the unbeaten American overwhelmed his opponent. The referee stopped the contest after the third knockdown, ending a one-sided fight.

Balaz had previously troubled Johnny Fisher, but he could not withstand Vanhouter’s early assault. The 21-year-old recorded his eighth consecutive stoppage, continuing his run of quick finishes.

Light welterweight Kayla Allen (2-0, 1 KO) earned a hard-fought six-round points victory over Julia Igel (5-3, 4 KOs), with the referee scoring it 58-56. Both fighters threw freely from the opening bell, with Allen’s pressure forcing Igel onto the back foot.

Igel stood her ground often enough to land heavy replies, making Allen work throughout her second professional fight. Allen bloodied her opponent and maintained the higher volume, while Igel’s output dipped during spells.

The German southpaw continued firing back, but Allen landed effectively in the later rounds to secure the verdict. After stopping Edina Kiss on her debut, Allen gained valuable rounds against an opponent who tested her beyond the opening attack.

Middleweight Sam Hickey (7-0, 4 KOs) stopped Amaury Massenaux (16-5-1, 4 KOs) in the fifth round of their scheduled eight-round bout. Hickey controlled the action, taking his time to build his attack against the more experienced Belgian.

The Scot maintained steady pressure and inflicted mounting punishment without rushing his work. Massenaux stayed in the contest but could not do enough to disrupt Hickey’s control.

Hickey increased the intensity before the referee stepped in during the fifth to prevent further punishment. The 2022 Commonwealth Games gold medallist passed his latest test with a controlled stoppage victory in his seventh professional outing.

Light heavyweight Umar Dzambekov (15-0, 11 KOs) knocked out Zach Parker (26-3, 18 KOs) with a body shot at 1:47 of the fourth round in their scheduled 10-round bout. Parker had some early success with straight right hands and punches to the body, but Dzambekov repeatedly caught him with his arcing southpaw left.

The unbeaten Austrian’s ability to land that punch gave Parker problems despite the competitive start. Early in the fourth, Parker briefly went down after their legs tangled, with no knockdown scored.

Dzambekov then drove a left hand into the solar plexus, sending Parker to the canvas in pain. Parker could not beat referee Kieran McCann’s count, giving Dzambekov the biggest victory of his career.

Cruiserweight Lucas Roehrig (10-0, 6 KOs) stopped Connal McDonald (5-2, 1 KO) in the seventh round of their scheduled eight-round bout. Roehrig controlled the action with combinations and a sustained body attack, building a lead before forcing the finish.

McDonald struggled to interrupt his offense as Roehrig kept the pressure on. In the seventh, a barrage of unanswered punches drove McDonald to his knees and brought the referee in to stop the contest.

The Scottish Area champion represented a step up for Roehrig, who dealt with the test without needing the scorecards. Trained and managed by George Groves, the 23-year-old earned his sixth stoppage victory.

Featherweight Masood Abdulah (14-1, 8 KOs) scored two knockdowns to defeat Adan Palma (14-2) by an eight-round unanimous decision. The judges scored it 78-72, 77-73 and 76-74.

Abdulah dropped Palma with a short left hook in the opening minute, then used his jab and compact hooks to catch him coming forward. Palma fought his way back into the contest, landing heavy right hands in the fourth round that forced Abdulah to clinch.

A well-timed check left hook sent Palma down again in the sixth, slowing his attack and giving Abdulah more room to dictate the action. Abdulah worked behind his jab and continued finding the left hook over the final two rounds to secure the victory.

Vinnie Kemp (1-0, 1 KO) stopped Liam McElhinney (0-3) with a barrage of body shots at 2:33 of the opening round in their scheduled four-round middleweight bout. Making his professional debut, Kemp charged forward from the opening bell, throwing hard punches and goading McElhinney.

The referee briefly paused the action to warn Kemp about his verbals before allowing the fight to continue. Kemp resumed his attack, stalking McElhinney and driving punches into his midsection.

McElhinney bent forward and covered up against the ropes under the sustained body attack, prompting the referee to wave it off. Kemp’s aggression gave him a quick debut victory, although McElhinney offered little to test him.

Sports.title: Joshua Buatsi vs Willy Hutchinson 2 Live Results: Round-by-Round Updates
Sports.content:
Welterweight Jack Rafferty (28-0-1, 18 KOs) defeated Hovhannes Martirosyan (20-2, 12 KOs) by a 12-round unanimous decision to claim the vacant IBO title. The judges scored it 116-111, 116-111 and 114-113 after a hard-fought contest that saw both men land heavy punches.

Martirosyan boxed effectively off the back foot and enjoyed lengthy spells of success, while Rafferty kept pressing and throwing in volume. Rafferty scored a disputed knockdown in the 12th, with the incident drawing questions over whether a push had sent Martirosyan through the ropes.

That call proved crucial on the closest card, where Rafferty finished just one point ahead. Martirosyan’s late fade allowed Rafferty to finish strongly, but the unbeaten favorite had to work through a much tougher fight than the two wider scores suggested.

Bradley Rea (23-2, 12 KOs) knocked out Ezra Taylor (13-2, 9 KOs) in the second round to retain his WBA Inter-Continental light heavyweight title. The scheduled 10-round contest ended abruptly as Rea punished Taylor’s decision to trade early.

Taylor was dropped and appeared unsteady, raising questions about whether the referee should have ended the fight sooner. Rea finished the job with a heavy knockout, handing Taylor his second consecutive defeat. Taylor’s own punching power offered little protection once Rea had him hurt.

Coming off a stoppage win over Liam Cameron, Rea delivered another decisive finish to strengthen his position in the division.

Gully Powar (14-1-1, 1 KO) captured the vacant British featherweight title with a unanimous technical decision over Zak Miller (17-2, 3 KOs). The judges scored it 96-95, 97-94 and 96-94 after the scheduled 12-round contest was halted in the 10th.

Severe swelling on Miller’s forehead from accidental head clashes prompted the doctor to stop the fight and send it to the scorecards. Powar’s persistent pressure and punch volume helped him edge a competitive contest, with both fighters landing quality shots.

Miller remained willing to fight, but the swelling prevented him from getting the final two rounds to overturn Powar’s lead. Powar secured the Lonsdale Belt at his second attempt after drawing with Rhys Edwards in his previous British title challenge.

Middleweight Stephen Clarke (11-0, 2 KOs) defeated Harley Collison (3-10-2) by an eight-round points decision. Referee Steve Gray scored it 80-72, awarding Clarke every round. The Liverpool prospect controlled the contest and took a clear victory over the experienced Southampton fighter.

Collison completed the distance, giving the 25-year-old Clarke eight rounds of work. A former national amateur champion, Clarke is trained by Stephen “Swifty” Smith and managed by Paul Smith. This was another step in his professional education, although stronger opposition will provide a better measure of his progress.

Junior middleweight John Joe Carrigan (5-0, 5 KOs) stopped Cheikh Diop (6-2) in the fourth round to maintain his perfect knockout run. The 19-year-old southpaw secured the finish against an opponent who had previously lost only by decision.

Diop entered with more professional experience but became the fifth fighter unable to go the distance with Carrigan. The Carlisle teenager turned professional in late 2025 after winning gold at the Under-19 World Championships.

He trains in Hartlepool and has carried his amateur success into a promising start with Queensberry Promotions. The official time of the stoppage was not immediately available.

Tony Yoka (16-3, 12 KOs) defeated Kostiantyn Dovbyshchenko (10-21-1, 7 KOs) by a six-round points decision in their heavyweight bout. The reported score was 59-55 for the Frenchman.

Yoka controlled the contest, although the Ukrainian veteran took him the distance. Dovbyshchenko has also gone the rounds with Moses Itauma, making this a predictable opportunity for Yoka to get some work.

The 2016 Olympic gold medalist is rebuilding after consecutive defeats to Martin Bakole, Carlos Takam and Ryad Merhy. This victory kept that process moving, but beating an opponent with Dovbyshchenko’s record offers little evidence of how Yoka would fare against contenders.

Javokhir Ummataliev (3-0, 1 KO) defeated Atacayte Santana (4-4-2, 1 KO) by a six-round points decision in super middleweight action. The referee scored it 60-54, giving the Uzbek all six rounds. Ummataliev controlled the contest and secured a clear win in his third professional appearance.

Santana completed the distance after entering as a clear underdog. The 21-year-old Ummataliev arrived in the professional ranks with a strong amateur background, including a 2025 World Championship gold medal. After stopping Damian Drabik in two rounds in his previous outing, he gained more rounds of professional experience against Santana.

Super middleweight prospect Alex Arthur Jr. (6-0, 1 KO) defeated Jose Aguirre (2-32, 1 KO) by a six-round points decision. Referee Steve Gray scored the contest 60-54, awarding Arthur every round.

The 24-year-old Scot controlled the fight and finished with a clear victory over the experienced Costa Rican. Aguirre completed the distance, giving Arthur six rounds of work in his sixth professional outing.

Arthur is the son of former WBO super featherweight champion Alex Arthur. The win provided more experience, although Aguirre’s lengthy losing streak limits what it tells us about the unbeaten prospect.

Tumi Phillips (7-1, 1 KO) defeated Angelo Dragone (10-17-1) by decision in their super lightweight bout. The referee scored it 40-37 for Phillips.

Phillips controlled the contest and was a clear winner at the finish. The younger fighter produced a solid showing against an opponent with considerably more professional experience.

Dragone heard the final bell after suffering a stoppage defeat in his previous outing. No knockdowns were reported, with Phillips taking the victory without any major drama. The official score was not immediately available.

Sports.title: Da’Mazion Vanhouter Floors Ivan Balaz Three Times In TKO Win
Sports.content:
Da’Mazion Vanhouter (14-0, 11 KOs) overwhelmed Ivan Balaz (9-2, 7 KOs) with three first-round knockdowns, using a destructive body attack to secure a TKO victory on Saturday at the Copper Box Arena in London. The scheduled eight-round heavyweight contest lasted less than two minutes before the referee stopped it following the third knockdown.

Balaz had previously dropped Johnny Fisher, but he never established that kind of threat against Vanhouter. The 21-year-old American attacked early and repeatedly put him on the floor, turning a potentially dangerous opening round into a brief, one-sided fight.

Much of Vanhouter’s damage came downstairs. His body punching gave Balaz more to defend than shots aimed at the head, and the repeated knockdowns left the Slovak without enough time to recover or build an attack of his own. By the third trip to the canvas, there was little reason to continue.

The result extended Vanhouter’s stoppage streak to eight and followed his recent victories over Raphael Murphy and Raphael Akpejiori. His British debut provided another example of his early finishing power, although the speed of the victory limited what could be learned about his ability over longer fights.

Balaz’s previous performance against Fisher gave this matchup some interest. An opponent who has already hurt a bigger-name heavyweight presents an obvious risk if a prospect leaves himself open while chasing a knockout. Vanhouter removed that risk quickly by making Balaz defend from the outset.

The body attack was the most encouraging part of the performance. Young heavyweight punchers can become too focused on landing one spectacular shot upstairs, especially when opponents begin retreating or covering up. Attacking the torso gives them a larger target and can punish a defensive guard that protects the chin while leaving the ribs and midsection exposed.

Against Balaz, Vanhouter’s approach produced immediate results. The knockdowns arrived too quickly for the fight to settle into anything resembling a competitive contest. Balaz needed an opportunity to interrupt the American’s offense, but he could not create one before the referee intervened.

Vanhouter’s physical progression also makes him an unusual heavyweight prospect. Having begun his professional career near 154 pounds, he has developed into a fighter weighing more than 230. That change makes future opposition particularly relevant: stronger heavyweights who can absorb his opening attack will provide a better indication of how his power and conditioning hold up together.

Those questions remain for later fights. Balaz could not take Vanhouter beyond the opening round, much less force him to adjust after several rounds of resistance.

For this outing, Vanhouter completed the job emphatically. Three knockdowns and a sustained attack to the body gave him another early stoppage, keeping his unbeaten record intact and providing a clear reason to increase the difficulty of his next test.

Vanhouter is already drawing inevitable comparisons to Moses Itauma. Same age bracket, identical trail of early bodies, and the usual promoter machinery hyping him as the next heavyweight savior. The difference is Itauma actually stepped up, and Filip Hrgovic quickly proved what happens when an explosive kid runs into a granite chin that doesn’t fold in two minutes.

That is why nobody should get carried away by Vanhouter’s demolition of Ivan Balaz. Smashing an overmatched target to the ribs is easy work. Dropping a guy three times inside two minutes tells you zero about how Vanhouter reacts when somebody takes his best shot, walks through the fire, and makes him fight backward. Beating up a hurt fighter is a world away from surviving a dogfight.

If Vanhouter is going to become what his backers claim, he needs opponents who come to fight, not collect a check. Racking up highlight-reel knockouts against soft touches looks great on social media, but Itauma learned the hard way what happens when you skip the learning curve. Vanhouter handled business, but until he finds someone willing to fire back, we have no idea how good he actually is.

Sports.title: Moses Itauma Wants Hrgovic Revenge, Warren Requires Top-10 Test
Sports.content:
Moses Itauma wants another shot at Filip Hrgovic, but Frank Warren says he must reestablish himself first. The promoter is targeting a top-10 heavyweight for Itauma’s comeback, although the opponent’s style will reveal far more than a ranking number about how effectively that fight prepares him for revenge.

Warren hopes to announce Itauma’s return next week. Hrgovic also has mandatory business to complete against Frank Sanchez, leaving Itauma with a rebuilding job while the title picture plays out.

“Well, that’s what he’d like. He asked for that immediately, and it’d be a big event. There’s no doubt about it,” Warren told BoxNation regarding an Itauma-Hrgovic rematch. “Sold out last time. I’m sure if we put it on again, it was so exciting a fight, it would sell out again. But first of all, he’s got to reestablish himself, and Filip’s got to get rid of his mandatory against Sanchez.”

Asked what level of opponent he wanted for Itauma’s return, Warren answered: “Top 10.”

That sets a high bar on paper, yet it reveals little about the specific technical hurdles Itauma will need to clear. A top-10 ranking covers vastly different tactical challenges. Pairing him with someone like Bakhodir Jalolov would force Itauma to solve height, reach, and distance management against a towering southpaw who dictates range behind a long jab. That offers a valuable puzzle, but it represents a different examination from the physical pressure that broke him down against Hrgovic.

A veteran like Joseph Parker represents the opposite stylistic end. Parker possesses the durability to absorb clean contact, the veteran craft to work on the inside, and the sustained output to test whether Itauma can defend while moving. Backing up in straight lines leaves a fighter vulnerable to being marched into the ropes. An opponent with Parker’s engine would compel Itauma to pivot off the centerline, escape off the back foot, and reset ring position rather than settling into a simple linear retreat.

A useful return bout must also address what happens at the end of his combinations. Against an opponent who fires back through incoming punches, Itauma cannot afford to admire his work with his chin exposed or his guard down. A fighter who punches between exchanges will compel him to roll, tuck his chin, or slip out of range the moment his offense concludes.

Pacing remains just as central to his development. Itauma built his reputation on early knockouts, but burning through his reserves trying to blast out a durable contender carries obvious hazards. A test against someone capable of taking solid contact would force Itauma to establish his jab, vary his punch selection, and bank rounds without exhausting himself in search of a single finish.

Warren does not need to throw him into another firefight to achieve those ends. Another loss would derail the rematch entirely. The trick is finding an opponent who makes Itauma solve the specific stylistic puzzles Hrgovic presented while still offering a clear route to a confidence-building win.

Sanchez could alter that landscape before Itauma gets his second chance. Warren noted that Sanchez previously stepped aside to permit the initial bout and now holds mandatory status. Should Sanchez take the belt, avenging the loss to Hrgovic and pursuing the world title will point in different directions.

Queensberry would then have to weigh whether a grudge match carries enough commercial appeal without the hardware on the line. For Itauma, the immediate priority remains narrower: overcome an opponent who asks enough difficult questions to make a second meeting with Hrgovic truly winnable.

Putting Itauma right back in with Hrgovic after a single confidence builder is a classic promotional trap, and history shows that rush rarely ends well for a young fighter.

At 21, Itauma suffered the exact kind of loss that leaves scar tissue. Being carried out on a stretcher after emptying his entire gas tank through eight rounds reveals a deficit you cannot patch up in one training camp. Hrgovic did not just beat him on points; he broke him physically and mentally by weaponizing his granite chin, size, and steady, chopping output.

Hrgovic’s pre-fight psychological read proved spot on: he openly predicted that Itauma had never faced real adversity, had never felt what happens when his best shots fail to stop a man, and would drown in deep water. Itauma swept early rounds, but by round eight, he had completely redlined trying to force a finish.

Once Hrgovic survived the storm, Itauma had zero tactical fallback. Going back into the ring with a 6’6″ puncher who now knows he can absorb everything Itauma throws and outlast him is handing Hrgovic the psychological blueprint on a silver platter.

One tune-up does not solve that kind of problem. A single soft touch or showcase fight lets a fighter look explosive again, but it teaches him nothing about pacing in rounds nine through twelve, managing energy against someone who refuses to go down, or handling heavy incoming shots when fatigued.

If Warren matches him with a hand-picked opponent who folds inside four rounds, Itauma steps right back into a Hrgovic rematch with the same structural flaws that got him stopped in August.

Itauma needs two or three genuine developmental bouts against durable, grinding heavyweights who make him work every minute of ten or twelve rounds without handing him an early exit. He has plenty of time on his side. Rushing him into an immediate rematch to salvage a narrative risks cutting a potentially elite career short before it even gets off the ground.

Ghana News.title: BoG Governor Johnson Asiama says professional journalism is vital in fighting digital misinformation
Ghana News.content:
Bank of Ghana Governor, Dr Johnson Pandit Asiama, has described professional journalism as “society’s compass”, saying it remains essential in helping citizens navigate the growing challenges of the digital age.

Speaking at the 30th Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Media Awards in Accra on Saturday, November 7, 2026, he said technological advancements had transformed how information is created, distributed and consumed, presenting both opportunities and challenges for society.

Dr Asiama noted that while digital platforms had expanded opportunities for citizens to participate in public discussions and share information, they had also contributed to the spread of misinformation, disinformation, online abuse, misleading data and hate speech.

“Although digital platforms have created unprecedented opportunities for citizens to get involved and share information, they have also brought significant challenges, including misinformation, disinformation, online abuse, misleading data and hate speech,” he said.

The Governor said professional journalism plays a critical role in helping citizens distinguish facts from falsehood, evidence from speculation and informed analysis from sensationalism.

He described journalists as guardians of public discourse whose work contributes to social cohesion, informed debate and the protection of democratic principles.

“As guardians of public discourse, journalists are essential for building social unity, encouraging well-informed discussions, and safeguarding democratic principles,” he stated.

Dr Asiama also highlighted the media's role in making complex economic and financial issues accessible to the public.

He cited monetary policy decisions, inflation trends, financial sector reforms, exchange rate movements and digital financial innovations as issues that require accurate and balanced reporting to help citizens understand developments affecting their lives.

He said effective journalism translates such technical subjects into information that the public can understand and use.

The 30th GJA Media Awards were held under the theme, “Celebrating Excellence, Advancing Media Freedom and Combating Hate Speech in the Digital Age”.

The theme highlights the need to protect press freedom while promoting responsible journalism in an increasingly digital information environment.

The Bank of Ghana has also pledged to continue supporting initiatives that recognise excellence in economic and financial reporting.

Ghana News.title: Egypt sacks coach Hossam Hassan over ‘negative impact’ on team image
Ghana News.content:
Egypt coach Hossam Hassan was sacked on Saturday for what the soccer federation cited as “a negative impact on the positive image of the team.”

The Egyptian Football Association did not elaborate in a statement, adding only that “maintaining the team’s stability is a paramount priority” that cannot be compromised.

Egyptian media believed the decision had more to do with Hassan’s personal life than rumors of disagreements with Egyptian players, including star forward Mohamed Salah.

Egypt’s Supreme Council for Media Regulation banned Hassan last week from appearing in all media outlets, an unprecedented decision against a national coach. That followed disputes in Hassan’s personal life becoming public.

Hassan was appointed Egypt coach in 2024 and became the first former Egypt player to coach the national team at a World Cup this year. Egypt was knocked out by Argentina in the last 16.

The EFA immediately replaced Hassan with Ali Maher, a long-time head coach in the Egyptian Premier League currently leading fourth-placed Ceramica Cleopatra.

Maher must get quickly up to speed. Egypt plays Malawi on Nov. 13 and 17 in qualifying for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations. Egypt leads Group B.

Ghana News.title: BoG introduces economic and financial journalism award with international training opportunities at 30th GJA Media Awards
Ghana News.content:
The Bank of Ghana (BoG) has announced a new award scheme to recognise excellence in economic and financial journalism, offering winners opportunities for international exposure, professional training and further studies.

The Governor’s Economic and Financial Story of the Year Award was announced by Bank of Ghana Governor, Dr Johnson Pandit Asiama, in a speech he personally delivered at the 30th Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Media Awards at the Palms Convention Centre, La Palm Royal Beach Hotel, Accra, on Saturday, November 7, 2026.

The package includes sponsorship for the winner to attend either the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank Spring Meetings or Annual Meetings, a laptop computer and a one-year internet data subscription.

It will also provide access to professional fellowships with institutions such as the Thomson Foundation, the Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism and accredited local journalism training centres.

Other opportunities include scholarships for further studies in media, communications and related fields, as well as professional exchange programmes with international media organisations such as Bloomberg and Reuters.

“Our objective is simple: to invest in the development of journalists who can continue to elevate the quality of economic and financial reporting in Ghana,” the Governor said.

The Governor described the media as an essential partner in helping the public understand economic and financial developments.

He noted that issues such as monetary policy, inflation, financial sector reforms, exchange rate movements and digital financial innovations could be complex, making accurate and accessible reporting important to public understanding.

“It is through accurate, balanced, and insightful reporting that these issues are translated into information citizens can understand and use,” he said.

The Governor also emphasised the importance of effective communication in central banking, saying public understanding of the Bank's policies was critical to their effectiveness.

“Our policies are most effective when they are clearly understood by the public. Transparency, credibility, and accountability require open and effective engagement with all stakeholders, including the media,” he said.

The award forms part of the Bank’s efforts to encourage specialised reporting on economic and financial issues and promote greater public understanding of developments in the sector.

It is expected to provide journalists with opportunities to build their reporting skills and deepen their knowledge of issues that affect businesses, households and the wider economy.

Ghana News.title: Real Madrid beat Valencia to move level on points with leaders Barcelona
Ghana News.content:
Real Madrid moved level on points with La Liga leaders Barcelona after a comfortable victory at struggling Valencia.

Captain Federico Valverde opened the scoring in the 28th minute with a crisp, low drive from 20 yards after Kylian Mbappe's free-kick came back off the wall.

Eight minutes later, Jose Mourinho's side doubled their advantage as Arda Guler volleyed in from six yards after Jude Bellingham's cutback was deflected kindly into his path.

The visitors remained in control in the second half and the result was put beyond doubt 15 minutes from time when Guler found Mbappe, who rounded the goalkeeper to score his 13th league goal of the campaign.

It only got worse for Valencia as captain Jose Gaya was sent off for scything down Mbappe with the striker set to streak clear on goal.

A fourth straight league win means only goal difference keeps Real off top spot, although Barca can restore their three-point advantage when they play third-placed Atletico Madrid on Sunday (20:00 GMT).

Valencia stay 19th, a point from safety, after a seventh league defeat from 12 games.

The game was paused nine minutes into the first half to allow players and fans to pay tribute to Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel, who died after suffering a serious injury during a Spanish second-division match, with a minute's applause.

Ghana News.title: Government renews commitment to unravel Ahmed Suale’s murder – Kwakye Ofosu
Ghana News.content:
The government has reaffirmed its commitment to unraveling the murder of investigative journalist Ahmed Suale, whose killing in January 2019 remains unsolved.

Speaking on behalf of President John Dramani Mahama at the 30th GJA Media Awards in Accra, Minister of State in charge of Government Communications, Felix Kwakye Ofosu, said journalists in Ghana had lost their lives in the pursuit of accountability.

He cited the killing of Mr Suale, an investigative journalist with Tiger Eye PI, and said the government remained committed to finding those responsible.

“Journalists in our country lost their lives in pursuit of accountability, and I refer to the unfortunate killing of Ahmed Suale, whose murder remains unsolved, and the government remains committed to unraveling it,” he stated.

Mr Kwakye Ofosu also acknowledged the dangers faced by journalists who publish reports considered uncomfortable by powerful interests.

He referred to journalists in the northern part of the country who, he said, had to flee for their lives after publishing such reports.

“Our words in support of free speech must not ring hollow, especially when in the north, through the past, journalists had to flee our country for fear of their lives because they published uncomfortable truths,” he stated.

Ahmed Suale was shot dead in Madina, Accra, in January 2019. He was part of the Tiger Eye PI investigative team and had worked on investigations into corruption and other matters of public interest.

His killing remains unresolved, with the GJA and other media stakeholders continuing to call for justice.

The government's latest pledge comes amid broader concerns about journalist safety and the need to protect media practitioners from intimidation and attacks.

Mr Kwakye Ofosu said the government remained committed to pursuing the circumstances surrounding Suale's murder and protecting journalists across the country.

Ghana News.title: Ghana Tennis Federation boss, Aboagye Duah, elected as West Africa Prez & Veep at Tennis Africa
Ghana News.content:
LUANDA, ANGOLA, 7 November 2026 — Ghana has secured a significant leadership position in African tennis following the election of Mr Isaac Aboagye Duah, President of the Ghana Tennis Federation (GTF), as President of the West Africa Zone and Vice President of Tennis Africa.

Mr Duah was elected unopposed at the Tennis Africa Annual General Meeting held in Luanda, Angola, filling the vacancy created by the passing of former Zone President, Ing. Ifedayo Akindoju Dayo, last year. In accordance with the Tennis Africa Constitution, the position was filled through an election at the next AGM.

The West Africa Zone comprises 15 countries. Mr Duah’s election presents an opportunity for Ghana to contribute more directly to continental tennis governance and for the sub-region to strengthen cooperation in developing the sport.

A Record of Inclusive Leadership

Mr Duah has served as President of the Ghana Tennis Federation since 2017. His tenure has focused on inclusive governance, stakeholder engagement, and creating opportunities for the growth of tennis.

Two significant initiatives stand out. First, he championed the recognition of players, coaches, officiating officials and clubs as delegates at the highest decision-making body of tennis governance in Ghana, ensuring that key stakeholders have a voice in shaping the sport’s future.

Second, he has promoted an open-door policy that creates an enabling environment for tennis clubs and foundations to operate, partner with the Federation and organise internationally recognised World Tennis competitions.

Under his leadership, Ghana has participated in West African junior competitions over the past nine years, achieved notable success in African 12-and-under competitions, and continued to represent the country in the Davis Cup and Billie Jean King Cup.

Mr Duah also serves on the African Cup of Nations Sub-Committee of Tennis Africa, contributing to the development of continental tennis.

A Vision for African Tennis

Commenting on his election, Mr Duah said:

“I am deeply honoured by the confidence placed in me and humbled by the opportunity to serve tennis across West Africa and the African continent. My leadership philosophy has always been anchored in inclusion, collaboration and the belief that tennis can only grow when players, coaches, officials, clubs and foundations are recognised, valued and given a meaningful voice.

“I look forward to bringing this spirit of inclusive leadership to Tennis Africa. Working with our 15 West African member countries and stakeholders across the continent, we can strengthen our institutions, develop our players and officials, attract greater investment and create sustainable opportunities for the next generation. My vision is for an African tennis community that is united in purpose, strong in governance and increasingly competitive on the world stage.”

His new responsibilities will provide an opportunity to promote stronger cooperation among national federations, expand junior development, strengthen institutional capacity and encourage investment in tennis infrastructure and competitions.

Academic Background

Mr Duah is an alumnus of the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), where he obtained a Bachelor of Science degree in Chemistry. He also holds an Executive Master of Business Administration (EMBA), a Master of Arts in Leadership and Management, and a Chartered Institute of Marketing (CIM-UK) qualification as a Chartered Marketer.

He received his secondary education at Pope John Senior High School and Minor Seminary in Koforidua.

His election marks an important milestone for Ghanaian sports administration and offers an opportunity to strengthen the country’s contribution to tennis development across West Africa and the continent.

The Ghana Tennis Federation congratulates its President on his election and looks forward to his continued service to the sport at both national and continental levels.

Ghana News.title: Government does not expect favourable headlines from media – Kwakye Ofosu
Ghana News.content:
The government has reaffirmed its commitment to media freedom, saying it does not expect favourable headlines from journalists as a condition for engagement with the media.

Speaking on behalf of President John Dramani Mahama at the 30th GJA Media Awards in Accra, Minister of State in charge of Government Communications, Felix Kwakye Ofosu, said the media must be free to question government, scrutinise public expenditure, investigate public institutions and examine decisions taken by public officials.

He said the government recognises that a democratic administration must be prepared to respond to difficult questions and accept legitimate criticism.

“We do not expect favourable headlines as a condition for engagement, nor do we expect journalists to surrender their editorial independence in the name of partnership. Indeed, a government that is confident in its democratic credentials must be prepared to answer difficult questions and accept legitimate criticism,” he stated.

Mr Kwakye Ofosu said journalists must be allowed to criticise government when it falls short, acknowledge achievements when they are delivered and demand explanations whenever the public interest requires it.

“The media must be free to criticise whenever there's a shortfall, acknowledge achievements when we deliver, and demand explanations whenever the public interest requires it,” he said.

The Minister also highlighted the need to protect journalists from attacks, threats and unlawful detention while carrying out their professional duties.

He said allegations of attacks, including those involving security personnel, must be investigated and accountability pursued where wrongdoing is established.

“No journalist should be assaulted, threatened, or unlawfully detained for undertaking a legitimate professional assignment. Allegations of attacks, including those involving security personnel, must be investigated, and where wrongdoing is established, accountability must follow,” he stated.

The comments come amid concerns about the safety of journalists and the state of media freedom in Ghana.

The Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) has recorded more than 50 incidents involving attacks, arrests and harassment of journalists between 2022 and January 2026.

The government says it will continue to work with media stakeholders to ensure that constitutional guarantees of freedom of expression and media independence are reflected in the everyday experiences of journalists.

Ghana News.title: Threatening to kill the President and his children is criminality, not free speech – Kwakye Ofosu
Ghana News.content:
Minister of State in charge of Government Communications, Felix Kwakye Ofosu, has described threats to kill President John Dramani Mahama and his children as “brazen criminality”, insisting that such conduct must not be defended in the name of free expression.

Speaking on behalf of the President at the 30th Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Media Awards in Accra, he urged political leaders not to support threats and incitement to violence for partisan advantage.

“For instance, threatening to kill a president and his children is not free speech. It is brazen criminality. We, as political leaders, must not lend support to this level of criminality only because it enures to the benefits of our political fortunes,” he said.

Mr Kwakye Ofosu said political leaders must demonstrate consistency in their defence of free speech, particularly when journalists face threats for publishing critical or uncomfortable reports.

“Our words in support of free speech must not ring hollow, especially when in the north, in the past, journalists had to flee our country for fear of their lives because they published uncomfortable truths,” he stated.

The Minister stressed that efforts to combat hate speech should not become a justification for restricting dissent, critical journalism or unpopular opinions.

He said democracy depended on the freedom to disagree, but should not accommodate deliberate incitement of hatred, violence and intolerance.

“Democracy thrives on disagreement, and what it cannot accommodate is the deliberate incitement of hatred, violence, and intolerance. A clear distinction must be struck between criminal conduct and the expression of free speech,” he said.

The comments were made at the 30th GJA Media Awards, held under the theme, “Celebrating Excellence, Advancing Media Freedom and Combating Hate Speech in the Digital Age.”

The event brought together journalists, media organisations and other stakeholders to recognise excellence in journalism and discuss issues affecting media freedom.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Real Madrid beat Valencia 3-0 to draw level with La Liga leaders Barcelona
World.content:
Valverde and Guler’s first-half goals put Madrid in the driving seat, and Mbappe added a third in the second half.

Share Real Madrid beat Valencia 3-0 to draw level with La Liga leaders Barcelona on social media

Kylian Mbappe scored for the seventh match running as Real Madrid pulled provisionally level on points with La Liga leaders Barcelona after a 3-0 win at 10-man Valencia.

Reigning champions Barca visit Atletico Madrid, third, on Sunday, aiming to move back clear of the chasing pack.

Jose Mourinho’s Madrid largely dominated at Mestalla Stadium on Saturday, securing an eighth win in a row across all competitions.

Federico Valverde and Arda Guler’s first-half goals put Madrid in the driving seat, and Mbappe added a third in the second half.

Los Blancos were without winger Vinicius Junior, who was serving the final game of a four-match ban.

Madrid have thrived in his absence, putting heavy pressure on Barca, whom they beat in the Camp Nou Clasico on October 25.

In the ninth minute, the match stopped for players and fans to pay tribute to Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel, who tragically died on Tuesday.

Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois made a smart save to deny Aaron Mayol, who had picked Aurelien Tchouameni’s pocket in a dangerous area.

Valencia’s Guido Rodriguez had a goal disallowed for offside before Mourinho’s side took control.

Valverde drilled Madrid ahead from outside the area after Mbappe’s free kick was blocked by the Valencia wall and fell to the Uruguayan.

Guler soon doubled the lead after Jude Bellingham’s cross was deflected kindly into his path.

Guler had a good chance for the third early in the second half, but Valencia goalkeeper Stole Dimitrievski grabbed the ball as the midfielder tried to round him.



Minutes later, Dimitrievski saved well from Mbappe, as the French striker ran through and tried to dink the ball over him.

Bellingham powered through the defence and was also denied by the goalkeeper, as was Mbappe, who followed up with an overhead kick, as Madrid tried to find a third to kill off the game.

Eventually, Mbappe produced it, bursting onto a dangerous pass by Guler to dart past Dimitrievski and squeeze home his 13th league goal of the campaign.

It was the forward’s 17th goal in 16 games across all competitions. Mbappe has netted in his last seven appearances for Madrid.

Valencia’s Jose Gaya was dismissed with about 10 minutes remaining for a late sliding foul on Mbappe to further spoil Javier Aguirre’s team’s night.

Earlier, new Espanyol coach Eder Sarabia’s side were held to a goalless home draw by Deportivo A Coruna.

Osasuna snatched a late 1-1 draw against Athletic Bilbao, while Racing Santander came from behind to beat Malaga 2-1.

World.title: Who is behind Europe’s suspected hybrid attacks?
World.content:
Bomb hoaxes and supermarket cyberattacks are heightening security fears.

Italy says civilian infrastructure in Europe is “under attack”.

A series of bomb threats this week grounded flights and put airports on high alert. No explosives were found, and the threats appear to be false.

But the disruption is not limited to aviation. Hackers have also targeted supermarket freezers in several countries, raising temperatures and spoiling food.

Together, the incidents are raising fears and questions about a wider campaign of hybrid attacks.

Who could be behind these threats? Are they connected? And can European nations come together to counter these acts of aggression?

World.title: What we know so far after Krakow gun attack
World.content:
Six people - four women and two men - are confirmed to have been killed, including a British national. Three victims are Polish and two have not been identified.

Sixteen people, including five foreigners and the attacker, were taken to hospital. Among those being treated are two police officers who were shot while detaining the attacker. The interior ministry later said they were from Britain, Austria, Russia, Germany and Portugal.

Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk later named the injured officers as Senior Constable Jakub Kulik and Senior Constable Artur MoraÅski.

Tusk said three bodies - two women and one man - were found at the gunman's house when it was searched after the attack.

One of the police officers was described as being in a "very critical condition" by a Polish government minister after being shot three times while arresting the attacker. The officer is undergoing surgery, he added.

Polish authorities have not confirmed the names and ages of the other victims.

World.title: Israel's president tasks opposition leader Eisenkot with forming government
World.content:
Israel's president says he will task opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming a new coalition government.

Isaac Herzog has been holding talks with political parties after neither Eisenkot's bloc nor that of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu secured a majority in Israel's parliament, known as the Knesset, following last week's election.

Eisenkot will now have 28 days to try to form a new administration, with a potential 14-day extension.

"Now is the time to form a national emergency government. I will do everything to ensure we are worthy," the former military chief wrote on X.

No political party in Israel has ever won an outright majority, meaning all governments have been coalitions.

Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party and its far-right and ultra-Orthodox Jewish allies won 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, while Eisenkot's centrist Yashar party and three other Jewish opposition parties in his bloc won 48.

Two Arab-led alliances, the United Arab List and the Joint List, together won an unprecedented 19 seats following a surge in turnout among Arab voters.

That positions them as potential kingmakers. However, all but one of the Jewish parties pledged before the polls not to work with them to form a government.

Herzog said that, after consulting all parties during the week, he would give Eisenkot the first chance to form a government.

A statement from the president's office said he had informed both Eisenkot and Netanyahu of the decision.

Following consultations with delegations from the incoming Knesset members, Eisenkot received 67 recommendations for the premiership and Netanyahu 46, the statement said.
