— Kasey Williams

World.title: Manning Cup quarterfinalists decided
World.content:
In this file photo, Kingston College’s Deshawn Byfield (left) and Mona High’s Jermaine Morgan vie for the ball during the ISSA Walker Cup final at Stadium East. (Photo: Naphtali Junior)

Former champions Jamaica College (JC), Mona High and Wolmer’s Boys were the last three qualifiers to the ISSA Manning Cup quarterfinal following the final set of games in the round of 16 on Saturday.

JC drew 1-1 with Eltham and finished second on five points in Zone 4. Eltham won the group with seven points. Norman Manley defeated Tivoli Gardens 4-2 and grabbed third place with three points. Tivoli Gardens ended with a point.

In Zone 1, defending champions Excelsior came from behind to beat St George’s College 2-1 and consolidated their position at the top with nine points. The Light Blues finished at the bottom with a point.

Mona High booked their spot with a comprehensive 4-0 win over St Catherine High and finished with six points and second spot in Zone 1 as St Catherine were eliminated with a point in third spot.

Wolmer’s Boys blanked Hillel Academy 2-0 and finished second in Zone 3 with six points and into the last eight. St Andrew Technical High School (STATHS) topped the group with maximum nine points after whipping St Jago High 5-0.

Kingston College defeated Calabar 1-0 to top Zone 2 with maximum nine points. Calabar, who had already qualified for the quarterfinal, were second with six points.

The quarter final pairings have been decided with Group A consisting of Excelsior high, Eltham High, Wolmer’s Boys and Calabar High while Group B will have KC, STATHS, Mona and JC.

–Howard Walker

World.title: NWC customers miss out on $50m
World.content:
SOME National Water Commission (NWC) customers missed out on hundreds of dollars in compensation as the utility paid only $23.76 million of the $73.78 million potentially available for breaches of its Guranteed Standards during the 2025–2026 financial year.

The shortfall of approximately $50 million is outlined in the Office of Utilities Regulation (OUR) 2025–2026 Annual Report, tabled in Parliament on Tuesday.

The report shows that the NWC committed 14,817 breaches of its Guaranteed Standards during the period April 1, 2025 to March 31, 2026.

But the utility paid just 32 per cent of the potential compensation its customers should have received.

Among the reasons cited for the non-payment were customers failing to submit the required claim forms and NWC receiving relief from the Guaranteed Standards following Hurricane Melissa in October 2025.

The OUR excused the utility from meeting certain service requirements between October 24 and December 31, 2025, because of the disruption caused by the Category 5 storm.

This meant the utility could avoid paying compensation for breaches covered by that relief during the period.

The report also disclosed that, in March 2026, the NWC requested a further six months of relief, beginning January 1, 2026. At the end of the reporting period, that request was still under review, with the OUR indicating that a decision would be issued in the next financial year.

The Guaranteed Standards are service requirements that utility providers are expected to meet. Where a provider breaches an applicable standard, affected customers may qualify for compensation, subject to the relevant conditions and procedures.

The NWC’s compensation figures form part of wider concerns about customer service and unresolved complaints recorded by the OUR during the financial year.

The OUR said it received 3,558 contacts from consumers about utility services during the period, of which 1,168 related to the NWC. These included complaints, enquiries, and other matters brought to its attention.

At March 31, 2026, the NWC also accounted for 251 of the 625 complaints that remained open across all utility providers, representing 40 per cent of the outstanding cases.

The report found that billing disputes and service interruptions were the leading reasons consumers contacted the OUR, accounting for 48 per cent and 18 per cent of all contacts, respectively.

The regulator also noted that it had secured approximately $21.34 million for customers through investigations of appeals and complaints during the financial year.

The NWC accounted for the largest share, paying approximately $9.45 million for consumers, or 44 per cent of the total. The OUR said it would continue reviewing the NWC’s request for additional relief in the following financial year.

The utility recently applied for a 51 per cent tariff increase which is to be considered by the OUR.

World.title: Labourities riding westJLP forgoes customary public rally at National Arena for scaled-down conference in MoBay
World.content:
The sea of green at the public session of the JLP’s 2023 annual conference which will not be repeated this year as only delegates will be invited to the conference to be held in Montego Bay, St James. Karl McLarty

NO National Arena spectacle, no sea of supporters bussed from across the island, no grand public rally.

The Jamaica Labour Party (JLP) will again scale back its 2026 annual conference, opting for a delegates-only business meeting in Montego Bay on November 15.

JLP Deputy Leader Desmond McKenzie, who announced the decision at a media conference at the party’s headquarters on Belmont Road in New Kingston on Friday, said the party recognised that although thousands of Jamaicans had received assistance through the Government’s response in the wake of Hurricane Melissa one year ago, much more needs to be done.

“In that vein of recognising the moment and the mood of a section of the country, in respect of our annual conference we have chosen to forgo the usual spectacle which we have had at the National Arena in Kingston,” said McKenzie.

He said the annual conference will be held at the Montego Bay Convention Centre in St James, beginning at approximately 10 am, with about 6,000 delegates expected to attend.

The decision means there will be no customary mass public meeting, with the party saying it wants to show solidarity with Jamaicans who are still struggling more than a year after the Category 5 storm, particularly those in western Jamaica which was among the areas hardest hit.

According to McKenzie, the decision to scale down the conference was based on a recommendation from the party’s officers, which was approved by its central executive, with the conference instead taking the form of a business session to address internal party matters, political issues, and its role in the recovery effort.

McKenzie explained that prime minister and Party Leader Dr Andrew Holness is expected to address the conference at approximately 1:30 pm, with his speech to be open to the media and broadcast live.

But, McKenzie underscored that the rest of the conference’s business will take place behind closed doors, with attendance restricted to party delegates.

Meanwhile, JLP Deputy General Secretary Dr Andrew Wheatley told Friday’s media briefing that the party’s constitution requires it to hold an annual conference, which is traditionally a business meeting involving delegates.

He said the large public gathering usually associated with the event is a separate public session. Wheatley said the party had chosen to hold the business meeting in Montego Bay to engage stakeholders and workers in western Jamaica who were affected by the hurricane. “We want to empathise with the people, those affected by Hurricane Melissa, especially those in western Jamaica. So we wanted to forego the celebratory aspect of our annual conference and deal with a private business session that will afford us the opportunity to programme political activities, do a self-assessment as to where we are as a political party, and engage the most important members of the party — the delegates of the party — as we…take decisions for not only the betterment of the Jamaican Labour Party but, by extension, the people of Jamaica,” Wheatley said. He also urged delegates to participate actively as the party prepares for the next local government elections. Leadership changes will also be on the agenda, with the private session expected to include elections for the party leader and deputy leaders. Wheatley said the party understood that supporters would miss the usual opportunity to gather and celebrate its achievements, but argued that the circumstances required a different approach. JLP Chairman Robert Montague defended the decision, saying the party had a responsibility to identify with Jamaicans who were still dealing with the effects of the hurricane. He rejected suggestions that the JLP was copying the Opposition People’s National Party (PNP), which held the public session of its 88th annual conference at Independence Park in Savanna-la-Mar, Westmoreland, on Sunday, September 20, after moving the event from its usual venue at the National Arena in Kingston. “As a party that cares and as the national party of this country and the party that forms government, we also have a responsibility — a responsibility to those who are still suffering and who are still recovering from the hurricane. We have a responsibility to provide mature leadership to the country. [We] say, rather than jollyficate with some while some persons are struggling, let us identify with our brothers and sisters who are struggling,” he said. “You will also note that the party leader, who is prime minister, has basically put the country on notice that it is time we as a nation begin to tighten some belts, to cut some expenses in order to bring relief to those who are suffering. So, it’s a mature decision and it’s a decision if we did not take, our members and supporters would have condemned us,” Montague added.

World.title: Decide verdict on evidence, judge tells jury in Ruddock murder trial
World.content:
Taneka Gardener was allegedly murdered on the orders of Kevin Smith at Kingdom Restoration Ministries in Albion St James.

JUSTICE Leighton Pusey has implored the seven members of the jury in the Andre Ruddock murder trial not to arrive at a verdict based on anything they have heard outside of court, but, rather, to stick to the evidence.

Pusey began his summation to the jury on Friday morning in the Home Circuit Court, downtown Kingston, after the prosecution and defence teams finished their cases and gave their closing addresses to the jury on Thursday.

Pusey indicated from early that he would not be rushing his summation and spent a couple hours going over some of the evidence which was presented during the trial and gave the jurors instructions on how to approach their decision after some 10 witnesses testified during the trial which began in September.

Ruddock is on trial for murder in relation to the October 17, 2021 killing of Taneka Gardner at Pathways International Kingdom Restoration Ministries in St James.

Gardner was killed in what is said to have been a human-sacrifice ritual and it is alleged that Ruddock cut her throat on instructions from the now-deceased Pastor Dr Kevin Smith.

“Despite the fact that Mr Ruddock is here, he is presumed innocent. What this means is that you can’t take into consideration anything else that you may have heard or know of him, or anything that might be in terms of his circumstances. The only thing you look at is what has been said in court.

“And what has been said in court must be sufficient to satisfy you that he is guilty beyond a reasonable doubt before you can come to a verdict of guilt. In other words, he doesn’t have to prove to you that he didn’t do anything,” Pusey told the jurors.

“He doesn’t have to prove to you that he is a good person. He doesn’t have to prove to you that he is a nice person or not. That does not matter. He is innocent like any other citizen in the country from anywhere else. And therefore, you cannot start a case with anything in terms of what you have heard or anything else. The only thing that you’re going to be looking at is the evidence and the evidence only,” Pusey warned.

The judge emphasised that the accused has no requirement, no need in law, to prove that he did not do anything.

“He’s been charged with murder and in law, we define murder as the unlawful killing of a person. And so, for the purposes of that definition of law, these are the things that you need to look at. You have to first come to the conclusion of whether the person was killed.

“That is why you — not just the persons who say something — but you have a post-mortem and you also have seen, heard the evidence of the person who identified the body. So if you remember, you heard from Taneka Gardner’s father and he indicated that this is his daughter and he said that he identified the body and went to the post-mortem. So therefore, you have the evidence that Taneka Gardner died,” Pusey said.

“But also, more importantly, you have the evidence of the doctor who did the post-mortem and he gave you in great detail exactly what happened to her and what caused her death. So, in this circumstance, you have clear evidence that somebody died and that person died from a cut to the throat. It was not an accidental death, or something like that. That she was killed by somebody who cut her throat.

“The one question that you need to come to in this case is whether or not that particular person who killed her is in jail. As I said, it is not necessary for us to go through and try to find out all the things that happened on that day. Who did what. Who was good and who was bad. What we are trying to determine is whether or not Andre Ruddock was the person who killed Taneka Gardner,” added Pusey.

The judge is expected to complete his summation on Monday, which will pave the way for the jurors to begin their deliberation and return a verdict.

World.title: Alarm at Mount Alvernia High
World.content:
The entrance to Mount Alvernia High School in Montego Bay.

Principal points to gastro; students question food safety

MONTEGO BAY, St James — Principal of Mount Alvernia High School Kayon Whyne has sought to allay fears that there are food safety issues on the campus after a number of students became ill at the institution on Thursday, with a few having to seek medical treatment.

The all-girl school is awaiting results of a probe by the St James Health Department, but the educator suspects a stomach bug may have caused symptoms including vomiting and diarrhoea among several students, mainly from the lower grades. School was dismissed early Thursday, and only students from grades 10 to 13 were allowed to attend classes Friday.

“Monday, we will be back to normal. Some of the students would have wanted to come in on Friday but we took the decision,” Whyne told the Jamaica Observer Friday afternoon.

“They are in classrooms now, grade seven to nine are in online learning, the teachers are meeting with them,” she added.

When contacted the parish’s Chief Public Health Inspector Shericka Lewis confirmed that an investigation had been launched into the matter.

“We’ve gotten a preliminary report, not the fulsome report, we are still investigating,” she told the Observer Friday afternoon.

“We got a report yesterday and dispatched a team,” Lewis added, referring to the department’s initial response.

Lewis provided an initial assessment of the situation without identifying a possible cause.

“It was predominantly vomiting amongst several students,” she said.

Jitters have been rippling through the school and among concerned parents since Thursday as rumours swirl about what could have caused discomfort among those affected. According to an email from concerned students, some of their peers became ill after eating meals purchased at school.

“Several students reportedly experienced symptoms, including vomiting, after consuming food from the school canteen,” the message said.

“What makes this situation particularly concerning is that the reports are not limited to students who consumed cooked meals. Students who purchased other food items, including patties, have also reportedly experienced illness,” it continued.

Questions were also raised about why some students were allowed to return to school on Friday when the cause of the illness had not yet been confirmed.

“If the school has been deemed safe, students and parents deserve clarification on why certain year-groups are being advised to remain away while others are expected to continue attending,” the email said.

“Furthermore, what specific measures have been implemented to ensure that students who are still required to attend are not exposed to potential health risks,” it added.

The students insisted that they deserve to have confidence that the food purchased at school is safe.

“The school canteen is an essential part of the daily school environment, and maintaining appropriate food safety standards should never be treated as optional,” said writers of the emailed message.

The principal’s approach has been to treat the issue as gastro, a common ailment in schools and other closed environments such as cruise ships and nursing homes. According to Whyne, they issued a gastroenteritis alert to parents and classes were dismissed early Thursday as a precautionary measure.

But up to Friday she was still puzzled about what really happened to the girls in her care.

“We buy patties from two stores, so I don’t know. The students ate patties and I am telling you there are other parents who gave their children packed lunches for school and they would have experienced the same thing. We don’t know if it’s airborne or waterborne, we don’t know,” the school principal told the Observer.

“The health inspectors, they were just here and they say that it’s inconclusive but they are doing tests. I just had my lunch and no impact,” she added.

About 50 to 70 per cent of gastro outbreaks are caused by viruses. However it can also be caused by bacterial contamination of food and water, or passed from person to person. Gastro is typically spread when tiny particles of stool or vomit from an infected person get onto hands, surfaces, food, or water, and are then transferred to the mouth.

Whyne said two students were given medication intravenously (IV) but they are back home.

One parent confirmed that his ninth-grader was among those who became ill Thursday.

“A pure vomit she a vomit, them say she cannot come to school today. Well, most of the school have to stay home,” he told the Observer Friday.

He said he was monitoring his daughter’s condition to determine whether she would need medical attention.

The treatment regime for gastro involves small, frequent sips of liquid; gradual reintroduction of bland food; and rest. Medical care is recommended if there are signs of severe dehydration and an inability to keep any liquids down for 24 hours.

World.title: ‘45 years of Joy’
World.content:
Back row: (from left) Vice-principal of Siloah Primary Janice Larmond; Dr Joy Spence, Appleton Estate master blender; Principal Oneil Larmond; and Vice-Principal Cynthia Morris. Front row (from left): Head Boy Ammere Atkinson, Head Girl Emeika Williams, Marlonae Harriott, deputy head boy; and Kymarley Brown, deputy head girl; at the JOY45 Handover Ceremony at Siloah Primary School.

STUDENTS and teachers at Siloah Primary School are set to benefit from improved drinking water storage, classroom cooling, and teaching resources following a donation valued at $1.9 million, as part of Dr Joy Spence’s 45th anniversary celebrations at J Wray & Nephew Limited.

The contribution — made through the J Wray & Nephew (JWN) Foundation and Appleton Estate — included two 1,000-gallon water tanks for drinking water storage; 18 water stands with a supply of five-gallon water bottles; three smart televisions with wall mounts; 24 wall-mounted fans for six classrooms; and a water testing kit.

The water tanks will strengthen the school’s drinking water storage capacity, while the water stands and bottled water will support access throughout the school day.

The fans are intended to create more comfortable conditions for students, including those preparing for their Primary Exit Profile examinations, and the smart televisions will provide additional classroom teaching resources.

The handover continued a relationship that began five years ago during the ‘40 Years of Joy’ initiative, which introduced a breakfast feeding programme for primary schools surrounding Appleton Estate in St Elizabeth.

During her visit to Siloah Primary at that time, Spence was struck by Principal Oneil Larmond’s commitment to the school and the warmth of its students, inspiring her to continue supporting the institution.

Earlier this year, that support included a commitment to provide feminine hygiene supplies for girls in grades five and six throughout the year. This latest donation builds on that relationship by addressing practical needs that affect students’ comfort and readiness to learn.

“My passion is for education, and I always support causes for education through the foundation, through scholarships, and initiatives such as this. This donation responds to everyday needs that can make a real difference to a child’s school experience.

“Having drinking water readily available, cooler classrooms, and technology to support teaching can help students feel more comfortable and better able to concentrate on learning,” said Spence.

“As I celebrate 45 years with J Wray & Nephew, it is deeply rewarding to share that milestone in this way. Through the JWN Foundation, scholarships and initiatives such as this, I hope to continue helping young people access the support and opportunities they need to fulfil their potential,” added Spence, Appleton Estate’s master blender.

The school’s welcomed the contribution and acknowledged the continued support of Spence and the JWN Foundation.

“Total joy when Dr Joy Spence is around. We are extremely happy for her donation of water drums, water coolers, wall fans and smart televisions. This has transformed our learning environment, allowing our students and staff to work more effectively. This will enhance the performance of all our students. Special thanks to Dr Joy Spence and the JWN Foundation for always being there for our school and community,” said Larmond.

Education has been a meaningful thread throughout JOY45, which celebrates Spence’s journey from joining JWN as chief chemist in 1981 to becoming the first female master blender in the spirits industry in 1997.

Alongside the Siloah Primary contribution, an anniversary dinner at The University of the West Indies, Mona, on October 15 acknowledged scholarship recipient Cara Fraser, connecting the celebration of Spence’s achievements with opportunities for another generation.

The school handover brought that commitment into the community surrounding Appleton Estate, marking the anniversary with practical support for students and the educators guiding them.

World.title: CHASING THE DREAM
World.content:
SPEID... victory on aggregate will help not only to get to the semi-finals of the Nations League and qualify to the Gold Cup, but also helps us in World Cup ranking (Photo: Joseph Wellington)

SITTING calmly at the head table, Jamaica’s Head Coach Rudoph Speid set a tone of pragmatic realism and intense focus as he unveiled his 23-man squad to face Concacaf powerhouse Mexico in a pivotal two-legged Nations League clash, aiming to qualify for the regional showpeice — the Gold Cup.

The Jamaicans are set to host Mexico on Friday, November 14, at the National Stadium at 8:00 pm, and then travel to Mexico for the second leg on Tuesday, November 17 in Monterrey at 9.30 pm Jamaica time.

The winner of the two-legged tie will advance to the semi-final of the Nations League and by extension gain an automatic spot in the Concacaf Gold Cup.

“Victory on aggregate will help not only to get to the semi-finals of the Nations League and qualify to the Gold Cup, but also helps us in World Cup ranking for the World Cup Qualifiers in 2030. So it’s a very important game for us,” Speid pointed out during the press conference.

“What is important in this particular game, which is very significant, is that video assistant referee (VAR) will be on display,” Speid noted with a faint smile.

“They are using VAR in both games. I mean I must tell you that we have no luck with VAR so far, but let’s see,” he added.

Speid, who took charge of the Reggae Boyz in November 2025, almost one year in the hot seat, announced his 23-man team including one newcomer, Denzel Hall of Rotherham United in League Two in England.

The 25 year-old Hall, who plays right back, previously represented The Netherlands youth teams from Under-15 to Under-17 between 2015 and 2017. Hall is of Jamaican parentage.

“He was always someone that we were watching. But at this particular time, you know, there’s a real shortage of players in that position and he has done well enough to get a call-up. And we decided to call him to see what he could do. He learned his football in the Dutch League,” said Speid.

Sixteen players are returning from the last window in this 23-member squad: Andre Blake, Amal Knight, Richard King, Miguel Freckleton, Joel Latibeaudiere, Christopher Ainsworth, Kyle Ming, Ronaldo Webster, Brandon Cover, Courtney Clarke, Karoy Anderson, Kaheim Dixon, Ronaldo Cephas, Javon East, Tyreece Campbell, and Damion Lowe.

The other players are goalkeeper Jahmali Waite, Kevon Lambert, Tyrese Hall, Dwight Merrick, Warner Brown and Khori Bennett.

If goalkeeper Blake is selected for both games he will achieve 100 caps for Jamaica.

Speid explained why Leon Bailey and Dujuan Richards were not included.

“…When you come to a play-off game you have to be sure of every single person that you put in that squad because we only have 23 and if you have people that are doubtful and you bring them in you could end up with a lot less players than you really need. And I am telling you, in this particular game, players have to be fit. Mexico is no joke. It’s like playing two away games.

“So, you know, you have to look at the risk. We’re getting people that are not 100 per cent as against somebody who’s playing every single day, day in, day out and putting up very good performances,” said Speid.

The Regage Boyz enter the tie on an upward trajectory, still number one in the Caribbean, sitting sixth in the Concacaf and 69th globally. Mexico are 59 spots ahead, coming in at number 10 in the world.

Jamaica holds four hostorical victories over Mexico and Speid is under no illusions regarding the magnitude of the task ahead.

“A team that is ranked 10th in the world is no joke. We understand the type of monster we’re up against. But that is why the games are being played. They are not unbeatable. You just have to be on your best game and you need a little luck too,” he pointed out.

The players should arrive for camp between November 8 and 9.

World.title: Ein Spaziergang mit Bodo Ramelow
World.content:
Share on LinkedIn

Share on WhatsApp

Share on X

Share via email

Die Welt spielt verrückt, doch im Präsidium des Bundestages herrscht überraschende Einigkeit. Bundestagsvizepräsident Bodo Ramelow (Die Linke) gibt im Gespräch mit Gordon Repinski einen seltenen Einblick in die überparteiliche Zusammenarbeit, auch bei Nachtschichten. Dabei wird deutlich, mit welcher Strategie das Gremium den Provokationen der AfD begegnet.

In seiner eigenen Partei brodelt es derweil gewaltig. Ramelow findet deutliche Worte zur Antisemitismus-Debatte innerhalb der Linken und kritisiert das taktische Lavieren einzelner Abgeordneter. Warum er trotzdem eine Gesinnungsprüfung ablehnt, aber klare rote Linien beim Existenzrecht Israels zieht, offenbart die tiefe Zerrissenheit seiner Partei.

Zudem verrät er, warum die Wahrnehmung der Linken im Bundestag derzeit auch von der Gruppe der „Silberlocken“ abhängt, wie sich die Silberlocken regelmäßig absprechen und warum er sich trotz aller Krisen nicht verrückt machen lässt.

Mit den Linken, aber auch der SPD und den Grünen beschäftigt sich auch der neue Podcast von POLITICO und WELT. In „Inside Links“ geht es jede Woche darum, wie in Deutschland womöglich eine neue linke Mehrheit entsteht, zu welchem Preis und wer künftig dabei möglicherweise am Regierungstisch sitzen könnte. „Inside Links“ gibt es auf den Podcast-Plattformen zu hören und zu sehen, unter anderem auch hier.

Das Berlin Playbook als Podcast gibt es jeden Morgen ab 5 Uhr. Rixa Fürsen, Maximilian Stascheit und das POLITICO-Team liefern Politik zum Hören – kompakt, international, hintergründig.

Für alle Hauptstadt-Profis: Der Berlin Playbook-Newsletter bietet jeden Morgen die wichtigsten Themen und Einordnungen. Jetzt kostenlos abonnieren.

World.title: Merz’s conservatives poised to nominate Germany’s first woman president
World.content:
President of the Bavarian parliament Ilse Aigner arrives at the Christian Social Union party congress in Munich, on Oct. 23, 2026. | Alexandra Beier/AFP via Getty Images

BERLIN — Bavarian politician Ilse Aigner is set to become Germany’s next president, making her the country’s first woman to hold the office, according to two senior conservatives with knowledge of the matter.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s conservative bloc and the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD) will nominate Aigner to succeed outgoing German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, the officials told BILD, which, like POLITICO, is part of the Axel Springer Global Reporters Network. Both officials were granted anonymity to discuss internal party matters freely. Aigner’s nomination will officially be announced Monday, according to the officials.

Aigner, who previously served as agriculture minister under former German Chancellor Angela Merkel from 2008 to 2013, is currently president of the Bavarian State Parliament. She is also a member of the Christian Social Union (CSU), the Bavarian sister party to Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s Christian Democratic Union (CDU).

World.title: Trump’s ‘big, beautiful’ European security plan isn’t convincing Europe
World.content:
The latest U.S. proposal underscores growing anxiety around Trump’s fresh rapprochement with Russia as he ramps up pressure on Ukraine and his administration attempts to revive long-stalled talks to end Moscow’s full-scale war against Kyiv.

POLITICO spoke to 12 NATO diplomats, EU envoys and European government officials, all of whom were granted anonymity to speak freely on the sensitive issue. NATO allies were not briefed about the American plans in advance, according to three alliance diplomats, and many remain skeptical of the idea.

U.S. President Donald Trump late Thursday talked of a “big, beautiful agreement,” after meeting with Putin’s envoy Kirill Dmitriev, adding: “It’s going to involve more than Ukraine, and I could even say it might involve all of Europe.”

“Our objective is to develop practical arrangements that address the security concerns of all sides, reduce the risk of future conflict, and create a more stable and predictable security environment,” Trump’s son-in-law and envoy Jared Kushner added soon after.

Kushner said the arrangement would have five goals: “Permanent security consultations, reliable crisis communications, greater military transparency, reciprocal measures to reduce escalation risks, and an enduring framework for long-term European security and stability.”

“It is a bit obscure what Kushner meant,” said one NATO diplomat. “The general sentiment in Europe is that any discussion with Russia on the future architecture at the moment will just be used by Moscow to legitimize their arguments ... it will not fly with the European allies.”

World.title: Wave of bomb threats target Irish media outlets and more European flights
World.content:
“We have expected a rise in hybrid threats to Ireland because of our hosting of the EU presidency, and the EPC meeting will be by far the biggest set-piece event of that presidency, so one must presume it’s no coincidence that we’re experiencing this spike in hybrid activity now,” the Irish official said.

The Irish government said the threats against media outlets were probably part of a European-wide pattern of threats that have targeted dozens of airlines this week, including Irish carriers Ryanair and Aer Lingus. Hackers also targeted supermarket refrigeration systems in at least seven European countries.

“It is not known yet who is responsible for these threats, whether it is individuals or a centralized or coordinated effort,” the Irish government said in a statement. “However, these threats come on the heels of the ongoing disruption to aviation around Europe caused by similar threats, and it seems likely that this is a coordinated campaign of disruption.”

Bomb threats also targeted at least 18 European flights Friday, after at least 22 the day before, raising concerns that the hoaxes may be part of a coordinated campaign to disrupt air traffic.

Spanish Foreign Minister José Manuel Albares told Spanish public broadcaster TVE on Friday that the bomb threats affecting flights could be “an attempt at hybrid aggression and war in some psychological way.” He added that “it cannot be a coincidence that so many identical events occur with the same modus operandi throughout Europe.”

Luis Gallego, CEO of airline group IAG, said: “It is clear that what they [the perpetrators] are looking for is to create chaos and disruption in the different airports.”

World.title: EU capitals urge Brussels to ‘swiftly’ sign electricity deal with UK
World.content:
A group of countries are now urging the European Commission to wrap up discussions by the end of 2027, according to an EU diplomat granted anonymity to discuss internal discussions.

Proponents say the plan would unlock new renewable energy investment in the North Sea and could cut electricity prices.

But the EU says the U.K. would have to make a contribution to EU cohesion funds as the price of participating in the market — a politically difficult ask for London.

Clean energy hub

The leaders, including German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten, write that the agreement is “necessary to unlock the full potential of the North Sea” and to “transform it into the largest clean energy hub in the world.”

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President António Costa give a press conference at the end of a European Union summit at the EU headquarters in Brussels on October 16, 2026. | Nicolas Tucat/AFP via Getty Images

“An agreement will thus enhance Europe’s energy security and contribute to a competitive economy that centres on access to clean and affordable energy,” the letter to European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President António Costa states.

“These benefits underline the importance of swiftly concluding the ongoing negotiations. We call on you and the UK to agree during the Summit on a path towards the conclusion of these negotiations.”

World.title: Spain and the Netherlands battle over ECB presidency
World.content:
Exiting European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde gives a press conference in Frankfurt am Main, Germany, on Oct. 29, 2026. | Kirill Kudryavtsev/AFP via Getty Images

Pablo Hernández de Cos and Klaas Knot are in the hunt for the top job after Christine Lagarde’s exit.

BRUSSELS — The Netherlands and Spain on Friday submitted candidates to succeed Christine Lagarde, who steps down as president of the European Central Bank on Feb. 7.

Pablo Hernández de Cos, a former governor of Spain's central bank, and the Netherlands' Klaas Knot, a former president of the Dutch central bank, were the only candidates to emerge after the 5 p.m. deadline, as expected.

Their candidacies are part of a larger game of musical chairs that includes France and Germany, as Europe’s four economic powerhouses negotiate how to secure their seats on the ECB’s executive board.

World.title: ‘I don’t know if it reassured or worried them’: European envoys quiz Le Pen over lunch
World.content:
The group of ambassadors from the eight countries that share a border with metropolitan France — Germany, Spain, Belgium, Italy, Luxembourg, Switzerland, Monaco and Andorra — already met with conservative presidential candidate Bruno Retailleau in September. They are planning to host meetings with the other presidential hopefuls, including far-left candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon, at their respective embassies in the coming months.

“I don’t know if it reassured or worried them,” said an adviser to Marine Le Pen who accompanied her to the lunch. “What is sure is that they can now report back to their capitals what the National Rally wants to do,” the adviser added.

Le Pen was mainly questioned about her plans to downsize the EU and on bilateral issues, as well as U.S. President Donald Trump after his seismic defeat in the midterm elections.

While in the past, the National Rally has been supportive of Trump, the party has progressively distanced itself from the U.S. president. The National Rally’s Jordan Bardella on Wednesday said his party was not affected by the result and suggested that Trump’s popularity was undermined by the war in the Middle East and its economic consequences.



Le Pen has also been campaigning for a harsher approach on migration, which would involve stricter checks at the borders, potentially impacting countries whose envoys she met on Wednesday. All of them, apart from Andorra and Monaco, are part of the Schengen free-movement area.

“There is a general interest on what would her stance be on the key issues of mutual interest and cooperation on which we are working with France,” said one diplomat from a participating country.

“It was a very frank exchange. She told them what she says everywhere and she was able to elaborate on a number of topics a little more at length than she would do on TV,” the same adviser said, adding that Le Pen regularly meets ambassadors.

World.title: Election favorite says Spain should quit as World Cup co-host if Morocco stages the final
World.content:
Feijóo noted that the 2030 World Cup was originally a Spanish-Portuguese bid, until Morocco was invited at a later stage. Despite that chronology, Moroccan officials have been pushing vigorously to stage the final, which is the world’s most prestigious sports event.

Rafael Louzán, Spain’s football chief, told POLITICO in June that he was confident either Madrid or Barcelona would host the final, despite Morocco pouring vast amounts of cash into football infrastructure.

Tensions have flared between the two countries in recent months. Spanish political parties this summer accused Morocco of stoking a migrant crisis in Spain’s North African territory of Ceuta, after 80,000 people surged into the city in late July.

A Sigma Dos poll for El Mundo following the Ceuta crisis found that 84.4% of Spaniards opposed Spain continuing to co-host the World Cup with Morocco.

Leftist party Sumar, the Socialists’ junior coalition partner, said this summer that the World Cup “cannot be shared with a country that uses desperate people for its own geostrategic interests.”

The left-wing party tabled a resolution in parliament that far-right Vox backed in an unusual convergence. The text never made it to a vote because parliament was dissolved ahead of the snap election.

World.title: Poland: Footage shows people taking cover as a gunman opens fire in Krakow
World.content:
Terrified pedestrians fled through the streets of Kraków on Saturday as a gunman opened fire in the historic Main Market Square, killing six people and injuring 16 others.

 

Witness footage captures people running for safety as vehicles race past and shots ring out. Other images show shattered windows, overturned café chairs, ambulances and police cars rushing to the scene, with a helicopter circling overhead.

Police said the attacker, a 25-year-old Polish citizen, fired indiscriminately from a car before exchanging shots with officers nearby. He was wounded, arrested and taken to hospital.

The victims included four women and two men, one of them British. Two police officers were also injured, one critically.

The interior minister said the suspect held ultranationalist views, while the defence minister called the attack an act of terror. Investigators believe he acted alone.

World.title: Ukraine: Russian strikes hit Kyiv region, damaging infrastructure
World.content:
Footage released by Ukraine's emergency services shows crews directing powerful jets of water towards burning industrial structures, with firefighters working among the wreckage as flames spread through the site.

 

The attacks also damaged energy facilities and a major bridge in Kyiv. In the capital, a kindergarten was left severely damaged, with a large crater in its grounds, shattered walls and children's toys scattered among the rubble. Workers began clearing debris from the destroyed building, while nearby residents inspected the damage. Five people were reported wounded in the strikes.

The latest attacks come as Ukraine prepares for another difficult winter, with its energy infrastructure repeatedly targeted by Russian forces. Damage to power facilities threatens to disrupt electricity and heating supplies as temperatures fall, placing further pressure on an already strained network.

The renewed bombardment also comes amid diplomatic efforts to bring the war to an end, with talks involving Ukraine, Russia and the United States under discussion. Despite these initiatives, strikes on civilian areas and critical infrastructure continue, highlighting the challenges facing Ukrainians as the conflict enters another winter.

World.title: Liverpool FC targets counterfeit pro-Palestinian shirts using altered club crest
World.content:
The organisation "UK Lawyers for Israel" (UKLFI) had on 26 October 2026 alerted four Premier League clubs to possible trade mark infringements and reported on them in an online article. On 5 November the online portal "Jewish News" also carried a report.

 

Liverpool FC has confirmed that it is taking action against the sale of unauthorised football shirts featuring pro-Palestinian messages that display a modified version of the club crest. The club fears that fans could mistakenly take these shirts for official merchandise.

The Premier League club has therefore taken measures against online retailers who are using its protected trade marks without permission. The shirts are being sold via the website "From Palestine to the World".

Crests and sponsor logos deliberately altered

Fake jerseys for several English Premier League clubs with pro-Palestinian messages are being offered online. Club crests, lettering and sponsor logos have been altered to spread political messages. The shirts are not authorised by the clubs concerned.

Manchester United: The club crest has been combined with the slogan "Manchester with Gaza", and the centre shows a dove of peace carrying an olive branch. The club has passed the information on to its brand protection department.

Chelsea FC: The crest has been turned into "Palestine Club", and the word "Palestine" appears on the shirt in place of the usual sponsor logo. The club has referred the matter to the relevant internal department for review.

Manchester City: The official shirt sponsor EtihadAirways has been replaced by the wording "Palestine Airways". The club has confirmed receipt of the letter but has not yet announced any specific measures.

Liverpool FC: The iconic club crest has been modified and marked with the initials "P.L.C.", which stand for the Palestinian legislature (Palestine Legislative Council).

The club has already taken steps and reported the relevant sales offers to website operators and social networks over possible trade mark infringements. Further action is planned.

Legal background

The background to these moves is possible breaches of UK trade mark law (Trade Marks Act 1994). Using protected club crests and logos without permission can constitute a trade mark infringement. Political expression and support for Palestine are generally protected by law, but this does not create a right to use protected trade marks.

There is also a risk that fans may mistake the shirts for official merchandise and thereby attribute to the clubs a political stance they have not adopted.

World.title: Video shows people fleeing as gunman opens fire in Kraków, Poland
World.content:
At least six people have been killed and around a dozen wounded after a gunman opened fire in the historic centre of Kraków, Poland's second-largest city, according to police.

 

Amateur footage shows people fleeing as shots ring out, with cars passing through the area. Other videos capture the aftermath, showing emergency services responding to the scene, broken glass and overturned chairs scattered nearby. A helicopter can also be seen flying over the area.

World.title: 'Peace is possible and we are called to build it' Pope Leo XIV says in Uruguay
World.content:
During his sixth apostolic journey, Pope Leo XIV stopped in Paysandú, in Uruguay, where he celebrated Mass in the Parque París Londres in front of more than 40,000 faithful.

 

Arriving at the exhibition area in the popemobile from the "Brigadier General Aviator Tydeo Larre Borges" International Airport, the Pontiff made his way through the cheering crowd, blessing those present. When he reached the altar, next to an image of Blessed Jacinto Vera, he centred his entire homily on the key concepts of unity and community.

"Peace is possible and we are called to build it," the pontiff said during the liturgical celebration. He then offered the multitude three symbols characteristic of Uruguayan soil to show how to safeguard and spread the Christian faith today.

The first element he evoked was the "General Artigas" bridge, a metaphor for the importance of building strong bonds and engaging in dialogue with others. The second was represented by the local palm trees, which grow together in groves and recall the communal nature of the Church. Finally, there was mate, the famous traditional drink shared at moments of encounter, highlighted as a deep emblem of familiarity and brotherhood. "An element deeply significant to your culture, around which friends or relatives gather to share," Leo XIV said.

At the end of the service, after official thanks from the bishop of Salto, Arturo Eduardo Fajardo Bustamante, the Pope presented a chalice to the local diocese.

Faithful await Pope Leone XIV AP Photo/Andrew Medichini

Leo XIV's programme in Uruguay

The packed schedule for the day continued with an intense itinerary of institutional and pastoral engagements. After the liturgy in the park, a visit to the Basilica of Our Lady of the Rosary followed for the unveiling of a commemorative plaque and a greeting to the faithful outside the building. The Pontiff then left Paysandú for the capital, Montevideo, where the second part of his busy official agenda continued.

In the late afternoon in the capital, the Pope will meet the social community of Casavalle at the Parish of Our Lady of Guadalupe. This will be followed by an engagement with the academic and education sector at the Catholic University of Uruguay. Both moments will be a central opportunity for direct dialogue with the educational and care institutions of the South American country.

The day will conclude at Montevideo's Centenario Stadium, which the Pope will reach by travelling in the popemobile to allow once again for an encounter with the public. In the sports venue, Leo XIV will preside over a solemn prayer vigil together with thousands of young people and faithful who have travelled from all over the country for the closing event.

On Sunday, the pope is expected in Florida, about 90 kilometres from the capital Montevideo, considered the "cradle" of the nation because it is where the Declaration of Independence took place in 1825. It is also an important religious centre due to the presence of the National Shrine of the Virgen de los Treinta y Tres. In the square in front of it the Pope will celebrate Sunday Mass.

World.title: Latest news bulletin | November 7th, 2026 – Evening
World.content: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond in this Euronews news bulletin. In just a few minutes, our newsroom brings you the latest news and breaking news across world affairs, business, politics, culture, entertainment and travel, with the context you need to make sense of a fast-moving day. Reported with the independence and the European perspective that define Euronews, this regular round-up gives you a clear and reliable overview of the stories shaping our world right now, wherever you are watching from.

World.title: ‘We need to change everything’: Mélenchon uses Le Bourget rally to press home his programme
World.content:
On Saturday, Jean-Luc Mélenchon invited his supporters to Le Bourget, north of Paris, for a major rally dedicated to the presentation of his manifesto, “L’Avenir en commun”, which had gone on sale in bookshops the day before.

 

The leader of La France Insoumise began his hour-long speech, delivered before several thousand supporters, with a minute’s silence in tribute to Pengo Bossio Wangi, aged 26, a victim of the racist attack in Trappes, before calling for a “cultural liberation” of France in the face of “fascist culture”.

For Jean-Luc Mélenchon, racism and “the liberal abandonment of the people” both threaten the unity of the nation.

The radical left-wing candidate called for a “social state of emergency” and hailed a “France in turmoil”, referring to the secondary school students’ movement, which has expanded over the past few weeks to include demands against the high cost of living and in defence of public services.

Jean-Luc Mélenchon also called for the introduction of the right to vote at 16, a measure which, he believes, “will make the others [the current government] much more vigilant about what is happening in secondary schools”.

Firmly in second place in the polls

Beyond these two burning issues, the four-time presidential candidate promised to create a “new ecological state”, based on planning and “a mixed economy geared towards ecological imperatives”.

His choice of venue for this latest campaign event also appears calculated.

It was in Le Bourget that François Hollande delivered his now-famous declaration during the 2012 presidential campaign: "My real opponent is the world of finance."

The statement was intended to establish his left-wing credentials before he went on, once elected, to pursue supply-side economic policies - a first for a French Socialist leader.

Nearly fifteen years later, Mélenchon is seeking to position himself as the candidate of a decisive break with the left, at a time when social unrest is spreading across the country.

Firmly in second place in the polls on around 18%, the France Unbowed (LFI) leader has picked up several endorsements in recent days.

On Thursday, most Communist and overseas-territories MPs in the National Assembly formally backed his candidacy, despite French Communist Party leader Fabien Roussel also running. The Greens, meanwhile, are expected to decide in mid-December on a possible alliance with LFI.

Despite this momentum, Mélenchon still trails well behind Marine Le Pen, who is polling at between 35% and 37%.

'Liberty, equality, solidarity'

A few hours before his rally in Le Bourget, Mélenchon unveiled his campaign poster.

It shows his portrait set against a Gergovie landscape, a backdrop that also evokes a rural France where the LFI vote remains weak, along with a reworked republican motto: "liberty, equality, solidarity."

On social media, some internet users are already comparing it with François Mitterrand's 1981 poster, which showed him in front of a Burgundy village dominated by its church, above the slogan "quiet strength."

While previous versions of the programme placed the creation of a Sixth Republic at the top of the agenda, ecological transformation has now become one of France Unbowed's main priorities.

Among its proposals, the party is proposing to replace existing administrative regions with "eco-regions" organised around the management of water resources. It also wants to enshrine stronger environmental protections in the constitution.

France Unbowed is also sticking to its commitment to a gradual phase-out of nuclear power, although the target of reaching 100% renewable energy has been pushed back from 2050 to 2060.

'L'Avenir en commun'

On the economic and social front, Mélenchon is keeping faithful to his long-standing pledges: to raise the minimum wage (SMIC) to €1,700 pcm and eventually lowering the legal retirement age to 60 for people who have paid into the pension system for 40 years.

The programme has been published without a detailed financial breakdown, but party officials stress that it is a "foundation" that will be supplemented by around 50 documents detailing the various measures.

At a press conference in mid-October, Mélenchon and Éric Coquerel, the LFI head of the National Assembly's finance committee, presented their "revised budget" for 2027 in the event of victory.

It contained roughly €100 billion in additional revenue to be generated through tax measures, as well as €80 billion in additional spending.

In foreign policy, the LFI is continuing to focus on the war in Gaza and Israeli settlement activity in the West Bank. It is also proposing to suspend the association agreement between Israel and the European Union.

On Ukraine, the document calls for a ceasefire but says little about military support for Kyiv. It also advocates setting up a new European security framework that would include Russia.

A 'plan to dismantle France'

Mélenchon's manifesto has already drawn strong reactions from his opponents.

In a post on X, Le Pen, the far-right National Rally presidential candidate, hit out at what she called a "plan to dismantle France".

"It takes the process of deconstruction initiated by Emmanuel Macron since he came to power to its logical conclusion," she wrote.

Speaking near Marseille on Saturday, former prime minister Édouard Philippe, who is also running in the presidential election, criticised what he dubbed Mélenchon's "communitarian vision" and his "administered economy".

Referring to his two rivals on the far right and the hard left, the centre-right candidate said he saw "many points in common" between Le Pen and Mélenchon, notably their "hatred of European integration" and their desire to "leave NATO".

World.title: Six killed and more than a dozen injured after gunman opens fire in historic centre of Kraków
World.content:
At least six people were killed and 16 injured, among them two police officers, after a gunman opened fire on the main square of the Polish city of Kraków.

 

Katarzyna Cisło, a police spokesperson, said the perpetrator was wearing military-style fatigues and a bulletproof vest and used a military-type long gun in the attack.

Police found many other weapons, as well as ammunition, in his car. He kept firing at the police even after being shot himself, she said.

The attacker engaged in a “wild ride” around the Main Square, Cisło said, which is why people were wounded at several locations.

The suspect, a 25-year-old Polish citizen, was fascinated with far-right ideologies and held “very radical" and “ultra-nationalistic" views, Polish Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said at a news conference.

An armed police officer secures a cordoned off area after a shooter opened fire in a market square in Krakow, Poland, Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. AP Photo/Beata Zawrzel

Polish Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz called Saturday’s fatal shooting an “act of terror” on the people of Krakow, Poland's second-largest city, which receives 15 million visitors a year, most of them passing through the Main Square.

Thirteen of the 16 people injured were brought to the hospital with serious injuries, and five of them were foreign citizens.

Videos posted on social media by witnesses show people running away from the square to take cover on small streets nearby, as well as first responders trying to resuscitate victims.

In one of the videos, a policeman is seen repeatedly shooting the attacker, who is lying on the street, only to later slowly collapse himself to the ground.

Poland’s Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński tweeted: “Police officers risked their lives while intervening in Kraków. They acted immediately. Thanks to their heroic actions, the attacker was quickly apprehended.

One police officer has a gunshot wound; the condition of the second is very serious — he suffered three gunshot wounds. He is currently undergoing surgery.”

Forensic investigators remove their suits a cordoned off area after a shooter opened fire in a market square in Krakow, Poland, Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. AP Photo/Beata Zawrzel

Malopolska police confirmed that the gunman is a Polish citizen and denied reports about a possible second perpetrator being sought.

A spokesperson of the Malopolska Chief Police Commander, Andrzej Fijołek, stated that the perpetrator comes from Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski.

He added that he had not been on police records before. The car he was driving was registered under his 52-year-old father's name, who, local media reported, holds several gun licences.

Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz denied reports that the perpetrator was a soldier of the Polish Army. "The man was not and is not a soldier of the Polish Army and has never had anything to do with the army", he said.

President Karol Nawrocki said his he was "deeply concerned by reports of the tragic events in central Kraków" and that his "thoughts are with the victims, those injured and their families."

The president announced two days of national mourning, on 8 and 9 November.

Both Nawrocki and Prime Minister Donald Tusk are reported to be on their way to Kraków.

EU Foreign Chief Kaja Kallas said "the tragic loss of life in the shooting in Krakow is a tragedy that will be felt far beyond Poland," in a post on X. "My thoughts are with the victims and their families and the first responders."

World.title: Poland: Gunman kills 6 in Krakow main square
World.content:
A gunman who fired from a car killed at least six people, including a British tourist, in Krakow's main market square. Officials said the shooter was fascinated with "radical" and "far right' ideologies.

At least six people were killed and 16 injured in a shooting on the main market square in the southern Polish city of Krakow on Saturday.

The perpetrator, a 25-year-old Polish man who acted alone, was wounded during an exchange of fire with police, authorities said.

"Until now in Poland we haven't had such drastic cases of terrorism," Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk told reporters in Krakow.

"That's what we have to call this cruel attack on people's lives here in Krakow," he added.

Shooter aimed at random people, police say

The gunman aimed at random people as he drove through the city's main square, which is a popular tourist attraction.

"At around 3 pm (1400 GMT), a man who had driven into the market square in a car began shooting at random people from inside the vehicle," police said on X, adding officers were among the wounded.

Deadly shooting in popular Krakow tourist spot To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

"The perpetrator was shot by police ‌officers and is currently being ‌transported ​to a hospital," police said. Authorities later clarified that the man drove to multiple spots in the square and opened fire at each with an automatic weapon.

Later Saturday evening, Polish police chief Marek Boron said a British citizen was among those killed.

"There are six fatalities: four women and two men; three Polish women, one British national, and two people who have not yet been identified," Boron told reporters.

Krakow police had earlier said that five of the 16 people injured in the shooting were non-Polish nationals. An Interior Ministry spokesperson confirmed that they came from Austria, Germany, Portugal, Russia and Britain.

Police secure an area near the city's main market square Image: Jakub Włodek/Agencja Wyborcza.pl/REUTERS

Bodies found in shooter's house

On Saturday night, Tusk said that the bodies of two women and a man were found in the shooter's home by police.

There was "much to suggest that they are members of the [suspect's] immediate family."

The residence is located in Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski, a city about 150 kilometers (93 miles) northeast of Krakow.

"We have the next acts of this tragedy," Tusk told reporters.

Shooter fascinated by 'far-right' views

Polish Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski said that the shooter, whom she declined to identify, was "fascinated by far-right ideologies" and held "ultranationalistic" and "very radical" views.

The shooter wore military-style fatigues and a bulletproof vest and used a long gun in the attack, said Katarzyna Cislo, a spokesperson for the Krakow police,

Numerous other weapons and ammunition were found in the gunman's car.

Police personnel at the site of shooting Image: Jakub Włodek/Agencja Wyborcza.pl/REUTERS

Poland to observe 2 days of mourning

Prime Minister Tusk posted on X that police were investigating the attack and called it a "tragic" incident.

Tusk later said Poland would observe two days of mourning for the victims of the shooting.

Polish President Karol Nawrocki wrote on X that his thoughts were with the victims and wounded, as well as their families.

'Poland does not stand alone,' European politicians show support

The European Union's top diplomat, Kaja Kallas, said the shooting was a tragedy that will be felt far beyond Poland, adding that "Poland does not stand alone."

"I am deeply saddened by the events in Krakow. My thoughts are with the victims and their families," German Chancellor Friedrich Merz wrote on X, adding that "Germany stands alongside Poland as a friend and partner during these difficult times."

Krakow is located about 250 kilometers (155 miles) from Warsaw, the capital of Poland.

With a population of over 800,000, Krakow is Poland's second-largest city, as well as a popular tourist destination.

World.title: Ebola: Why is there still no vaccine?
World.content:
Ebola has been known about for decades, but there is still no vaccine against the Bundibugyo strain of the virus causing the current outbreak. New research raises hopes of protection against the various types of Ebola.

1976: A hitherto unknown disease breaks out near the Ebola river in the country then known as Zaire, now the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). This was the first scientifically documented Ebola epidemic.

Now, 50 years on, the DRC once again finds itself at the center of a major Ebola outbreak. This time the pathogen is the less common Bundibugyo type of the genus Orthoebolavirus. The virus was identified in 2007 during an outbreak in Bundibugyo, Uganda. Another outbreak occurred in the DRC in 2012.

Bundibugyo: Preparations could have been made

How can a virus that has been known for decades continue to infect thousands of people, yet there is still no licensed vaccine or official treatment?

Torsten Feldt, a doctor of tropical medicine at Düsseldorf's University Hospital, sees this as a missed opportunity. "We had come across the Bundibugyo virus in two previous outbreaks: 2007 in Uganda and 2012 in DR Congo. So we had enough time to develop vaccines and therapeutic options. But we didn't make use of this opportunity, meaning crucial time was lost during the current outbreak."

Leonie Mayer from the German Center for Infection Research (DZIF) and the Institute for Infection Research and Vaccine Development at the University Medical Center in Hamburg-Eppendorf agrees. "They could of course have developed a vaccine and run pre-clinical trials before," Mayer told DW. She stressed, however, that their effectiveness can only be assessed and confirmed during an actual outbreak.

Mayer is the lead author of a recently published study that examined whether Ervebo, an Ebola vaccine that has already been licensed, can be used against other types of Ebola as well.

Congo's Ebola crisis: Fear, mistrust and a growing outbreak To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Why Ebola is a good candidate for vaccine development

From an immunological point of view, and compared to — for example — influenza or HIV, Ebola is a very worthwhile candidate for a vaccine. Influenza viruses are constantly mutating, and the human immunodeficiency virus is particularly good at evading our immune defenses. Ebola is far more predictable.

"I think — and perhaps it's kind of a blessing in disguise — that it will be relatively straightforward to develop a vaccine against Bundibugyo," says Mayer.

Herein lies the paradox. From a scientific point of view, Ebola is a good vaccine candidate, yet there is still no licensed form of prevention against the Bundibugyo variant that is currently circulating.

Mayer explains that vaccines cannot be developed as a precautionary measure against every potential pathogen. Lack of funding or the prioritization of other pathogens often have a role to play. Many researchers had assumed that a fresh outbreak of the Sudan Ebola virus was more likely, and vaccine development for this strain is more advanced.

Different types of Ebola

Another part of the problem is that Ebola is not one single virus. The known, highly dangerous orthoebolaviruses include Ebola virus (EBOV), previously called the Zaire Ebola virus (ZEBOV), the Sudan virus (SUDV), and the Bundibugyo virus (BDBV). The existing vaccine, Ervebo, was developed and licensed for use against the Zaire variant. But there is still no approved protection against the others.

This is why the existing Ebola vaccine has been of only limited use to people in the areas of the current outbreak.

Another factor may also be relevant: The Bundibugyo virus appears to be less aggressive than the Zaire variant. At first, that sounds like good news, but it may make it harder to contain, as people remain mobile for longer after being infected, and can pass on the virus without realizing.

Ervebo vaccine: Immune response to Bundibugyo

In the recently published study, Mayer's research team from the DZIF investigated whether the already licensed Ebola vaccine could trigger an immune response not only against EBOV, but against other types of Ebola as well. They found cross-reactive T-cell responses against Bundibugyo, and also, to a lesser extent, against the Sudan virus.

For Mayer, this is already an important finding: "We now know that the immune cells can most likely also recognize the Bundibugyo virus." But she also observes: "Our data does not enable us to answer the question of whether this immune response actually provides protection, or if it results in a milder progression of the disease." This is currently an important gap in our knowledge.

Why the existing vaccine cannot currently be deployed

If there's a vaccine that has already been licensed, and indications that it could protect people, why isn't it simply being deployed?

Mayer explains the dilemma. For one thing, she says, it's not ethical to deploy a vaccine if you're not sure whether or how well it works. Also, if it were used on a large scale, it would no longer be possible to establish whether it actually works: A reduction in cases could also be a result of other measures, or the epidemic might already have passed its peak.

Jürgen May, a specialist in tropical diseases at the Bernhard Nocht Institute, also warns against mass vaccination: "Mass vaccination without proof of efficacy could create a false sense of security, forfeit trust, and, if it does not provide sufficient protection, make study impossible."

It's very important for there to be acceptance on the ground. "If we inoculate people with a vaccine on a large scale, and afterwards it turns out that it was nothing like as effective as we expected, it's very difficult to communicate that to people on the ground," Mayer says. In a worst-case scenario, people could subsequently refuse inoculation with more effective vaccines.

Why Ebola is still so difficult to contain

But the current outbreak also shows that medical innovation alone is not enough. Conflicts, difficult transport routes, attacks on healthcare facilities, and gaps in contact tracing all make it harder to contain.

The DRC has had more than 10,000 cases of Bundibugyo since May. Recently, it has also been reported in Kenya and Nigeria Image: Andrew Kasuku/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance

Torsten Feldt says identifying Bundibugyo is no longer a problem in itself. What is often limiting is the practical availability of diagnostic tools. "In remote or conflict-affected regions, samples often have to be transported over long distances," he explains.

Here we see another Ebola paradox. The world is getting ever better at diagnosing infections, but it still struggles to contain outbreaks fast enough. The authors of an article in the current issue of Nature come to the same conclusion: The problem is often not identifying cases, but the speed with which people react. Finding Ebola is often easier now than stopping Ebola, they write.

From a Bundibugyo vaccine to a pan-Ebola one?

Many researchers believe the current crisis could potentially also provide a great opportunity. The so-called Tumaini study, which is testing different vaccine candidates, has now been launched in the DRC.

These include Ervebo, developed by Oxford University, and a Moderna mRNA vaccine. The study aims to provide the first reliable data about their efficacy against the Bundibugyo virus.

Whether these vaccines could still help control the current outbreak is uncertain. There is hope, but experts estimate that, realistically, it will be several months before any such vaccine is available for widespread use; perhaps not until mid-2027.

"Ideally, we will develop cross-reactive pan-Ebola vaccines," Christof Geldmacher, a co-author of the DZIF study, says of their long-term plans. This is also something that is being worked on. For now, though, the focus is on developing an effective vaccine against the Bundibugyo variant of the virus.

World.title: Israeli president tasks Gadi Eisenkot with forming government
World.content:
President Isaac Herzog has picked former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot, leader of an anti-Netanyahu alliance, to take the first shot at trying to form a government, with tricky coalition talks expected.

Israeli President Isaac Herzog has chosen Gadi Eisenkot to have the first opportunity to form a new Israeli government, according to a statement released by his office on Saturday evening.

The statement said Eisenkot was informed of Herzog's "intention to task him with forming a government" and would be invited to the president's residence, where a formal ceremony will take place on Sunday.

The decision comes after a neck-and-neck race with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Israel's October election.

Eisenkot's wide-ranging group, fashioned in opposition to Netanyahu, won 48 of the Israeli parliament's 120 seats in October's elections. Netanyahu's camp secured 53, leaving neither with the required majority of 61 seats.

Former Israeli military chief Eisenkot is the leader of the centrist Yashar party and heads an anti-Netanyahu alliance.

While Netanyahu ruled out working with Arab parties to gain a majority, both Arab majority lists had announced during the week that they would recommend Eisenkot to be next prime minister.

Can Netanyahu survive his last big fight? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

What happens next?

The move is the first step toward what will almost certainly be complicated coalition talks.

Should Eisenkot succeed in forming a government, he would take over as prime minister from Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving premier, whose religious-nationalist coalition lost its majority in the election, despite emerging as the largest bloc.

Although Eisenkot was runner up, he managed to secure endorsements from leaders of Arab parties, which are opposed to Netanyahu.

Eisenkot faces a tricky path to forming a government, involving difficult constellations of Arab and ultra-Orthodox parties. He will have 28 days to round up the 61 votes needed to form a government.

Herzog can provide a 14-day extension if Eisenkot comes up short before the mandate must be offered to someone else.

If no candidate succeeds, Israel will head to fresh elections.

World.title: Trump offers White House press secretary role to Dana White
World.content:
US President Donald Trump has offered the White House press secretary job to Dana White, the chief executive of the Ultimate Fighting Championship. White has neither formally accepted nor turned down the invitation.

US President Donald Trump announced on Saturday that he has asked Dana White, the CEO of Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC), to serve as White House press secretary.

"I am pleased to announce that the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior, has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States," Trump wrote on his Truth Social account.

"Dana, please take the job!" Trump said, calling on the longtime fight promoter to bring "assistants" with him "even though some are not from our country."

Is Dana White the new press secretary?

While White has neither formally accepted nor turned down the offer, the 57-year-old shared a photo of himself behind the lectern in the White House press briefing room on his Instagram Stories. Over the photo, he wrote: "On to the next chapter."

Minutes later, he reposted Trump's full Truth Social post offering him the White House press secretary job.

Meanwhile, CNN citing ‌a ​source familiar with the matter reported that White, who has been president of the UFC since 2001 and its CEO since 2023, turned down the offer.

White House press secretary role vacant since mid-October

The position of White House press secretary has been empty since October 16 when Katie Zacharia left the high-profile job after a shaky debut press briefing.

Zacharia was out as press secretary after just five days on the job. She replaced Karoline Leavitt, who stepped down from the role at the end of August.

Trump's offer to White came a day after he appointed Stephen Miller as his next chief of staff following massive Republican losses in the midterm elections.

Trump and Dana White are close friends

White is one of Trump's loyal supporters. The UFC chief publicly backed ​Trump's presidential campaign in ‌2016. When Trump won reelection in 2024, White appeared alongside Trump for his victory speech.

In recent years, Trump has attended several UFC events, including bouts in Miami, New York and New Jersey since winning his second White House term.

In June, the White House hosted its first-ever UFC event on the White House South Lawn as part of ⁠celebrations marking the 250th anniversary of US independence.

World.title: France sees new round of Yellow Vest, student protests
World.content:
Although fewer protesters turned out in comparison with previous weeks, several cities saw clashes between police and demonstrators.

Fewer protesters than expected turned out for the fourth weekend of mass demonstrations in France, although clashes with police were reported in several cities, the Interior Ministry said on Saturday.

Authorities had expected up to 170,000 people to protest nationwide, including 60,000 in Paris.

The ministry reported a slightly lower nationwide total of 146,000 people, out of which some 46,000 took to the streets of the French capital, where the afternoon was reported to have remained mostly calm, with some isolated incidents reported in the evening involving the deployment of tear gas.

Protest organizers gave a higher nationwide count of over 250,000 protesters, which is nevertheless fewer than the 320,000 to 500,000 that were reported to have turned out last Saturday.

Clashes between police and protesters were reported in Toulouse, Marseille, Lyon and Bordeaux.

The Interior Ministry reported some 350 arrests nationwide by the evening in connection with the protests.

Trash cans were set on fire in Marseille Image: Justine Meddah/AFP

Fourth week of protests in France

Students and labor unions had called an authorized central Paris march "against the high cost of living and in support of young people."

A protest march began at Place de la Republique Satursday Image: Stephanie Lecocq/REUTERS

In Paris, an authorized march proceeded peacefully from Republique to Nation, but tensions erupted after police said some 200 "violent individuals" attacked law enforcement after a man was arrested for setting fire to a trash can, according to Paris' police headquarters.

Depsite several incidents, French authorities said the protests in Paris were mostly calm Image: Stephanie Lecocq/REUTERS

Separately, the country's so-called "Yellow Vest" movement — which gained notoriety eight years ago by violently protesting a proposed fuel tax hike rejected invitations to join the student rally.

Instead, the "Gilets Jaunes" held a banned event at Paris' Place de la Concorde, close to parliament and the presidential Elysee Palace. Two of its leading figures, Benjamin Ball and Solene Azelma Sigaux, were arrested and taken into custody.

Ahead of Saturday's protests, French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said 70,000 police and security forces would be deployed across the country over the weekend, adding that authorities will "be ready" for "rioters and looters."

France protests turn violent nationwide To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Can France afford to raise wages, invest in schools?

The large police presence comes on the heels of weeks of mass demonstrations that have at times grown extremely violent, most notably on October 17, when France's worst rioting in years resulted in more than a billion euros in damage to private and public property.

On Thursday, police made over 600 arrests during a nationwide strike that included blockades and other protest action.

Authorities say that, for the most part, protests have remained peaceful.

But there have continued to be numerous incidents of violent clashes with police, as outgoing President Emmanuel Macron and his government struggle to address public discontent over the rising cost of living.

Although Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu is scheduled to meet with trade and employee unions on Monday, organizers say the only thing that will quell anger will be for the government to bow to their demands.

"The only thing that will bring the protests to an end is a response to the demands that have been put forward for several weeks by workers, civil servants, young people and pensioners," according to an inter-union coalition statement published on Friday.

This latest round of protests began with students calling for improvements to the national education system and unions joining in to call for wage hikes and tax reforms.
