World.title: Iraqi-Spanish Economic Business Council convenes in Madrid
World.content:
Madrid (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi-Spanish Economic Business Council convened in Madrid on Friday, bringing together Iraqi Ambassador to Spain Ali Shamran Hashim Al-Bayati, a senior government delegation, and executives from major Spanish industrial, trade, and investment institutions.

Hosted by the Spanish Chamber of Commerce, the forum aimed to deepen commercial cooperation between Baghdad and Madrid, broaden bilateral investment opportunities, and establish structured joint ventures across vital economic sectors.

Delegates reviewed pathways to expand Spanish commercial involvement in Iraq, particularly in transport, renewable energy, water management, healthcare, and civil infrastructure.

The Madrid summit reflects ongoing efforts by the Iraqi federal government to diversify foreign partnerships beyond traditional markets, encouraging European corporate participation in post-reconstruction development through direct investment, technical joint ventures, and sustainable cross-border trade frameworks.

World.title: US Embassy in Baghdad warns citizens of security risks
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The U.S. Embassy in Baghdad issued a formal security alert on Saturday, warning American citizens residing in or traveling through the Middle East of heightened operational risks stemming from potential armed attacks by the Iranian-backed Houthis, alongside reported Iranian efforts to target U.S. government personnel and interests across the region.

According to the consular advisory, American diplomatic authorities urged citizens to exercise heightened vigilance and prepare for potential commercial aviation disruptions, including short-notice flight cancellations and intermittent airspace closures.

Travelers were advised to monitor airport operational statuses and coordinate directly with commercial airlines for updated departure schedules. The mission highlighted that retaliatory threats or proxy militia actions could extend to commercial facilities, enterprises, and public venues associated with the United States.

To mitigate operational vulnerabilities, the embassy instructed U.S. citizens to maintain a low profile, avoid large crowds, demonstrations, and sites of heavy security deployment, closely monitor local media for situational updates, and strictly comply with instructions issued by host-nation authorities.

World.title: Iraqi Airways resumes direct flights to Beijing starting November 14
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Airways announced on Thursday the resumption of scheduled direct flights to the Chinese capital, Beijing, starting November 14, 2026, marking a significant step in restoring direct air connectivity with one of Iraq’s primary commercial and economic partners.

In an official statement, Director General of Iraqi Airways Mustafa Talib confirmed that the national carrier will operate two weekly round-trip flights servicing the strategic route (Baghdad – Basra – Beijing).

Outbound flights from Iraq are scheduled every Tuesday and Saturday, with return legs operating out of Beijing on Sundays and Wednesdays.

Talib highlighted that the service reinstatement aligns with directives issued by Minister of Transport Wahab Al-Hasani to expand the national carrier’s international route network and inaugurate high-yield commercial air corridors.

By linking Baghdad and the southern oil hub of Basra directly to Beijing, the route aims to streamline business travel, facilitate bilateral freight and corporate logistics, and support expanding commercial and industrial cooperation between Iraq and China.

World.title: Iraq and Syria sign water accord to coordinate Euphrates inflows
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq and Syria have signed a bilateral technical agreement in Damascus to establish joint mechanisms for managing cross-border water resources and align their diplomatic positions ahead of anticipated trilateral negotiations with Turkey over the Euphrates River basin.

The discussions brought together technical delegations led by the Senior Technical Undersecretary of the Iraqi Ministry of Water Resources, Hussein Abdul-Amir Bakka, and Syria’s Deputy Minister of Energy for Water and Electricity Affairs, Osama Abu Zaid.

The bilateral protocol establishes immediate operational measures, including the deployment of joint hydrological gauging stations along the river, regular technical data exchanges, coordinated water quality testing, and collaborative frameworks for monitoring dam integrity and coordinating reservoir discharges. Both parties agreed to work toward convening a tripartite technical meeting including Turkish representatives in March 2027.

The agreement builds directly on previous bilateral coordination meetings held in Baghdad in late June, aiming to settle longstanding operational frictions between the two downstream nations.

Under their 1989 bilateral quota arrangement, Damascus commits to releasing 58% of Turkish Euphrates water inflows into Iraq while retaining 42% for domestic use. However, seasonal flow reductions and conflicting agricultural timelines frequently lead to operational strain around the Tabqa Dam in Syria and the Haditha Dam in Iraq.

Beyond bilateral synchronization, the Damascus talks represent a unified push by downstream states against Turkey’s transboundary water policies.

Ankara continues to govern Euphrates flows under a temporary 1987 protocol establishing a baseline release of 500 cubic meters per second, a framework severely constrained by upstream impoundments under Turkey’s Southeastern Anatolia Project (GAP). Both Baghdad and Damascus are pressing for a permanent, legally binding trilateral treaty aligned with international water law to guarantee equitable baseline quotas.

World.title: Iran says forces ‘stronger’ than at beginning of war
World.content:
Tehran – Iran said Saturday its military has grown “stronger” since the outset of its war with the United States, which has offered a $20 million reward for information about Tehran’s nuclear programme.

Mediators have been working to prevent any resumption of fighting after months of deadlock in the Middle East conflict, which began when the United States and Israel attacked Iran in late February.

Tehran has sought to limit traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption.

Iranian army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia said Tehran retained control over the strategic waterway and that it would remain closed until its demands were met by the United States.

He also said Iran’s forces had grown stronger and more confident, state news agency IRNA reported on Saturday.

“Today, the Islamic Republic’s armed forces… having gained experience from direct confrontation with the United States and the Israeli regime, are on higher alert and are stronger than they were at the beginning of the war,” he said.

“They now possess greater motivation, commitment, and self-confidence.”

“Under the order of the Supreme Leader, the response of the armed forces will be immediate, effective, and without geographical limitations,” he added.

– Reward offered –

On Friday, the US military said it was offering a $20 million reward “and possible relocation” for information about Iran’s nuclear programme.

Rewards for Justice, a State Department programme, was seeking information on topics including “facilities, equipment, and associated personnel, such as those in the scientific community,” US Central Command said on X.

The programme was established in 1984 under the State Department’s national security rewards programme to offer money for information that protects American lives and interests.

In a statement about the reward, the State Department said Iran’s “lack of compliance with the (International Atomic Energy Agency) on safeguards obligations has led to the agency’s loss of ‘continuity of knowledge’ regarding Iran’s production and inventory of key components like centrifuges.”

It did not specify what type of information would warrant a $20 million reward.

US President Donald Trump has repeatedly said US forces have effectively obliterated Iran’s nuclear programme.

“If we didn’t hit Iran, you wouldn’t have Israel today,” Trump said Friday night in West Palm Beach, Florida.

“If they had nuclear, they would have used nuclear. They would have obliterated the Middle East.”

– Dialogue –

The president also said Iran — which he stressed has had its economy and military severely damaged over eight months of war — is eager to end the conflict.

“We’re dealing with them now. They want to make a deal very badly,” he said.

Trump called Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani on Friday to discuss efforts to end the war.

Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian said this week his government was still trying to resolve the crisis through dialogue.

Early on Saturday, Iran’s Tasnim news agency reported that two missiles had struck Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, adding there was no official information about any damage.

Iranian state television reported two explosions on the island.

The Iranian army said early Saturday that its air defences had “struck and destroyed” a US drone that was flying over the island, according to state media. It did not say whether the island was attacked.

World.title: Cavs thump 76ers in James return, Celtics crush Hornets
World.content:
Los Angeles – The Cleveland Cavaliers spoiled LeBron James’s latest homecoming on Friday, beating Philadelphia 119-95 to snap the 76ers’ five-game NBA winning streak.

James, playing his first game in Cleveland since opting to head to Philadelphia as a free agent in June rather than returning for a third stint with his hometown Cavs, was greeted by warm cheers — and scattered boos — when he was introduced.

The four-time NBA champion, playing his 24th NBA season at the age of 41, was cheered again when he exited the game late in the fourth quarter.

In between it was a rough night for James and his Sixers teammates, who suffered just their second defeat of the young season.

The league’s all-time leading scorer finished with eight points on three-of-12 shooting with seven rebounds, three assists, two steals and six turnovers.

Star center Joel Embiid missed all nine of his shots from the floor, making six free throws for six points.

Jaylen Brown, like James an off-season import, led the Sixers with 20 points, but the Cavaliers seized control early and repelled every Philadelphia surge to halt their two-game slide.

Donovan Mitchell scored 10 of his 23 points in the first quarter. Evan Mobley added 22 points, and Cleveland out-rebounded Philadelphia 56-42 despite the injury absence of center Jarrett Allen.

“I did not feel in a good rhythm offensively,” James said. “We didn’t look like much offensively. We had a couple of spurts. We were able to cut (the deficit) to three in the third quarter. But too many turnovers on my behalf.”

Friday’s games were part of NBA Cup group-stage action. The New York Knicks won the in-season tournament last year before going on to win their first NBA title since 1973.

Group-stage Cup games will be played throughout November, all counting in the regular-season standings. Quarter-finals will be played December 4-5 and semi-finals December 8-9 before the final on December 11 at Hinkle Fieldhouse in Indianapolis, Indiana.

The Boston Celtics drained a whopping 24 three-pointers on 44 attempts in a 119-80 blowout of the Hornets in Charlotte.

Jayson Tatum, back after sitting out Wednesday’s win over the Bucks, drilled five three-pointers on the way to a game-high 34 points for Boston — who led by as many as 46 points in the wire-to-wire win.

“I thought every shot he took was a great shot,” Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla said of Tatum, who added eight rebounds and nine assists.

– Thunder roll past Grizzlies –

The Oklahoma City Thunder continued their dominance of the Grizzlies with a 128-97 win in Memphis.

Ajay Mitchell scored a career-high 35 points and two-time defending NBA Most Valuable Player Shai Gilgeous-Alexander added 28 for the Thunder, who notched a 13th straight regular-season win over the Grizzlies despite missing injured starters Jaylen Williams, Cason Wallace and Chet Holmgren.

The absences were irrelevant as the Thunder jumped to a 71-49 halftime lead.

Memphis dropped their third straight defeat after opening the season with six straight wins.

In Dallas, Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving came alive in the second half to help the Mavericks beat the Utah Jazz 112-100.

Dallas forward P.J. Washington scored 22 of his 26 points in a first half that ended tied 57-57.

Flagg, who scored four points before the break, finished with 21 and Irving, held to two points in the first half, finished with 14 as Dallas used a big third quarter to gain control and held on down the stretch.

World.title: Cyberattack shuts down internet fan fiction library
World.content:
Los Angeles – One of the world’s most popular fan fiction libraries has been dark for over a week after a cyberattack forced it offline, leaving millions of fans without access to their favorite stories.

Since October 29, anyone trying to reach Archive of Our Own — known to devotees as AO3 — has been met with a message saying the site is down for maintenance.

“It’s all over my social feed. People are in withdrawal,” Johanna Sarriot, a writer and co-founder of pop-up romance bookstore Love Love Books in Los Angeles, told AFP.

Fan fiction refers to stories written by amateur authors using characters and worlds from already-existing books, films or TV shows.

Contributors rewrite endings, invent romances or give minor characters their own adventures, then share them online for free.

Once a niche hobby, it has become a launchpad for the publishing industry, generating breakout smashes like E.L. James’s “Fifty Shades of Grey,” which began as “Twilight” fan fiction, and Ali Hazelwood’s bestseller “The Love Hypothesis,” which sprang from the “Star Wars” universe.

Launched in 2008, AO3 has become the genre’s main home, with more than 11 million registered users and nearly 18 million works stored on the platform.

In 2019, it won a Hugo Award for Best Related Work, one of science fiction’s most prestigious prizes.

“We wanted to make sure that there was a place for fans to engage in non-commercial creativity in ways that wouldn’t barrage them with ads, censor them to placate advertisers, sell their data, or do anything but provide a space for fandom,” said Harvard Law School professor Rebecca Tushnet, who helped found the Organization for Transformative Works (OTW) which runs the site.

– ‘AO3 is not gone’ –

Romance fans have been among the hardest hit by the outage.

“Romance readers read really fast and they read a lot,” explained Sarriot.

For the bookseller, what is at stake goes beyond a website. Fan fiction is where many future authors learn their craft and where readers disover new writers.

“Writers who were able to cut their teeth on fanfiction, and just write as much as they wanted with all the joy and no constraints, can lead to really great novels,” she said.

OTW says it does not believe the user database, which holds usernames, email addresses and encrypted passwords, was stolen, but cannot rule it out.

“AO3 is not gone! There is no data loss and we look forward to restoring the site as soon as possible,” Tushnet added.

The non-profit says it hopes to have things up and running again within a month.

For web developer Yohan Mebrouk, the timeline is a sign of how serious the attack was.

The delay could reflect limited resources, he explained, or the need for a full software upgrade, which he called “an enormous job.”

Well-run sites keep backup copies of their databases, he added. “If they did things right, everyone will get everything back.”

In the meantime, Sarriot is happy to point stranded readers elsewhere.

“Come to Love Love Books and check out a romance novel!” she said, pointing to her shelves full of paperbacks.

World.title: US offers $20 mn reward for info on Iran’s nuclear program
World.content:
Washington – Washington is offering a $20 million reward “and possible relocation” for information about Iran’s nuclear program, the US military said Friday, as President Donald Trump reiterated Tehran wants to make a deal to end the war.

A State Department program, Rewards for Justice, “is offering a reward of up to $20 million and possible relocation for information about Iran’s nuclear program, including its facilities, equipment, and associated personnel, such as those in the scientific community,” US Central Command said on X.

The program was established in 1984 under the State Department’s national security rewards program to offer money for information that protects American lives and interests.

In its statement about the reward, the State Department said Iran’s “lack of compliance with the IAEA (International Atomic Energy Agency) on safeguards obligations has led to the agency’s loss of ‘continuity of knowledge’ regarding Iran’s production and inventory of key components like centrifuges.

It gave no specific parameters on what information would yield a $20 million reward.

Trump has repeatedly said US forces have effectively obliterated Iran’s nuclear program.

“If we didn’t hit Iran, you wouldn’t have Israel today,” Trump said Friday night in West Palm Beach, Florida. “If they had nuclear, they would have used nuclear. They would have obliterated the Middle East.”

But the president also said Iran — which he stressed has had its economy and military severely damaged over eight months of war — is eager to end the conflict.

“We’re dealing with them now. They want to make a deal very badly,” he said.

Diplomatic efforts by mediators have been in full swing in an attempt to prevent any resumption of fighting.

And on Tuesday Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian said his government was still trying to resolve the crisis through dialogue.

Earlier this week Trump said he still had to “take care” of one or two targets, including so-called Pickaxe Mountain in central Iran, a suspected nuclear site which Tehran denies is such a facility.

World.title: US detains Lawrence aide Harry Boxer, extradition efforts on
World.content:
NEW DELHI

:

Notorious gangster Hari Chand Jaat, aka Harry Boxer, has been detained in US at the instance of Indian law enforcement agencies. Boxer was apprehended in California Friday and efforts are on to bring him back to India, sources said.

Coming close on heels of gangster Himanshu Bhau's detention, the development has sent ripples across the underworld, with many gangsters planning to leave US, they said.

Indian security and intelligence agencies had been closely tracking Boxer's movements since the firing incident at film director Rohit Shetty's home in Mumbai earlier this year. His detention is being seen as a big breakthrough as Boxer operated a core module of the Lawrence Bishnoi criminal syndicate from overseas.



His name had also surfaced in connection with firing incidents at comedian Kapil Sharma's cafe in Canada, besides several cases across Delhi, Rajasthan, Punjab and Haryana.

Boxer (40), a resident of Chatarpura village in Kotputli-Behror of Rajasthan, earned his moniker due to his background as a sports enthusiast and boxing coach. Transitioning from a sporting and farming background, he moved into the underworld and has been absconding since 2022, eventually fleeing India.

NEW DELHI: Contributions received by the Congress in excess of Rs 20,000 totalled Rs 130.7 crore in 2025-26, which is barely one-fourth of its Rs 517.4 crore donation receipts in 2024-25.As per the 2025-26 contribution report of the Congress filed with EC, Prudent Electoral Trust contributed 19% of Congress's total donation kitty in the relevant year. In 2024-25, Prudent had accounted for 41.8% of contributions received by Congress.Prudent is the only electoral trust through which donations, largely corporate, were routed to Congress last year. At Rs 25 crore, the trust's contributions to the party, however, were only 11.5% of the Rs 216 crore funds it had channelled to the party in 2024-25.The steep 75% decline in Congress's total contributions in excess of Rs 20,000, compared with 2024-25, could be due to several factors. Given that 2024-25 was the general election year, a marked rise (84% as compared to 2023-24) in contributions to the main opposition party was on expected lines. What is interesting though is that the Rs 130.7 crore contribution receipts in 2025-26 are nearly 53% less than the amount it had received even in 2023-24.The steep decline was witnessed despite 2025-26 being the year of Bihar assembly elections and the run-up to elections in Assam, Keralam, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal and Puducherry held in April 2026.The Congress audit report for 2025-26, which is not available yet, will throw light on the party's other sources of funding. In 2024-25, Congress's collection from the issuance and sale of coupons was over Rs 350 crore.Among the key contributors last year, other than Prudent, were Star Cement Ltd (Rs 5 crore), Sajjan Bhajanka (Rs 4 crore), Afnan Constructions (Rs 3 crore), Prem Kumar Bhajanka (Rs 2 crore) and IPSUM Proadvisors and SMS Builders (Rs 1 crore each).Just nine contributions of Rs 1 crore or more accounted for Rs 43 crore, or nearly one-third of the party's total receipts. In comparison, 1,321 contributions of Rs 5 lakh or less together added up to Rs 37.2 crore, accounting for just 28.5% of the total. The median contribution among the 1,735 entries was Rs 3 lakh, highlighting how a relatively small number of large donations accounted for a substantial share of the party's funding.

World.title: Elephant calf airlifted from Keralam to Vantara for life-saving treatment
World.content:
Maya, an elephant calf found alone as a newborn on a riverbank 18 months ago, was airlifted from Keralam to Vantara's hospital in Jamnagar on Nov 5, after fractures in both front legs left her unable to stand.

Acting on an initiative by RIL exec director and Vantara founder Anant Ambani, the organisation deployed a specialised veterinary team following a transfer order from Keralam's chief wildlife warden, P Pugazhendi.

Found near Kaprikkad on Apr 19, 2025, the weak, dehydrated newborn had not received her mother's milk and couldn't even suckle. Assistant forest veterinary officer Binoy Babu and caregivers fed and nursed her for over a year.



In July 2026, Maya slipped while playing and injured her shoulder. Despite physiotherapy, splints & supplements, her bones became increasingly fragile. By Oct, she had front-leg fractures, a chest infection and pressure sores. Her prognosis was grave.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

After Kerala's chief wildlife warden sought wider expert opinion, Vantara veterinary adviser Kushal Konwar Sarma identified a possible parathyroid-related disorder that may respond to treatment.





Yaduraj Khadpekar, head veterinarian at Vantara's Elephant Care Centre, concurred, and the medical board unanimously agreed.

Maya travelled by a life-support airlift, accompanied by three Vantara elephant veterinarians, paravets and caregivers, along with Binoy C Babu and her familiar caregiver, Nikhil Babu. She will receive round-the-clock monitoring, pain management, advanced diagnostics, hydraulic lifting support and hydrotherapy where appropriate. Vantara - a global wildlife rescue, care, welfare and conservation initiative based in Jamnagar - will facilitate her return to Abhayaranyam after treatment.

World.title: Hijack hoax forces flight back to Bengaluru
World.content: The discovery of a handwritten note threatening to hijack an IndiGo flight with 178 passengers aboard prompted the pilots to return to Bengaluru just 30 minutes after taking off for Lucknow Saturday evening. "The piece of paper (found in the toilet of the flight) carried the message: 'This plane is going to get hijacked exactly at 6.30. Ignore this and see the consequences.' It was found by a passenger who alerted the cabin crew. The crew immediately conveyed the information to the pilot," a senior police officer told TOI. After the aircraft landed in Bengaluru, security personnel conducted a thorough search of the flight that lasted around 90 minutes. The threat was subsequently declared a hoax, and the flight resumed its journey to Lucknow later at night, the officer added.

World.title: Skill subject to offer class X Board students a second chance
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Students may no longer have to fear failing the class X board exams as the CBSE has introduced a new rule that not only enhances the relevance of vocational education but also offers students an alternative pathway to pass. From 2027-28, students who fail a core academic subject such as Maths, Science or Social Science, will be allowed to use a passed skill subject as a substitute.This rule is only for students who have opted for one of the 22 skill subjects in class IX under vocational education. This excludes Kaushal Vikas, which is also a skill subject but is assessed internally by schools.Under the revised framework, class IX students will study nine subjects, combining core and skill-based courses. Vocational education includes 22 skill-based subjects, including AI, Data Science, Information Technology, Financial Markets, Automotive, Retail, Design Thinking, and Health Care.Under the NCF-SE, vocational education is mandatory from classes VI to X.A senior CBSE official says the goal is to expand choices for students and promote competency-based, experiential learning by embedding activity-based life skills alongside core academics.Class X students now have two attempts to pass CBSE boards in class X. If a student still cannot clear one core subject, this vocational component provides a cushion to clear class X and move to the next grade.A student who fails a core subject but passes class X through a skill subject can still sit for an improvement examination in the failed subject. CBSE does not have any regulation on which stream the student enrols in class XI as that is the school's discretion."Even if the student passes the boards using skill subject marks, he will have to pass Math or Science to enrol in science stream in class XI," adds the official.Teachers dismiss the idea that the replacement rule will dilute academic rigour, viewing it instead as a constructive stress buster. "This provision will help reduce examination stress, particularly among academically weaker students," says a teacher from PM SHRI KV NER Bareilly.

World.title: A century for Bharat Ratna Advani!
World.content:
Shri Lal Krishna Advani Ji enters the hundredth year of his life today, 8th November. This year, his birthday fittingly coincides with

, a festival associated with Prabhu Shri Ram and the Diya at a time when we are marking 75 years since the inception of the Jana Sangh, 125th Jayanti of Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee and recently celebrated a hundred years of the

.

There are very few people whose lives have touched so many different chapters of modern India. Advani Ji was born on 8th November 1927, on Dev Deepawali. As a youngster in 1947, he experienced the pain of leaving behind his familiar world in Sindh. He rebuilt his life from scratch without bitterness. This trait of being able to build from scratch, against all odds, has stayed with him throughout. It was seen while he was strengthening the Jana Sangh and later building the BJP.



His tenures as BJP President saw the Congress falling sharply from 400 to below 200 in 1989 and the BJP becoming the single largest party for the first time in 1996. Advani Ji nurtured generations of Karyakartas and gave the Party a clear foundation rooted in the principle of Nation First.

Two qualities always set Advani Ji apart as a leader. First, his ideological clarity and intellectual sharpness. This was reflected in his speeches and writings.





The Jana Sangh and BJP resolutions he authored remain worth reading even today, while his interviews were consistently incisive and precise. Second, the manner in which he exposed the pseudo-secularism propounded by a large section of the Indian polity for many years.

"Two qualities always set Advani Ji apart as a leader. First, his ideological clarity and intellectual sharpness."

Advani Ji took up every responsibility with immense diligence. As an RSS Pracharak, Advani Ji first worked in different parts of Rajasthan. From there, he went to the national capital, where he started working closely with Atal Ji.

History shows that it is rare for two towering political leaders to work together for several decades, cooperating with each other without becoming competitors. Advani Ji and Atal Ji set a remarkable example.

Together, they changed the course of Indian politics.

The Delhi that Advani Ji came to was coming to terms with the horrors of Partition. He immersed himself in making the Jana Sangh stronger. In 1967, Advani Ji became the Chairman of the Delhi Metropolitan Council, where he worked alongside the late Vijay Kumar Malhotra Ji (who became Chief Executive Councillor).

In 1970, Advani Jiâs Parliamentary innings began. His interventions have won appreciation across the political spectrum. He made a mark as an MP and later, as Leader of Opposition in both houses and from the treasury benches too. Despite parliamentary commitments, he frequently travelled across India meeting people.

"As a voter of Gandhinagar, I also had the honour of voting for Advani Ji on numerous occasions."

I vividly recall the 1991 Lok Sabha elections. It was decided that Advani Ji would contest the Lok Sabha elections from two seats, one of which was Gandhinagar.

He had an old link with Gujarat. His father had settled in Kutch after Partition. Advani Ji had also served as a Rajya Sabha MP from Gujarat. So, it was a homecoming of sorts. Being involved in the BJP organisation, I had the honour of helping prepare his papers and assisting him throughout the campaign.

The people of Gandhinagar sent him to Parliament time and again. As a voter of Gandhinagar, I also had the honour of voting for Advani Ji on numerous occasions.

The care and attention he devoted to his constituency is something to learn from.

The Emergency was a watershed moment in Advani Jiâs life. He was at the forefront of saving democracy and protecting the Constitution. His experiences found their way into his book, âA Prisoner's Scrap-Book.â One part of that book, titled âA Tale of Two Emergenciesâ, beautifully explained the striking similarities between the events in India starting June 1975 and those in Nazi Germany in 1933.

Advani Ji was a fiery Opposition leader but an equally excellent administrator. When the Janata Government came to office in 1977, Advani Ji became Minister for Information and Broadcasting. It is widely accepted that his work in this department was extremely impactful. As Deputy Prime Minister and one of Indiaâs longest-serving Home Ministers, he was instrumental in strengthening Indiaâs security apparatus.

His work in improving the lives of our security forces is remembered with great fondness. His unequivocal stand against terrorism ensured India got a tough anti-terror law.

"Advani Ji was a fiery Opposition leader but an equally excellent administrator."

Of course, an iconic moment in Advani Jiâs life was the Somnath to Ayodhya Rath Yatra. It changed the course of Indian society for the better. I consider it a privilege that I got the opportunity to be involved in this Yatra from the ideation stage to execution.

Being present at Somnath when the Yatra began was particularly special. A Yatra can be very demanding, requiring long hours, constant travel, physical endurance and an ability to remain focused despite fatigue.

Advani Ji embodied this endurance.

I also have memories of the saddening moments of Advani Jiâs arrest in Bihar. Then, in Gujarat, the BJP withdrew support from the Chimanbhai Patel Government. With this, a simple message was given, that when it comes to our ideology and the Ram Temple, there will never be any compromise.

Many of our senior leaders and Karyakartas took an oath that, come what may, a Ram Temple will be built. And, years later, with the blessings of the people of India, a grand Mandir for Prabhu Shri Ram became a reality in Ayodhya.

There is so much more of Advani Ji that is outstanding. His simplicity, for example. After the Navnirman Movement, Advani Ji had come to Junagadh and stayed for a month as an ordinary Karyakarta, preparing the Party for the Assembly elections in which Congress was rejected.

He has always shown what probity in public life is about. He is a voracious reader. Those who have spent time with him know how carefully he goes through newspapers.

He is a big fan of cinema and theatre, and has been an enthusiastic film critic. His sense of history and the need to preserve it is visible in his book, âMy Country My Life.â

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Advani Ji always remained in touch with Sindhi culture. Another effort he undertook was the popularisation of Sindhu Darshan Puja near Leh.

I myself had been to one Puja with Advani Ji and George Fernandes Ji.

Any account of Advani Jiâs remarkable journey would be incomplete without mentioning Kamla Advani Ji. She was a constant source of strength and support throughout his public life.

Growing up in Karachi, Advani Ji could hardly have imagined the path his life would take. In an expression of gratitude, the people of India conferred upon him the Bharat Ratna in 2024. As Advani Ji enters the hundredth year of his life, I pray that he be blessed with good health and that he continues to inspire us all as he has always done.

World.title: NMC sounds alarm over fake medical colleges, warns students against paying admission fees without verification
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The National Medical Commission (NMC) has warned students and parents against falling victim to fake medical colleges, fraudulent admission offers and forged approval documents, following a Supreme Court case involving a purported medical college allegedly operating from a farmhouse.

In an advisory, the medical regulator said some institutions were offering medical and allied courses without the requisite statutory approval or recognition. Misleading s, websites, social media promotions and unauthorised admission offers could leave students and parents vulnerable to fraud, it cautioned.

The warning follows the Supreme Court's intervention in Ayesha Jain vs Amity University, Noida & Others, in which it directed regulatory bodies, including the NMC, to alert students and parents against enrolling in institutions without first verifying their authenticity.



The NMC has specifically cautioned that a college figuring on its official list does not necessarily mean it has permission to admit students for the current academic year. Students must check the college's approval for the relevant year and its sanctioned intake through official NMC and Medical Assessment and Rating Board records.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

It has also advised candidates not to rely on brochures, websites, s or purported Letters of Permission circulated by institutions.





Admissions should be pursued through official counselling channels, including the Medical Counselling Committee wherever applicable, or the respective state counselling authorities.

The regulator has warned against making payments to unauthorised agents, personal bank accounts or unverified intermediaries. It has also clarified that approval or affiliation from another authority cannot be treated as NMC permission to run an MBBS course.

Students can report suspected fake colleges, forged approval letters and fraudulent admission offers to the NMC, state medical education departments or local police.

World.title: Trump offers UFC boss press secretary post, urges criminal probes of Democrats
World.content:
Facing an incoming Democratic Congress, U.S. President Donald Trump struck a combative tone Saturday (November 7, 2026), offering friend and “violent fighter” Dana White the White House press secretary job and ordering the Justice Department to investigate his opponents.

Democrats handed Mr. Trump’s Republicans a blowout defeat in the midterm elections this week and will take control of both chambers of Congress in January. They promise robust investigations into Mr. Trump and his administration.

Mr. Trump, however, showed no signs of being chastened.

He offered the press secretary post to Mr. White, a loyal supporter and head of the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) mixed martial arts organisation.

“Dana, please take the job!” Mr. Trump posted on social media, describing White as a “violent Fighter and Warrior.”

Speaking to reporters following a boxing event in London late Saturday (November 7, 2026), Mr. White said he was flying to Washington “right now” and will meet with Mr. Trump on Monday (November 9, 2026).

“I’ll have more to talk about after that,” he said.

Mr. White had earlier shared a photo -- possibly AI-generated -- showing him behind the lectern in the White House press briefing room, captioned “On to the next chapter.”

Mr. Trump on Saturday (November 7, 2026) also ordered the Justice Department to investigate Democrats for “extortion at the highest level.”

“The Democrats are going around threatening a lot of people,” he wrote, adding that he was ordering the Justice Department to “look into this criminal act.”

Denying that anyone in his administration had committed impeachable offenses, Trump called for prison time for “these EXTORTIONISTS.”

Combative

Saturday’s (November 7, 2026) announcements came a day after Mr. Trump appointed Stephen Miller to be his next chief of staff, describing the combative senior adviser as “a great fighter.”

He replaces Susie Wiles, whose departure marks the first staffing fallout from the Republican election debacle.

The pugilistic posts echoed comments Mr. Trump made after a smaller midterm defeat in 2018, when he said his White House would assume “a war-like posture” against any investigations. Mr. Trump was subsequently impeached in 2019 and 2021.

The White House has been without a press secretary since October 16 when Katie Zacharia left the position after less than a week on the job.

Mr. White, 57, is president and CEO of the UFC, the largest and most successful company in the world of mixed martial arts whose violent cage fights are broadcast across the globe.

Mr. Trump listed six UFC fighters that he hoped White would bring to the White House as advisers, “even though some are not from our Country.”

“We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left,” he said of the fighters, who include two Russians and one Brazilian.

Mr. Trump and Mr. White are old friends, and the U.S. leader has often tried to associate his MAGA brand of politics with the hugely popular UFC.

On his 80th birthday in June, UFC held a bloody cage match on the White House South Lawn. He has also attended bouts in Miami, New York and New Jersey since winning his second White House term.

When Mr. Trump won reelection in 2024, Mr. White appeared alongside the Republican for his victory speech.

Criminal act

If Mr. White formally accepts, he will have his work cut out for him.

Mr. Trump faces a radically transformed and hostile political landscape after Democrats seized both the House of Representatives and the Senate in Tuesday’s (November 10, 2026) midterms.

With control of committees in both chambers, Democrats can summon officials, demand documents and hold public hearings, potentially putting Mr. Trump and his senior aides under intense scrutiny.

Likely probes include the Mr. Trump family’s business and cryptocurrency dealings, government contracts involving billionaire Elon Musk, cuts to federal agencies, immigration enforcement, the conduct of the Iran war and the handling of files related to notorious sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

“Lawyer up,” wrote incoming House Oversight Committee chairman Robert Garcia on X as results became clear on election night.

Democrats could pursue a third impeachment against Mr. Trump, though party leaders have not promised it.

While the House needs only a simple majority to impeach the President, removing him requires a two-thirds vote in the Senate, far beyond the party’s majority.

World.title: Singapore-based senior IT executive shot dead over parking dispute in Faridabad
World.content:
A 42-year-old senior executive of a Singapore-based IT services and solutions company was shot dead following a dispute over parking in Faridabad on Friday (November 6, 2026) evening. The police have arrested the accused, identified as Mohan Sharma, a real estate agent who lived on the third floor of the same multi-storey building in Sector 21C where the victim resided with his family.

The victim, Paramjith Dhankhar, had returned from Singapore two days ago to attend a family wedding and celebrate Deepavali with his family.

According to the complaint filed by his 19-year-old son, Shaurya, the accused rang the doorbell of their flat around 8.30 p.m. and asked Mr. Dhankhar, who had returned from the gym a few minutes earlier, to come downstairs and move his car. Shaurya also accompanied his father to the parking area.

An argument reportedly broke out between the two men, following which Mr. Sharma allegedly pulled out a pistol and fired several rounds at Mr. Dhankhar. He also fired at Shaurya, who managed to escape unhurt by taking cover behind parked cars. The accused then fled the spot in his vehicle. Mr. Dhankhar succumbed to his bullet injuries.

“About 14-15 rounds were fired, of which eight or nine reportedly hit the victim. His son, who was present at the spot, escaped unhurt,” said Surajkund police station SHO Inspector Pahlad. The SHO said the two men had differences earlier as well and the accused allegedly used to create disturbances after consuming alcohol.

A case was registered at the Surajkund police station under charges of murder, attempt to murder and criminal conspiracy. The accused was subsequently arrested by the Sector 30 Crime Branch team on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

World.title: Morning Digest: Cash usage unchanged, fake notes on the rise after 10 years since demonetisation; Eisenkot tapped to try to form government, and more
World.content:
10 years since demonetisation: Cash usage unchanged, fake notes on the rise

Ten years after demonetisation, Reserve Bank of India (RBI) data show that the exercise has had little impact on reducing cash in circulation and that detection of counterfeit notes, particularly ₹500 notes, has also increased. On the other hand, the value of transactions on the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) has grown steadily year after year, even when measured as a percentage of India’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

Israeli President picks Gadi Eisenkot, Netanyahu rival, to try to form government

Israel’s president on Saturday (November 7, 2026) chose Gadi Eisenkot, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s strongest rival, to try ‌to form a new government following a deadlocked election that left neither man with ​a clear path to power. Mr. Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving leader, is fighting to stay in ⁠office after his religious-nationalist coalition lost its majority in an October 27 election but still emerged as the largest bloc in parliament.

NDA extends winning streak, set to crush YSRCP in ZPTC and MPTC elections as well

The TDP and its allies, the JSP and the BJP, continued their stellar performance in the elections to the Zilla and Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituencies (ZPTCs and MPTCs) after crushing the YSRCP in the Urban Local Body (ULB) polls. They were all set to pull off another decisive victory over the YSRCP. Polling was conducted for 582 ZPTCs and 7,767 MPTCs in 28 districts on November 5 following the declaration of 77 and 2,051 ZPTCs and MPTCs respectively as unanimously elected.

Multiple Elector Photo Identity Cards generated for same person during SIR, admits Karnataka CEO

After The Hindu reported that at least 803 voter IDs were linked to 397 people in Mahadevapura Assembly Constituency even after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), which was intended to weed out duplicate entries, the office of the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO), Karnataka, admitted that the discrepancies flagged in the report were due to “procedural circumstances during data processing”. The report highlighted instances of people holding multiple voter IDs within Mahadevapura, as well as cases where the same Elector Photo Identity Card (EPIC) number appeared in the final electoral rolls of two different Assembly constituencies.

T.N. may be heading towards a water crisis, unless northeast monsoon comes to the rescue

Tamil Nadu may be in for a spell of water crisis and lower rice production this time, if the current Northeast monsoon does not come to its rescue. As of now, the aggregate storage in the major 15 irrigation reservoirs is about a third of the combined capacity of the reservoirs. In the corresponding period last year, the situation was completely different with the combined storage being around 92%.

PM Modi conveys Deepavali greetings, says will celebrate the festival with soldiers

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday (November 7, 2026) conveyed Deepavali greetings to the nation, saying that, like in previous years, he will celebrate the festival with the brave soldiers of the country. In a video message posted on his social media handles, Mr. Modi said he will celebrate the festival with great enthusiasm.

CJP founder launches scathing attack on Central government

The Narendra Modi-led central government should go out in the 2029 general elections, Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke said in Kochi on Saturday (November 7) as he unleashed a scathing attack on the former over the alleged electoral malpractices and divisive politics. Addressing a protest named ‘Jantar Mantar @ Kochi’ demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), Mr. Dipke stressed that “Modi will go out in 2029.”

One injured in explosion at Ghaziabad police outpost; ATS, bomb disposal team at site

One person was injured in a blast at a police outpost in Ghaziabad district on Friday night (November 6, 2026). Bomb Disposal Squad, Field Unit and Forensic Team of the Uttar Pradeshpolice gathered all the evidence from the site on Saturday (November 7). The explosion damaged the window panes of the Vasundhara police outpost under the Indirapuram police station. A food delivery person present around the police outpost sustained minor injuries.

Enforcement Directorate is not a ‘super cop’, says Karnataka High Court

In a setback to the Directorate of Enforcement (ED), the High Court of Karnataka has held that the ED is “not a super cop” and cannot file a private complaint to initiate a money-laundering probe when the competent agencies decline to prosecute a scheduled offence based on the information filed by the ED.

Why are the U.S. midterm elections significant?

Midterm elections in the U.S. earlier this week ended President Donald Trump’s trifecta control of the federal government, as Democrats swept the polls and the Republican Party lost control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives. The election result was particularly significant for Democrats as they won historically “red States” such as Texas, South Carolina, North Carolina, Iowa, Kansas, Ohio, and Maine, besides holding onto their traditional strongholds, such as Colorado, Oregon, and Illinois, and retaining control of key swing States, such as Georgia, Michigan, and Virginia.

Trump says he wants UFC chief Dana White for White House press secretary

U.S. President Donald Trump on ​Saturday (November 7, 2026) said he had asked ‌mixed martial arts promoter ​Dana White to serve ⁠as White House press secretary and called on him to ‌bring some fighters along as assistants “even though some ‌are not from our ‌country.” Mr. White, ⁠chief executive of ⁠the Ultimate Fighting Championship, is a “violent Fighter and Warrior,” Mr. Trump wrote in ​a Truth ‌Social post.

U.S. military says it disabled cargo vessel in Gulf of Oman

​An American military aircraft fired ‌on and disabled a commercial vessel ​that tried to ⁠break the U.S. blockade of Iran on Saturday (November 7, 2026), U.S. Central Command ‌said. The St. Kitts-flagged cargo vessel tried to ‌depart regional waters after visiting ‌an ⁠Iranian port, and a ⁠U.S. plane fired precision munitions at its stern after U.S. forces ​directed the crew to ‌abandon targeted spaces, Central Command said. Building on a months-long naval blockade on Iran, ‌the U.S. military also said ​on Saturday (November 7, 2026) it is launching a task ⁠force to crack down on Tehran’s movement of advanced weapons ‌and other sanctioned material over its land borders and through the Caspian Sea.

Explosions heard in areas in southern Iran, Iranian media report

Explosions were heard on Saturday (November 7, 2026) evening in several areas in southern Iran, including on ​Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian state television reported. Iran’s ‌state TV suggested that the explosions might be linked ​to Iranian military activities in the strategic ⁠waterway, which has become subject to repeated attacks on commercial shipping since the war erupted between the U.S. and Iran in February.

World.title: Paraguay's ousted President charged with crimes linked to collapse of major bank
World.content:
Prosecutors in Paraguay on Saturday (November 7, 2026) charged recently deposed former President Santiago Peña with two crimes linked to the collapse of a major bank that has jeopardised the savings of hundreds of thousands of account holders and unleashed the nation's biggest political crisis in a decade.

In a press conference on Saturday (November 7), Nancy Salomón, the South American nation's chief prosecutor for corruption and economic crimes, said Mr. Peña would be investigated for the crimes of breach of trust and administration for personal gain.

Mr. Peña's removal marks a major crisis for Paraguay, which returned to democratic rule in 1989. Since then, the nation of six million people has been mostly governed by the conservative Colorado Party, of which Mr. Peña was a member.

Prosecutors said the former President could face up to 20 years in prison if he is found guilty of both crimes and have asked a judge to freeze Mr. Peña's assets and send him to prison while investigations continue.

Later on Saturday (November 7), Paraguayan Judge Humberto Otazu complied with that request and said Mr. Peña will be held at a military base as investigations continue, in order to “guarantee his compliance” with the anti-corruption probe.

On Tuesday (November 3), regulators in Paraguay intervened in Ueno Bank, freezing the accounts of nearly three million customers and triggering a political crisis that led to Peña's removal by Congress on Friday (November 6) night.

Earlier on Saturday (November 7), Mr. Peña was questioned by prosecutors at the Attorney General's compound, in the capital Asuncion. The former President was not in handcuffs but was escorted by police.

Lawmakers accused Mr. Peña of using his political influence to steer hundreds of millions of dollars in public funds into Ueno while regulators overlooked risky insider lending. Mr. Peña has denied wrongdoing.

Paraguayan prosecutors on Friday (November 6) ordered the arrest of Mr. Peña and former Central Bank chief Carlos Carvallo as part of a criminal investigation into alleged breach of trust and other offenses tied to the collapse of Ueno Bank. Peña was transferred to a military base late Friday (November 6) as hundreds of protesters gathered outside his home.

The arrest order was issued soon after the Senate removed Mr. Peña from office in a unanimous vote. He was replaced by Vice-President Pedro Alliana, who began naming a new Cabinet on Saturday (November 7). The Central Bank said Saturday that 1.2 million Ueno customers had received partial or full reimbursement of their deposits. Under Paraguayan law, deposits of up to $37,000 are insured.

Mr. Peña submitted his resignation on Thursday (November 5), but Congress did not accept it and pressed ahead with an impeachment trial. Opposition lawmakers insisted on his removal to prevent him from leaving office with immunity.

“He must go, but not home. He must go to a maximum-security prison,” opposition Sen Yolanda Paredes told reporters. “The public is fed up with impunity.”

In a farewell message released shortly before he was ousted on Friday (November 6), Mr. Peña expressed hope his departure would spare Paraguay further harm.

“I do not want my presence to be a cause of greater division or instability,” he wrote. “My responsibility is to put the country above my personal fate.”

Public outrage has intensified by the day. Thousands of protesters demanding access to their frozen savings and accountability for Ueno's failure have clashed with police firing rubber bullets and pepper spray this week. Paraguay's largest teachers' union, which has more than 40,000 members, plans to begin an indefinite national strike on Monday (November 9) to press for protection of public pension funds.

On Saturday (November 7), a few dozen protesters gathered outside the Attorney General's compound hoping to express their frustration with Mr. Peña, who was driven quickly out of the building.

Some of the protesters said they also want Paraguay's new President, who was a close ally of Mr. Peña, to be investigated.

“They are all accomplices,” said Liliana Jara, a demonstrator who showed up at the site. “They are part of the same clique.”

World.title: Strong earthquake with preliminary magnitude of 5.7 strikes Japan
World.content:
A strong earthquake shook central Japan early Sunday (November 8, 2026), shattering store windows, causing people to flee buildings and leaving at least 22 people injured, according to local media.

Japan's Meteorological Agency put the quake's magnitude at 5.7, while the U.S. Geological Survey reported it at magnitude 5.5. Smaller aftershocks were reported.

A wide area near Aichi Prefecture was affected, including the city of Hamamatsu, the ancient capitals of Kyoto and Nara and nearby prefectures of Yamanashi, where Mount Fuji is located, as well as Gifu.

Japanese TV footage showed shattered store windows and scattered shards of glass on the streets. A bookstore was left with mounds of books that had flown off the shelves. The injuries included people who fell down stairs while they were trying to flee.

The quake, which struck at 1:04 a.m. local time, was located about 40 km below the Earth's surface in Shizuoka Prefecture. Aichi and Shizuoka are neighbouring regions. They are far enough from Tokyo that the quake was not felt there. The most violent shaking was felt in Aichi, according to official seismic assessments.

The Shinkansen bullet trains were running at slower speeds in the affected areas as a precautionary measure. Sometimes quakes can damage the railways the trains run on.

Japan is located in an area that is prone to earthquakes.

World.title: Explosions heard in areas in southern Iran, Iranian media report
World.content:
Explosions were heard on Saturday (November 7, 2026) evening in several areas in southern Iran, including on ​Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian state television reported.

Iran’s ‌state TV suggested that the explosions might be linked ​to Iranian military activities in the strategic ⁠waterway, which has become subject to repeated attacks on commercial shipping since the war erupted between the U.S. and Iran in February.

It said Iranian ‌officials have not confirmed any missile strikes on the areas, while the semi-official Tasnim news agency cited ‌a source as saying that the explosions heard ‌on ⁠Qeshm Island were not related to missile strikes.

Iran’s Revolutionary ⁠Guards Navy said early on Sunday (November 8, 2026) that two oil tankers were on fire after hitting mines as they attempted to pass through an “unauthorised route” in ​the strait. It was not ‌immediately clear if the incidents referred to by the IRGC were linked to the sound of explosions heard in southern Iranian areas.

Iran has hit vessels it says have ‌violated its restrictions on passage through the waterway, as it ​seeks to assert control over the strait and exert pressure on Washington.

Earlier on Saturday (November 7, 2026), Tasnim news ⁠agency said two missiles struck Qeshm Island with no official information on possible damage.

The reported explosions come days after the U.S. ‌carried out strikes on the island. A U.S. official said those strikes were limited and not a resumption of major combat operations.

Countries in the region had been anticipating that U.S. President ⁠Donald Trump, who has held off on strikes on Iran during ⁠the weeks leading up to midterm elections, could restart attacks once the voting was over. Iran ‌has repeatedly said it would respond to new attacks by striking at U.S. and Israeli targets in neighbouring countries.

World.title: A bridge between past and present
World.content:
On November 3, Soumya Pathak, 23, a final-year medical student studying at a medical college in Ambala, Haryana, is exploring exhibits showcasing relics from prehistoric times at the Bihar Museum in Patna. Pathak belongs to Muzaffarpur in Bihar, and is looking at some coins from the Mauryan (321–185 B.C.E) and Gupta ages (early 4th to mid-6th Century C.E.).

She passes through interactive galleries which highlight Bihar’s pivotal role in shaping two major world religions: Jainism and Buddhism. “I have been thinking of coming here for a long time, but after reading on social media that the museum is ranked the best in Asia, I decided to spend a day here,” she says. Pathak is enroute to Muzaffarpur for the Deepavali holidays and came to the museum directly from Patna’s Jay Prakash Narayan airport, about four kilometres away. Pathak is proud of her State that is often in the news for poverty and violence.

World.title: Govt announces auto policy with focus on cheaper vehicles, EVs
World.content:
The federal government on Saturday introduced the new auto policy, with a special focus on cheaper vehicles and electric vehicles (EVs).

Information Minister Attaullah Tarar and Adviser to the Prime Minister for Industries and Production Haroon Akhtar Khan announced the policy while addressing a press conference in Islamabad.

Akhtar said the process of the cabinet’s approval began today, with Tarar saying they wanted to address the speculations before moving on to the approval.

The PM’s adviser emphasised that a lot of work was done in drafting the policy, adding that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had invested a lot of time in this regard.

He explained that the policy rested on six pillars: cheaper vehicles, especially for the middle class and lower middle class; encouraging exports; localisation; vehicle safety; promotion of EVs; and transparency.

The adviser said that the government intends to finance the proposed incentives for EVs through an automotive development levy (ADL) on vehicles powered by internal combustion engines (ICE) above 1,000cc — ordinary cars.

He said that the premier had introduced a tariff policy, the purpose of which was to lower the cost of production and the import bill of raw materials.

The policy sets a cumulative export target of $6 billion over five years. Akhtar noted that Pakistan’s auto exports remained limited, with most overseas shipments comprising parts rather than vehicles manufactured by local assemblers.

“You will see that prices of cars will come down … the manufacturing cost of automakers will come down; these were the prime minister’s specific instructions. The prices of all vehicles, except luxury vehicles, will come down,” Akhtar said.

He explained that prices would come down gradually as the duties for completely built units (CBUs), assembly plants and components would be reduced each year, eventually leading to competitive tariffs after five years.

He stressed that the government did not want Pakistan’s automotive industry to remain dependent on the import of CBUs or merely assemble completely knocked-down (CKD) kits without developing a strong domestic manufacturing base.

The PM’s adviser stated that there was no monopoly of any automaker in the market and currently there were 16 car or sport utility vehicle (SUV) makers and 100 two-wheeler manufacturers in Pakistan.

He added that the new policy will address the issue of additional charges commonly known as “on-money” in vehicle bookings; the policy makes it mandatory for manufacturers not to charge more than 20 per cent of the vehicle price as an advance payment at the time of booking.

The PM’s industries aide said localisation had been made mandatory, with targets to be given to manufacturers.

He added that a “rewards and penalty” system will also be introduced to boost exports, under which exporters will get 5 per cent Duty Drawback on Local Taxes and Levies (DLTL), with an additional 10pc incentive on incremental annual export growth.

“But if you do not achieve the targets, a penalty will be imposed as well,” he warned, adding that car manufacturers will not get DLTL unless they achieve the entire export target as well as their local manufacturing target.

Akhtar stressed that the government had made the export rebate conditional on the local manufacturing target, noting that PM Shehbaz wanted more jobs to be created in the country through increased plants.

Speaking on vehicle safety, Akhtar said the policy includes 45 additional safety standards in line with the United Nations’ WP.29 code. He contended, “When our vehicles will go through these safety codes, they will be considered the world’s safest vehicles — both manufactured and used.”

He said that the absence of adequate safety standards, particularly in imported used vehicles, had been a serious concern, referring to recurring road accidents caused by issues such as defective brakes and tyre failures.

Incentives for EV sector

The production adviser further said that the government’s aim of transitioning 30pc of all new vehicles in Pakistan to electric power by 2030 was “about to happen sooner than that”.

Explaining a “major benefit” for EVs, he said three categories of sales taxes have been planned — 1pc on purely electric vehicles, 6pc on range-extended (REEVs) and 9pc on hybrid EVs. However, he added this was subject to approval by the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

Akhtar also said no capital value tax (CVT), withholding tax or federal excise duty (FED) would be applicable on EVs that are priced up to $50,000. EVs above this will be considered “luxury” items and will be subject to normal taxation.

Furthermore, the State Bank of Pakistan’s car financing plan, which offers up to Rs3 million for ordinary cars, will be expanded up to Rs10m for all EVs, along with the tenure extended from three years to five years.

Akhtar went on to note that the government will also incentivise setting up charging stations, explaining that this was a key step in the ultimate goal of shifting to pure EVs, with hybrid and REEVs aiding in the transition period.

He said the government will fund the viability gap that currently exists, with the business community facing a lack of demand for charging stations, while consumers needed those stations in order to switch to EVs.

Sales tax on the equipment for charging stations has been reduced to 1pc, while customs duty has been removed.

Akhtar said that due to the government being committed to an IMF programme, it was aiming for “neutral revenue on whatever incentives we are giving”, adding that revenue would be collected from ICE vehicles above 1,000cc rather than EVs, so that lower and middle-income groups using cars less than 1,000cc are exempted.

He added that the revenue collected will also be used for export rebates and research and development.

Akhtar highlighted that following the launch of the New Energy Vehicle (NEV) Policy 2025-30 last year, the number of electric two-wheelers sold increased to 240,000 in FY25-26 from 60,000 in FY2024-25.

He identified the promotion of EVs as another major priority, particularly in view of Pakistan’s vulnerability to fluctuations in international oil prices.

He explained that rising oil prices increase the country’s import bill, put pressure on the current account and contribute to inflationary pressures.

‘Need of the time’

Addressing the press conference, the information minister regretted that under “protectionist policies” in past decades, wherein import duties were increased and local industry was supported, the local industry did not innovate or make value additions.

Tarar noted the increased use of electric motorcycles and scooties, terming it a “need of the time”. He also pointed out the need to prevent or even reduce the increasing import bills for oil, which in turn impacts the public through rising fuel prices.

He emphasised that no changes were made under the policy to ordinary petrol vehicles under 1,000cc, as many common citizens still use those.

On a question about rampant availability of non-custom-paid vehicles in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, where governor’s rule was imposed on Oct 11, Tarar said the province now has a transparent set-up working on the issue.

A formal policy is being framed so that no vehicle remains unregistered and all are registered through the Customs and Excise departments, he added, affirming that such issues contributing to terrorism were being addressed.

In a post on X, Tarar said the new policy was developed after consultations with all stakeholders, analysis of technical data, and a review of various global models.

“Innovation, value addition, and localisation will be promoted in the local industry to create employment opportunities and enable vehicle exports,” he said.

The minister highlighted that encouraging EVs will reduce carbon emissions and the oil import bill, adding that incentives have also been provided for establishing charging stations.

He termed the initiative a “significant step toward providing Pakistani citizens with affordable, high-quality, and environmentally friendly transportation”.

World.title: Israeli president picks Netanyahu's rival Gadi Eisenkot to try to form government
World.content:
Israel’s president on Saturday chose Gadi Eisenkot, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s strongest rival, to try to form a new government following a deadlocked election that left neither man with a clear path to power.

Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving leader, is fighting to stay in office after his religious-nationalist coalition lost its majority in an Oct 27 election but still emerged as the largest bloc in parliament.

Eisenkot, a former military chief, has declined to join forces with Arab parties, with whose support he would have a majority of seats in parliament.

But Arab leaders, incensed by what they view as the racist policies of Netanyahu and his far-right allies, still nominated Eisenkot to try to form a government first giving him the most endorsements.

“President Herzog has invited Gadi Eisenkot to the President’s Residence, where he will be tasked with forming the government tomorrow,” said the spokesperson of President Isaac Herzog, whose largely ceremonial role involves nominating a candidate to form a coalition after elections.

As part of this process, the president met Eisenkot and Netanyahu, among others, a statement by Herzog’s office said.

At the end of the consultations, factions comprising 67 Knesset members recommended to the president that Yashar party’s Eisenkot be tasked with forming the government, while factions comprising 46 Knesset members recommended Likud’s Netanyahu, the statement noted.

Meanwhile, seven Knesset members chose not to recommend anyone.

“Now is the time to form a national emergency government. I will do everything to ensure we are worthy,” Eisenkot wrote on X in his first reaction to the announcement of his designation.

Eisenkot faces long-shot bid to form govt

Weeks of protracted negotiations are expected to follow Eisenkot’s nomination. He has 28 days to try to forge a government, with a possible 14-day extension.

His potential pathways to power include trying to form a minority government with Arab support from the outside; forming a coalition with ultra-Orthodox parties that he and his allies have shunned in the past; or forging a unity government with Netanyahu.

Analysts say that all three options are unlikely to take shape.

If Eisenkot fails, another candidate can try to form a government and if that candidate fails, parliament can nominate another. There is a deadline for the process of around 100 days. If no one succeeds, another election is held.

Likud won the most seats of any single party with 27 in the 120-seat Knesset, but Netanyahu’s wider religious-nationalist coalition garnered only 53 in total, short of a 61-seat majority.

Eisenkot’s Yashar party emerged as the second-largest party with 21 seats, while his coalition, spanning four centre-left to right-wing Jewish-led parties, won just 48 seats. Two parties representing Israel’s Arab minority won an unprecedented 19 seats.

The result underscored the rightward shift among Israeli Jews during Netanyahu’s years as the country’s dominant political figure. The centre-left that dominated Israel for the first half of its history has been reduced to a small fringe.

Nearly all Jewish parties now share Netanyahu’s rejection of an eventual independent Palestinian state, the basis of internationally endorsed peace efforts since the 1990s.

Eisenkot and Netanyahu have both ​said they would not form a government with parties primarily representing Israeli citizens of Palestinian descent, who comprise around a fifth of the population.

A son of Moroccan immigrants, Eisenkot, 66, would be the country’s first prime minister from Israel’s Mizrahi community, Jews who trace their roots to the Middle East and North Africa.

Eisenkot only entered politics in 2022. He briefly served in Netanyahu’s wartime cabinet following Hamas’s Oct 7, 2023, attack on Israel before returning to the opposition. Eisenkot’s son and two nephews were killed fighting in Gaza.

How different are Eisenkot’s views from Netanyahu?

Eisenkot offers a break with Netanyahu’s leadership and far-right allies, but not with the hawkish security views that have hardened since Oct 7, 2023: he opposes Palestinian statehood and says Hamas’s military wing must be destroyed or dismantled.

Beyond that, Eisenkot has said Israel’s next government must prevent Iran from acquiring a military nuclear capability, either by force or through an “arrangement” such as a US-backed diplomatic solution.

He has emphasised his security credentials on the campaign trail, citing his “Dahiya doctrine” of responding to attacks with disproportionate force, which he deployed as a commander during Israel’s 2006 war with Hezbollah in Lebanon.

Eisenkot shares many of Netanyahu’s views on security and has backed the Gaza offensive that has reduced the territory to rubble.

Israel’s relentless campaign in response to the Hamas attacks killed over 74,000 Palestinians and has left it increasingly isolated on the world stage, with Amnesty International , Human Rights Watch and experts declaring its actions in Gaza as a “genocide”, which Tel Aviv rejects.

Both Eisenkot and Netanyahu say Israeli troops will not withdraw from Gaza until Hamas ​is disarmed, and that Israel is prepared to ​restart fighting to achieve this.

Eisenkot says the ⁠continued rule of Hamas in Gaza is a profound failure, and that within 18 months of taking office he would ensure that the Hamas administration had been replaced, either through a US-brokered plan or through military force.

From the opposition, Eisenkot publicly rebuked Netanyahu over his leadership, including his management of the military campaign in Gaza, and has sworn that he would not serve in government with him.

Although Eisenkot has criticised settler violence against Palestinians in occupied West Bank, which has surged since 2023, he favours settlement in principle and says it should comply with Israeli law.

He opposes settlements built without authorisation, aims to dismantle outposts in areas where ​they are forbidden and has pledged to rein in violent settlers.

Hundreds of thousands of Israelis live in the West Bank, settling in territory Israel occupied in a 1967 war, a practice nearly all countries consider illegal under international law.

Netanyahu and ​Eisenkot both say Israel must retain ultimate security control over all territory between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean Sea.

There are, however, differences in their emphasis. Eisenkot’s position on limiting settlements ​in the West Bank would reserve territory where Palestinians now exercise civil self-rule. Netanyahu’s coalition includes parties that openly call for Israel to fully annex occupied Palestinian land.

World.title: 'Please take the job': Trump asks UFC chief Dana White to be White House press secretary
World.content:
US President Donald Trump said on Saturday he had asked mixed martial ​arts promoter Dana White to serve ‌as White House press secretary and called on him to bring some fighters ​along as assistants “even though some ​are not from our country.”

White, chief ⁠executive of the Ultimate Fighting ​Championship, is a “violent Fighter and Warrior,” Trump ​wrote in a Truth Social post.

Trump asked for six current or former UFC titleholders to join White, including ​two athletes from Russia’s Dagestan ​region, Islam Makhachev and Khabib Nurmagomedov; Americans Justin ‌Gaethje, ⁠Daniel Cormier and “Kayla Harris,” likely a reference to Kayla Harrison; and Amanda Nunes, a Brazilian native who became ​an ​American citizen ⁠last year.

“We need these people to defend us against the ​Lunatic Left,” Trump wrote. White ​and ⁠UFC’s parent company, TKO Group Holdings, did not immediately return requests for comment.

Last month, White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia was “let go”, less than a week after she had taken on the role after Trump said he had told her to reconsider the job following public scrutiny.

“I told her: ‘I think you’re better off being happy, and I’m not sure you can ever be happy in this stuff.’ There’s nothing easy about this stuff,” Trump told reporters.

Zacharia had acknowledged that she had failed the bar exam, a prerequisite for practising law in the United States. She had earlier described herself as a lawyer during television appearances and on social media, and listed herself as general counsel of a California-based conservative nonprofit.

World.title: Pakistan's men down South Korea to win Asian Team Squash title
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan defeated South Korea 2-0 in the men’s final of the 23rd Asian Team Squash Championship at the Mushaf Squash Complex on Saturday.

In the men’s final, Pakistan’s Noor Zaman and Asim Khan outclassed their respective opponents. Noor beat Jeongmin Ryu 11-5, 11-7, 13-11 while Asim outplayed Seojin Oh 11-6, 11-5, 11-4 to give Pakistan the title.

In the women’s final, Hong Kong China downed Malaysia 2-1 to become Asian champions.

Hong Kong China and Malaysia men’s teams won bronze medal while Iran and Korea claimed bronze in the women’s section.

Pakistan’s Noor Zaman plays a shot during the final of the 23rd Asian Team Squash Championship in Islamabad on November 7, 2026. — Photo courtesy Pakistan Squash Federation

Squash legends Gogi Alauddin, Qamar Zaman and Jansher Khan, along with chief guest Asian Squash Federation Vice-President Adil Jassim Al-Ghareeb, Pakistan Squash Federation President Air Marshal Kazim Hammad and AVM Sohail Akbar, the PSF Senior Vice-President, graced the closing ceremony.

Women’s:

Korea bt Pakistan 3-0: Dami Kim (Korea) bt Sehrish Ali (Pakistan) 11-9, 11-3, 11-4; Mingyeong Heo (Korea) bt Sana Bahadar (Pakistan) 11-6, 3-11, 11-5, 11-5; Hwayeong Eum (Korea) bt Mahnoor Ali (Pakistan) 11-5, 11-3, 11-9

Hong Kong China bt Malaysia 2-1: Tse Yee Lam Toby (Hong Kong China) bt Yee Xin Ying (Malaysia) 5-11, 11-6, 11-5, 11-6; Chan Sin Yuk (Hong Kong China) bt Ainaa Amani (Malaysia) 11-7, 11-7, 9-11, 11-7; Yasshmita Jadishkumar (Malaysia) bt Lee Ka Yi (Hong Kong China) 11-8, 11-9, 7-11, 11-4

Men’s (final): Pakistan bt Korea 2-0: Noor Zaman (Pakistan) bt Jeongmin Ryu (Korea) 11-5, 11-7, 13-11; Mohammad Asim Khan (Pakistan) bt Seojin Oh (Korea) 11-6, 11-5, 11-4.

World.title: Pakistani startup led by Nust graduate wins award at Silicon Valley summit
World.content:
Pakistani startup RLabs has won the best startup award at the Silicon Valley November Summit in California, with the government on Saturday hailing the achievement as showcasing the “growing strength of our startup ecosystem”.

RLabs, a Pakistani startup incubated at the National Incubation Centre for Aerospace Technologies (Nicat) and led by Harris Ahmed, won the ‘GOAL Startup Award’ at the summit. The event, held from Nov 2 to Nov 5, was organised by Plug and Play, an innovation platform and a venture capital firm.

RLabs was among 18 startups from around the world that “earned the incredible opportunity to pitch their idea” at the summit under Plug and Play’s Global Overseas Acceleration & Learning (GOAL) programme.

“Had the opportunity to present our work on XR (extended reality) simulators, synthetic data and machine training on a platform that brought together more than 3,000 attendees, including founders, venture capitalists, corporate executives, innovation leaders, and government partners,” Ahmed wrote on his LinkedIn account, sharing a photo of him posing with the award.

Ahmed, a 2018 graduate of the National University of Sciences and Technology (Nust) as per his profile, said he “spent the last decade teaching humans how to operate complex machines in XR”.

“Now we use the same human experience to train machine instincts. (Launching in the US soon),” he added.

Ahmed noted that the summit centred on artificial intelligence (AI) and deep tech, featuring live demonstrations and pitches from over 300 startups across more than 20 industry programmes.

According to Nicat, RLabs had been training a proprietary Large Language Model to “power a modular, cross-platform simulation engine that cuts development time by 75 per cent”.

In a statement, also posted by the government’s official X account, IT Minister Shaza Fatima Khawaja wrote: “From Pakistan to Silicon Valley — a proud moment for our nation!”
